| | | How do we know non-citizen voting is a made up problem? Because **red states and conservative-leaning institutions have spent millions in taxpayer money** and donor dollars searching for it and finding minimal results. For example: The pro-Trump Heritage Foundation -- _an organization that has funded anti-voting initiatives for decades_ \-- maintains a database of "election crimes." **Their own records only list 24 instances of non-citizens voting in U.S. elections from 2003 to 2023**. In other words -- 20 years of elections, millions of votes, and only 24 alleged non-citizen voters. **Reuters has a fuller accounting in recent reporting.** Florida, for example, spent millions investigating voter fraud and creating a new state department to oversee election security. They've only prosecuted two non-citizens for voting since 2022. North Carolina said they found nine non-citizens registered to vote out of 7.7 million voters. Happy Hispanic Heritage Month

body:
Here's the part nobody in Washington is talking about. |
---
Patriot, For months, Senate leadership stalled, slow-walked, and shut doors in our faces on the **SAVE America Act**. We didn't stop. We flooded them with calls, emails, and activists. And now? **President Trump just made the SAVE America Act his number one priority** — calling for it to be attached to the one bill Congress absolutely must pass. Voter ID. Proof of citizenship to register. On the verge of becoming the law of the land. Even Elon weighed in after what we all watched happen in California: _"This is the only way to save democracy in America."_ But here's the part nobody in Washington is talking about — and the reason I'm not celebrating. Whether the SAVE America Act becomes law or not, the midterms are going to be a pure turnout war. So I'm not throwing a party. **I'm hiring.** My team at Early Vote Action is on the ground right now registering new Republican voters and building the most aggressive ballot-chasing and get-out-the-vote operation in our history. It's the exact playbook that flipped Pennsylvania for President Trump in 2024 — one voter at a time, at gun shows, truck stops, farmers markets, and front doors. President Trump did his part. The grassroots pressure is working. Now the midterms are on us. If we pair the SAVE America Act with a midterm landslide, we don't just win an election — we lock in a generation of victories.

# THIS PAST MONDAY...
**9/7 - I MARCHED WITH AN ARMY OF SUPPORTERS & VOLUNTEERS & THE MILFORD LABOR DAY PARADE**
Here are some [photos ](https://us.list-manage.com/eGni9mT_cBr?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)and [videos ](https://us.list-manage.com/17QwnJsjygY?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)we took!
#
ON TUESDAY...
**9/8 - I BECAME THE OFFICIAL REPUBLICAN NOMINEE FOR CONGRESS IN NH02**
To celebrate, I invited my supporters and volunteers to my home for home cooked Chinese food and BBQ. We took a [group photo](https://us.list-manage.com/ink3zB9Ke2l?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c).

Check out Concord Monitor's [article ](https://us.list-manage.com/Q9hWZEgbBcn?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)and [video](https://us.list-manage.com/6wrFPHPWFTr?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c).

I am looking forward to taking on Rep. Maggie Goodlander in debate, on the campaign trail, and the 11/3 General Election. Watch my WMUR Primary debate [here](https://us.list-manage.com/BkmxM0u8zNZ?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c).

**UPCOMING EVENTS**
# ** THURSDAY 9/17, 9AM - CONSTITUTION DAY @ FRANKLIN PIERCE UNIVERSITY - **
Calling for my supporters to represent me at the DiPietro Library Courtyard, Franklin Pierce University, 40 University Drive, Rindge, NH 03461 This is a great opportunity to engage and make supporters out of students.
Schedule: – Arrive after 9:00 AM to set up table – Readings in Democracy: 10:00 AM, DiPietro Library Courtyard – Civic Engagement Fair: 10:30 AM–1:00 PM, same location Campus full of first-time voters.

No RSVP needed, but please email cm@lily4congress.com if you are interested to coordinate further.
# **FRIDAY, 9/18 - HIGHLAND GAMES & FESTIVAL - **
Calling for supporters to represent me at the Loon Mountain Resort, 60 Loon Mountain Road, Lincoln, NH 03251 Tickets required, and my campaign will purchase your ticket if you attend with a Team Lily Gold shirt. Please email tfinney1@comcast.net if you are interested to coordinate further.
# **SATURDAY, 9/19 - HOLLIS OLD HOME DAYS -**
Lawrence Barn and Fields, 28 Depot Road, Hollis, NH 30th anniversary community celebration with parade, exhibitors, food, entertainment, fireworks. Fri 5-9pm block party, Sat 10am-9pm. Free. Source: [hollisoldhomedays.org](https://us.list-manage.com/jVbYzGfqwvU?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)

Iron Beam high energy laser weapon systems are displayed during the Security Equipment International at London Excel on September 10, 2025 in London, England. Photo by John Keeble/Getty Images.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.6SSSRc16HFhHsA5Xm7WRIIHjwyUqPO-wzA5Zqt8_P7U?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=215909803)
When Israel [deployed](https://substack.com/redirect/fefb1183-54f9-4c4f-b34a-cc7791ef7ad9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its Iron Beam laser weapon for the first time last December, the announcement by leading Israeli defense firms Rafael and Elbit Systems was met with fawning coverage worldwide. The futuristic laser system, designed to shoot drones and rockets out of the sky, was celebrated as a demonstration of the Israeli weapons industry's technological sophistication.
The Israeli Ministry of Defense described Iron Beam as "Israel's first domestically developed laser interception system," while touting the country as a pioneer in missile defense. The Arrow anti-ballistic missile system, another key example of Israel's purportedly homegrown ingenuity, was heavily employed to defend from Iranian missile attacks during two recent wars.
That alleged ingenuity is at the center of a debate roiling Washington this month as Congress returns to debates about whether to create a new office in the Pentagon to coordinate U.S. and Israeli military research, testing, and industrial production, giving institutional architecture to a relationship that is already deeply intertwined on a de facto basis. The legislation, known as Section 219, was included in the House-passed National Defense Authorization Act, but remains contested in the Senate. Backers of the bill argue that tighter coordination with Israel should not be seen as a giveaway or cost to the United States, but rather is a boon to U.S. military capacity because the U.S. benefits more from the partnership than Israel. Arrow and Iron Beam are routinely held up as case studies of such innovation.
But the real story of how these weapons were developed is quite different. In fact, both weapons systems were developed and financed by the United States before being handed off to Israel by acts of Congress, according to government documents and interviews with key personnel involved in their development--despite warnings from U.S. intelligence agencies that transferring the tech to Israel effectively hands it over to U.S. adversaries such as China and Russia.
The pattern has long been cause for concern inside the intelligence community and among some in the Pentagon, but the mandates have come directly from Congress.
David Pyne, who worked as a civilian in the Pentagon office that oversaw development of the Arrow 2 program in the early 2000s, said it still bothered him that the American military put in so much work, and American taxpayers footed the bill, yet the U.S. couldn't even fully benefit from the system. "They didn't contribute a dime into the program, but the thing that pissed me off at the time, and obviously since, is that they would not share the final product," said Pyne in relation to Israeli participation in the program.
Israel did spend money on the program, which is typically described as being split roughly down the middle by the U.S. and Israel. The U.S. directly contributed [more than $4 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/0f94e520-4cba-40a2-838d-d4ac507cceb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), while Israel's portion was paid for largely with U.S.-supplied [foreign military financing](https://substack.com/redirect/6bac9084-d733-4972-adef-32c9c6f1ed56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
That left Pyne frustrated at the amount of control Israel retained over the technology. "They wouldn't allow us to use the technology we co-developed with them at 100% U.S. taxpayer expense," Pyne said.
Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) became the primary contractor producing Arrow 2, though the U.S. maintained a veto over who it could be sold to, [which it exercised at one point in the case of India](https://substack.com/redirect/099c934e-8dbf-4f8f-a47c-7a01b43be4d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In 2002, Boeing cut a deal with IAI to make component parts for it, and the U.S. has ultimately been able to exploit some of the technology.
A veteran and former top national security aide to Sen. Mike Lee of Utah, Pyne currently serves as deputy executive director of the U.S. Task Force on National and Homeland Security. While working as a civilian for the Defense Department, Pyne traveled to Tel Aviv to try to work out an agreement in which the U.S. could benefit from the research it was carrying out and financing, but was repeatedly rebuffed, he said, eventually signing a lopsided agreement in June 2001. "I'd love to say that this was unusual, but I believe that was standard operating procedure for all missile defense systems we co-developed with Israel," he said. "That was just what we were willing to agree to." While public statements from the U.S. and Israel emphasized the joint nature of the program, he said, in reality the U.S. put in the work and the money, while Israel and Israeli companies got the benefit.
A former Pentagon contractor who worked on the Iron Beam project--speaking on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the program--told Drop Site that even in the early 2000s, the program was controversial inside the Joint Technology Office. Congress had mandated the program's details be shared with the Israelis, but the intelligence community refused to sign off on such knowledge transfers, they said, warning that Israel would immediately resell the technology to the Chinese.
A Defense Intelligence Agency report from 1999 backs up the contractor's claim. [The report was covered](https://substack.com/redirect/d5277918-0583-4cac-88ef-25201b64edcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Washington Times in an article headlined "Israel Suspected of Transferring U.S. Laser Weapon Data to China." The DIA found that Rafael had obtained restricted American technology from TRW Inc., the U.S. defense contractor running the THEL project, in 1996, which led TRW to halt further transfers. Israel responded with a tenacious pressure campaign on the State Department and the company's subcontractors, trying to restart the technology transfers. The DIA also found evidence that Israel was routinely transferring the technology to China and covering up the arrangement from the U.S. TRW was bought by Northurp Grumman in 2002.
Intelligence analysts would even bring Israeli defense industry marketing brochures to meetings, the contractor said, to demonstrate how flagrantly Israel was advertising its willingness to sell secret American technology to China. "We had tons of intelligence to justify not sharing the information with Israel but we were under pressure from Congress to figure it out and transfer the IP to Israel," said the contractor. "No matter how much evidence the intelligence community produced, the response we received from DOD leadership was that it's congressionally mandated, therefore we have to execute on the program."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5df5b87d-6c61-4a98-ac62-add2cd895534?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Iron Beam laser weapon. Photo: Israeli Ministry of Defense/[Wikimedia Commons](https://substack.com/redirect/2eabe476-bb43-431b-b6d1-6cd6e8c683b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
## To THEL and Back
In February 1996, at the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico, the U.S. military for the first time successfully destroyed a mid-flight warhead with a laser. The program, called Nautilus, was officially a joint U.S.-Israeli collaboration, but as a later Government Accountability Office report confirmed, the U.S. military "provided primary management functions for the program" while the "Israel Ministry of Defense provided support."
Two months later, President Bill Clinton met with Prime Minister Shimon Peres and agreed to enter into a deeper collaboration to produce a Tactical High-Energy Laser (THEL), backed by U.S. money and research, with the aim of producing a defensive weapon that could shoot down Hezbollah rockets at the Lebanese border.
At that point the program was operating under a memorandum of agreement, signed in 1996, that set out the terms of the deal. Lobbyists working on behalf of Israel kicked into gear. Between 1997 and 2001, the Israeli weapons maker Rafael and the Israeli Ministry of Defense spent more than $4.4 million lobbying Congress and the White House on weapons programs, according to foreign agent registration disclosures.
In 1999, using the NDAA--the same must-pass legislation lawmakers are currently using to further fuse the two militaries--Congress mandated the Secretary of Defense to develop a high-energy laser master plan and lay out funding needs. The next year's NDAA ordered the implementation of that program--aligning it with the agreement tying the program to Israel--and designated a senior civilian official to oversee it. By the late 1990s, the U.S. had spent[ more than $100 million on the program.](https://substack.com/redirect/d5277918-0583-4cac-88ef-25201b64edcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) In 2004 and 2005, Congress set aside $17 million and then $8 million for the program.
A [2024 bill](https://substack.com/redirect/b6d38289-89f7-4a18-b495-ea866c07356b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) provided $1.2 billion to Israel to boost its laser program, with President Joe Biden visiting to celebrate the partnership. "We have reaffirmed the unshakeable commitment to the United States to Israel's security, including partnering with Israel on the most cutting edge defense systems in the world, including the U.S. support for the Iron Dome and Israel's new laser-enabled system called the Iron Beam," [he said](https://substack.com/redirect/a0928c1d-3c5d-424c-989d-1bcbc0056881?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Under President Obama, the U.S. signed a memorandum of understanding that pledged $38 billion over ten years to support Israel's military.
The laser eventually shot down more than two dozen Katyusha rockets in tests, but the cost was soaring--more than $300 million at the time--and the chemicals used to produce the laser were deeply toxic and corrosive. The Joint Technology Office had also been researching steady-state lasers, less toxic and less corrosive to the equipment, but not enough advances had come along. So in 2005, THEL was canceled.
In 2007, Ehud Barak, who had returned to office as Israeli minister of defense, pushed to bring back the laser program, which Northrop Grumman was pursuing as "Skyguard," but most of the investment and resources on missile defense were still directed to kinetic interceptors like the Iron Dome.
In the meantime, research continued on the solid-state laser program that would become Iron Beam, almost exclusively funded by the U.S. In 2019, Democratic Rep. Ted Lieu introduced H.R. 1795, the United States-Israel Directed Energy Cooperation Act. It was enacted the next year as part of the NDAA, instructing the Department of Defense to conduct laser research with Israel, citing THEL as the historical precedent. "THEL became Iron Beam," the contractor said.
In a November 2023 Senate floor speech following the October 7 attacks, Sen. Deb Fischer (R-Neb.) urged her colleagues on the Senate Appropriations Committee to fund Israel's missile defenses, calling for replenishing Iron Dome and David's Sling and "investing in the development of the Iron Beam system," as part of a push to win $1.2 billion in funding for the system. Congress ultimately approved the funding as part of an April 2024 national security supplemental, which appropriated $5.2 billion in total for Israeli missile defense, including the $1.2 billion requested specifically for Iron Beam.
What kind of lobbying effort was underway is less clear from federal records than it should be. After 2001, Rafael stopped filing as a foreign agent, and began filing under the Lobbying Disclosure Database, which is created for American companies or foreign companies acting independently of a foreign government, like British Petroleum. But Rafael is a 100% Israeli-state-owned company. By not filing as a foreign agent, the bulk of the company's work remains obscured.
Rafael has received most of the public credit for the laser innovation, and controls the intellectual property, even as much of it was developed and funded by American taxpayers. Rafael did not respond to requests for comment for this story.
A review of public records also points to possible support from researchers at a variety of American universities, including Cornell University, for the project. Cornell, for instance, received a $100,000 grant from the Israeli Ministry of Defense (MOD)--money that likely originated with the U.S. Department of Defense--at the same time to provide research support to help improve fiber laser technology. This was one of several major financial contributions that the MOD made to Cornell researchers. The grants were noted in a 2020 announcement by the ministry's research arm, the Directorate of Defense Research and Development (DDRD), which credited a decade of work by DDRD, Rafael, Elbit Systems, and unnamed academic institutions who contributed to the project.
By following a series of papers published by researchers at American universities, it's possible to trace the incremental breakthroughs that culminated with Iron Beam.
Take Rafael Systems researcher Anatoly Parahovnik. Parahovnik became a research assistant at the University of Central Florida in the fall of 2017 specifically to help Rafael overcome engineering gaps, according to his LinkedIn and academic citations. Parahovnik was working on a central problem related to the laser technology: how to handle the extreme heat it created. According to his LinkedIn resume, "After successfully introducing new technologies from academia at Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, [Parahovnik was] selected to pursue Ph.D. as means to close a gap the firm was experiencing in liquid cooling methods for cooling electronics."
The position at the university was paid for by the MOD, according to an email provided to Drop Site from summer 2017. "I'm hiring a guy from RAFAEL and I want to make sure he will be supported for at least several semesters," wrote his mentor Yoav Peles to the MOD, a request that was quickly approved. The email was obtained as part of an investigation by anti-war researcher Mila Halgren for [Responsible Statecraft](https://substack.com/redirect/fd99bb05-eddc-458c-8ea8-b8cb196f5563?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

> The adiabatic thermalization mode at the micro scale under terrestrial conditions can be used to manage high frequency thermal loads, like radar, laser systems and a range of high-frequency applications. The nature of heat transfer pertinent to the piston effect in forced convection flows is poorly understood, but if properly revealed, it holds great potential to revolutionize copious critical technologies that depend on effective thermal transport.
A key 2020 research paper, co-authored by Parahovnik and his UCF mentor Peles, notes that the work was "funded mainly by the Office of Naval Research" as well as the Israel Ministry of Defense. "The authors would like to acknowledge the Cornell NanoScale Science & Technology Facility (CNF) for staff support, help, and use of facilities in the fabrication of the microdevices," it goes on. The paper was published in Physical Review Applied and titled, "Subcooled Flow Boiling of Carbon Dioxide Near the Critical Point Inside a Microchannel." Another paper, presented that year at the 2020 Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems, includes a similar acknowledgment. A 2021 paper in the International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer included the same funding disclosure.
Another Rafael researcher, Tomer Rokita, [came to the University of Michigan](https://substack.com/redirect/53c2521d-1737-4fce-af0f-fd0a7bf27df6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a year of research on hypersonics. The involvement of U.S. universities in the program [reflects](https://substack.com/redirect/347f03e5-0d2d-49a4-a7af-bbf1dae648e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a broader phenomenon of Israel drawing on the support of elite U.S. researchers to help advance its defense programs. American institutions and companies are producing the breakthroughs, paid for by U.S. taxpayers--sometimes routed through the Israeli MOD--yet it is Israeli companies who claim the IP and profit from sales of the new technology.

## Broken Arrows
The Arrow program began in the late 1980s under the Reagan administration's Strategic Defense Initiative, with the United States committing to fund the development of an Israeli interceptor capable of destroying ballistic missiles. By 1993, the U.S. government had already committed roughly $390 million to Arrow and its follow-on experiments, according to the Government Accountability Office, which warned at the time that Washington risked being drawn into financing much of the complete system--including its missiles, launchers and radar--without independently assessing its overall costs or alternatives.
That support continued as Arrow evolved from an experimental interceptor into a multilayered operational system that boasted new and more advanced capabilities. The Arrow 2 is designed to intercept ballistic missiles in or near the atmosphere, while Arrow 3 targets them at greater ranges and altitudes, outside the atmosphere.
Congressional appropriations records indicate that the United States had [provided](https://substack.com/redirect/d9360aef-7d37-48b1-ab90-1b7472e15f5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) just over $4 billion for the Arrow program by fiscal year 2021. Subsequent appropriations for Arrow 2 and Arrow 3 bring the cumulative public total to approximately $5 billion.
U.S. financing remains embedded in Arrow's current procurement. The Missile Defense Agency's[ fiscal year 2026 procurement justification](https://substack.com/redirect/6c0dd3ec-f843-480f-acd2-520ca8dfd05d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) records $609 million in prior-year procurement funding for Arrow 3 components, followed by $80 million in fiscal year 2024, $50 million in 2025 and a requested $100 million in 2026.
The Iron Beam technology meanwhile has been hailed as a solution to the problems created by modern missile defense systems, where expensive and slow-to-manufacture interceptor munitions are required to shoot down cheaper missiles and drones that can be fired in abundance. Israel has touted its deployment of Iron Beam during the recent war in Lebanon, portraying it as an example of the country's military ingenuity despite its origins in decades of U.S. military assistance.
But even then this system, created with tremendous U.S. financial assistance and other forms of handholding, is not a panacea to the problems faced by Israel in its wars.
The directed laser does not work effectively in all weather conditions and requires the operator to maintain a consistent lock on a moving target for an extended period of time. Consequently, the system is less likely to solve the challenging mathematics of missile interception than to place an additional band-aid on diminishing U.S. and Israeli interceptor stockpiles.
Regardless of the shortcomings of the system, more such joint projects are likely to be developed with the support of U.S. taxpayers as Congress searches for ways to defend against ever-cheaper drones and missiles, while also responding to a push from Israel lobby organizations in Washington to merge the country's defense sectors in a way that future administrations will find difficult to unwind--whether the American public likes it or not.

When Israel its Iron Beam laser weapon for the first time last December, the announcement by leading Israeli defense firms Rafael and Elbit Systems was met with fawning coverage worldwide. The futuristic laser system, designed to shoot drones and rockets out of the sky, was celebrated as a demonstration of the Israeli weapons industry's technological sophistication. The Israeli Ministry of Defense described Iron Beam as "Israel's first domestically developed laser interception system," while touting the country as a pioneer in missile defense. The Arrow anti-ballistic missile system, another key example of Israel's purportedly homegrown ingenuity, was heavily employed to defend from Iranian missile attacks during two recent wars. That alleged ingenuity is at the center of a debate roiling Washington this month as Congress returns to debates about whether to create a new office in the Pentagon to coordinate U.S. and Israeli military research, testing, and industrial production, giving institutional architecture to a relationship that is already deeply intertwined on a de facto basis. The legislation, known as Section 219, was included in the House-passed National Defense Authorization Act, but remains contested in the Senate. Backers of the bill argue that tighter coordination with Israel should not be seen as a giveaway or cost to the United States, but rather is a boon to U.S. military capacity because the U.S. benefits more from the partnership than Israel. Arrow and Iron Beam are routinely held up as case studies of such innovation. But the real story of how these weapons were developed is quite different. In fact, both weapons systems were developed and financed by the United States before being handed off to Israel by acts of Congress, according to government documents and interviews with key personnel involved in their development--despite warnings from U.S. intelligence agencies that transferring the tech to Israel effectively hands it over to U.S. adversaries such as China and Russia. The pattern has long been cause for concern inside the intelligence community and among some in the Pentagon, but the mandates have come directly from Congress. David Pyne, who worked as a civilian in the Pentagon office that oversaw development of the Arrow 2 program in the early 2000s, said it still bothered him that the American military put in so much work, and American taxpayers footed the bill, yet the U.S. couldn't even fully benefit from the system. "They didn't contribute a dime into the program, but the thing that pissed me off at the time, and obviously since, is that they would not share the final product," said Pyne in relation to Israeli participation in the program. Israel did spend money on the program, which is typically described as being split roughly down the middle by the U.S. and Israel. The U.S. directly contributed , while Israel's portion was paid for largely with U.S.-supplied . That left Pyne frustrated at the amount of control Israel retained over the technology. "They wouldn't allow us to use the technology we co-developed with them at 100% U.S. taxpayer expense," Pyne said. Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) became the primary contractor producing Arrow 2, though the U.S. maintained a veto over who it could be sold to, . In 2002, Boeing cut a deal with IAI to make component parts for it, and the U.S. has ultimately been able to exploit some of the technology. A veteran and former top national security aide to Sen. Mike Lee of Utah, Pyne currently serves as deputy executive director of the U.S. Task Force on National and Homeland Security. While working as a civilian for the Defense Department, Pyne traveled to Tel Aviv to try to work out an agreement in which the U.S. could benefit from the research it was carrying out and financing, but was repeatedly rebuffed, he said, eventually signing a lopsided agreement in June 2001. "I'd love to say that this was unusual, but I believe that was standard operating procedure for all missile defense systems we co-developed with Israel," he said. "That was just what we were willing to agree to." While public statements from the U.S. and Israel emphasized the joint nature of the program, he said, in reality the U.S. put in the work and the money, while Israel and Israeli companies got the benefit. A former Pentagon contractor who worked on the Iron Beam project--speaking on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the program--told Drop Site that even in the early 2000s, the program was controversial inside the Joint Technology Office. Congress had mandated the program's details be shared with the Israelis, but the intelligence community refused to sign off on such knowledge transfers, they said, warning that Israel would immediately resell the technology to the Chinese. A Defense Intelligence Agency report from 1999 backs up the contractor's claim. by the Washington Times in an article headlined "Israel Suspected of Transferring U.S. Laser Weapon Data to China." The DIA found that Rafael had obtained restricted American technology from TRW Inc., the U.S. defense contractor running the THEL project, in 1996, which led TRW to halt further transfers. Israel responded with a tenacious pressure campaign on the State Department and the company's subcontractors, trying to restart the technology transfers. The DIA also found evidence that Israel was routinely transferring the technology to China and covering up the arrangement from the U.S. TRW was bought by Northurp Grumman in 2002. Intelligence analysts would even bring Israeli defense industry marketing brochures to meetings, the contractor said, to demonstrate how flagrantly Israel was advertising its willingness to sell secret American technology to China. "We had tons of intelligence to justify not sharing the information with Israel but we were under pressure from Congress to figure it out and transfer the IP to Israel," said the contractor. "No matter how much evidence the intelligence community produced, the response we received from DOD leadership was that it's congressionally mandated, therefore we have to execute on the program." | | ---|---|--- Iron Beam laser weapon. To THEL and Back In February 1996, at the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico, the U.S. military for the first time successfully destroyed a mid-flight warhead with a laser. The program, called Nautilus, was officially a joint U.S.-Israeli collaboration, but as a later Government Accountability Office report confirmed, the U.S. military "provided primary management functions for the program" while the "Israel Ministry of Defense provided support." Two months later, President Bill Clinton met with Prime Minister Shimon Peres and agreed to enter into a deeper collaboration to produce a Tactical High-Energy Laser (THEL), backed by U.S. money and research, with the aim of producing a defensive weapon that could shoot down Hezbollah rockets at the Lebanese border. At that point the program was operating under a memorandum of agreement, signed in 1996, that set out the terms of the deal. Lobbyists working on behalf of Israel kicked into gear. Between 1997 and 2001, the Israeli weapons maker Rafael and the Israeli Ministry of Defense spent more than $4.4 million lobbying Congress and the White House on weapons programs, according to foreign agent registration disclosures. In 1999, using the NDAA--the same must-pass legislation lawmakers are currently using to further fuse the two militaries--Congress mandated the Secretary of Defense to develop a high-energy laser master plan and lay out funding needs. The next year's NDAA ordered the implementation of that program--aligning it with the agreement tying the program to Israel--and designated a senior civilian official to oversee it. By the late 1990s, the U.S. had spent In 2004 and 2005, Congress set aside $17 million and then $8 million for the program. Under President Obama, the U.S. signed a memorandum of understanding that pledged $38 billion over ten years to support Israel's military. The laser eventually shot down more than two dozen Katyusha rockets in tests, but the cost was soaring--more than $300 million at the time--and the chemicals used to produce the laser were deeply toxic and corrosive. The Joint Technology Office had also been researching steady-state lasers, less toxic and less corrosive to the equipment, but not enough advances had come along. So in 2005, THEL was canceled. In the meantime, research continued on the solid-state laser program that would become Iron Beam, almost exclusively funded by the U.S. In 2019, Democratic Rep. Ted Lieu introduced H.R. 1795, the United States-Israel Directed Energy Cooperation Act. It was enacted the next year as part of the NDAA, instructing the Department of Defense to conduct laser research with Israel, citing THEL as the historical precedent. "THEL became Iron Beam," the contractor said. In a November 2023 Senate floor speech following the October 7 attacks, Sen. Deb Fischer (R-Neb.) urged her colleagues on the Senate Appropriations Committee to fund Israel's missile defenses, calling for replenishing Iron Dome and David's Sling and "investing in the development of the Iron Beam system," as part of a push to win $1.2 billion in funding for the system. Congress ultimately approved the funding as part of an April 2024 national security supplemental, which appropriated $5.2 billion in total for Israeli missile defense, including the $1.2 billion requested specifically for Iron Beam. What kind of lobbying effort was underway is less clear from federal records than it should be. After 2001, Rafael stopped filing as a foreign agent, and began filing under the Lobbying Disclosure Database, which is created for American companies or foreign companies acting independently of a foreign government, like British Petroleum. But Rafael is a 100% Israeli-state-owned company. By not filing as a foreign agent, the bulk of the company's work remains obscured. Rafael has received most of the public credit for the laser innovation, and controls the intellectual property, even as much of it was developed and funded by American taxpayers. Rafael did not respond to requests for comment for this story. Cornell, for instance, received a $100,000 grant from the Israeli Ministry of Defense (MOD)--money that likely originated with the U.S. Department of Defense--at the same time to provide research support to help improve fiber laser technology. This was one of several major financial contributions that the MOD made to Cornell researchers. The grants were noted in a 2020 announcement by the ministry's research arm, the Directorate of Defense Research and Development (DDRD), which credited a decade of work by DDRD, Rafael, Elbit Systems, and unnamed academic institutions who contributed to the project. The Jewish calendar is built around the Torah. Each Shabbat, a different Torah portion is read, corresponding to a specific calendar week. On Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish new year, we read the [Akedah](https://substack.com/redirect/3d91e81a-b9f7-4660-9b33-13e92620dd62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In English, we call it the Binding of Isaac.
You know the story. God tells Abraham, "Take your son, Isaac, whom you love, and offer him as a burnt offering on one of the heights that I will point out to you." So Abraham packs up his son and sets off, along with two servants, whom he leaves at the bottom of the appointed mountain. On the way up, Isaac notices something is off--he asks his father, "Here are the firestone and the wood; but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?" Abraham responds (with, I can only hope, some shame): "It is God who will see to the sheep, my son." Abraham builds an altar, binds Isaac, and picks up a knife to slay his son. But at the last moment, an angel stops him, declaring on behalf of God, "Because you have done this and have not withheld your son, I will bestow my blessing upon you."
I read this story last weekend, sitting at the back of our temple's sanctuary. We'd already brought our kids--one and five years old--to the synagogue's shorter children's service. Afterwards, my wife kindly took the boys to wander through the cemetery across the street, so I could get in a few minutes of reflection as the main Rosh Hashanah services got underway.
I've never been very good at focusing on religious ceremony. That morning, skipping a few pages ahead in my prayerbook to the text of the Akedah, I found my mind pulled to a different text I'd been reading recently. On September 2, the United Nations issued a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/dc4a495f-7f91-4cea-9c87-668ca80b330e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--euphemistically titled "Limiting Overshoot: Navigating exceedance of 1.5°C and pathways towards return"--that confirms our world will breach the Paris treaty's goal of keeping global warming below 1.5°C, or 2.7°F.
To receive new posts, subscribe!
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..pMsw8iTgjhI6CMT2Hmf4qOFMiL585QeQ0LYoH1nDIa4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=215914278)
On the one hand, this pronouncement is not really a surprise to anyone who's been paying attention to the climate science. In 2015, the nations of the world determined that if we didn't limit warming to 2.7°F we'd be condemning our children to a Mad Max: Fury Road future. Then the powers that be went right back to letting Big Oil call the shots, increasing [climate pollution](https://substack.com/redirect/610fdb27-59cd-4b65-96d6-39410e38d0ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) almost every year since the treaty was signed and--in the U.S.--producing about 50% more [oil](https://substack.com/redirect/7b3188fe-9429-4298-8a8a-bab38ee6d0ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [gas](https://substack.com/redirect/181301e0-bbe1-4185-a4f3-32686c64416f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) today than in 2015. So of course we're blowing past our climate target. What else could anyone expect?
At the same time, this is a massive milestone--quite possibly the most important one in the history of our species. The international community agreed to this 2.7°F goal because heating the planet beyond that limit will guarantee deeply terrifying consequences for human civilization--consequences that we no longer have to imagine. We're already seeing these disasters, biblical in proportion--[world-historic cities burning to the ground](https://substack.com/redirect/5f5533bb-edef-42eb-b8cb-4ec53420a55b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [millions choking under hazy orange skies](https://substack.com/redirect/6c4229a8-82e3-4be0-b8b3-27e0169f79b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [once-great rivers turning to dusty streams](https://substack.com/redirect/11cde5eb-c2e6-4c14-aad3-57a29f42f36b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [heat waves with five-figure body counts](https://substack.com/redirect/519d6c39-ed00-4451-8ca2-c5d4795ce100?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [inland tsunamis wiping entire towns off the map](https://substack.com/redirect/539d35c9-34ed-4422-b18e-6c234a214a1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--hitting harder and faster each year. And we are at only the very beginning of an exponential curve of catastrophe, one that will, as this recent U.N. report essentially confirms, drive us towards what could be a genuine civilizational collapse. As the oil giant Shell predicted in a [1989 confidential planning document](https://substack.com/redirect/acdab788-d8e9-4ff0-88b9-f7e54bb86eda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that modeled what would become of the world if fossil fuels were not brought under control: "There would be more violent weather--more storms, more droughts, more deluges. Mean sea level would rise at least 30 cm. Agricultural patterns would be most dramatically changed. ... Boundaries would count for little--overwhelmed by the numbers. Conflicts would abound. Civilization could prove a fragile thing."
So it was not a challenging connection to make, sitting there in the last row of folding chairs that get pulled out every year, in every synagogue, for the High Holidays' expanded attendance, while my sons played outside in the unnaturally warm September air, and I read about Abraham's decision: to saddle his donkey, travel with his son up the mountain, tie Isaac on the altar, and raise up his blade, ready and willing to sacrifice his child.
And for what? Naturally, rabbis and philosophers have had a lot to say on this question over the years. It's a test of Abraham's faith in God. It's a demonstration of Abraham's love for God. Immanuel Kant rejected the whole framework, writing that God could not make such an unethical request, meaning Abraham should have refused "this supposedly divine voice." Søren Kierkegaard, in his classic work _Fear and Trembling_ , took the opposite approach, arguing that the story represents the incomprehensibility of faith, which we must understand as transcending standard ethics.
Beyond its philosophical glosses, this story--Abraham giving up what was most precious to him in obedience of God--has also become a symbol of martyrdom and sacrifice. And this is the interpretation that most sticks in my craw--because, of course, Abraham wasn't just sacrificing himself. If he wanted to be a martyr, that's his business. But Isaac was his own person, with his own consciousness, his own dreams. What right did Abraham have to steal his son's future, all so he could enjoy God's blessing and rewards?
He had no right. No more than the fossil fuel industry executives who predicted civilizational collapse and, rather than warning the public, lied--and continue to lie--in order to stall climate action. No more than the MAGA politicians who insist it's all a hoax, or the corporatist Democrats who acknowledge climate change while taking fossil fuel money and direction. No more than the millionaires and billionaires in their private jets, the advertising and law firm partners raking in cash to defend Big Oil, the corporate-backed think tanks and pundits promoting [climate hushing](https://substack.com/redirect/caf9bd66-3463-4ad6-9ace-9089cfffc420?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and championing increased oil and gas production as a "pragmatic" approach. All of these hedonists are pursuing their own selfish rewards while offering up our children--my sons, outside in the cemetery, and yours, but also, in the case of all but perhaps the wealthiest oligarchs with the most exorbitant bunkers, their own children and grandchildren, too.
What could inspire such short-sighted malevolence? Perhaps it's the too-uncritical internalization of a message threaded through the other Torah portion that's traditionally read on Rosh Hashanah, Genesis 1, where God creates the universe and gives man "dominion" over all the earth. If you think you own this world and its future, what is to stop you from burning it all to the ground?
But we don't own our world. As Pope Francis pointed out in _Laudato si '_, "We are not God. The earth was here before us and it has been given to us." As God admonished in Leviticus, "The land is mine; for you are strangers and sojourners with me."
And what of all of us strangers and sojourners? We did not create this cataclysm--that unforgivable sin lies fully at the feet of the wealthy and powerful, the fossil fuel corporations and oligarchs and their political puppets and lieutenants. But we are fully responsible for our response to the crisis. The window to avert true catastrophe is rapidly closing, and if there's one thing that should be clear by now, it's that there is no divine intervention coming to stay our sacrificer's raised blade. The knife is already plunging down towards Isaac, and we have just the blink of an eye until it connects with his exposed throat, severing all our children from the future they deserve.
What will we do with that time? Will we rush in to grab Abraham's hand, knock the knife away, take to the streets and demand the rapid action necessary to save our children, bound and prostrate on the altar? Or will we remain at the bottom of the mountain, waiting with Abraham's servants for our master to conduct his profane sacrifice and return, alone, from the unhallowed heights.
The beginning of a new year is a perfect time to ponder this question, and make a resolution.

clean_body: A Rosh Hashanah reflection on the Binding of Isaac on a burning planet. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more A Rosh Hashanah reflection on the Binding of Isaac on a burning planet. | | | Sep 15 | | | | | | | | | | | | The Jewish calendar is built around the Torah. Each Shabbat, a different Torah portion is read, corresponding to a specific calendar week. On Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish new year, we read the . In English, we call it the Binding of Isaac. You know the story. God tells Abraham, "Take your son, Isaac, whom you love, and offer him as a burnt offering on one of the heights that I will point out to you." So Abraham packs up his son and sets off, along with two servants, whom he leaves at the bottom of the appointed mountain. On the way up, Isaac notices something is off--he asks his father, "Here are the firestone and the wood; but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?" Abraham responds (with, I can only hope, some shame): "It is God who will see to the sheep, my son." Abraham builds an altar, binds Isaac, and picks up a knife to slay his son. But at the last moment, an angel stops him, declaring on behalf of God, "Because you have done this and have not withheld your son, I will bestow my blessing upon you." I read this story last weekend, sitting at the back of our temple's sanctuary. We'd already brought our kids--one and five years old--to the synagogue's shorter children's service. Afterwards, my wife kindly took the boys to wander through the cemetery across the street, so I could get in a few minutes of reflection as the main Rosh Hashanah services got underway. I've never been very good at focusing on religious ceremony. That morning, skipping a few pages ahead in my prayerbook to the text of the Akedah, I found my mind pulled to a different text I'd been reading recently. On September 2, the United Nations issued a titled "Limiting Overshoot: Navigating exceedance of 1.5°C and pathways towards return"--that confirms our world will breach the Paris treaty's goal of keeping global warming below 1.5°C, or 2.7°F. To receive new posts, subscribe! On the one hand, this pronouncement is not really a surprise to anyone who's been paying attention to the climate science. In 2015, the nations of the world determined that if we didn't limit warming to 2.7°F we'd be condemning our children to a Mad Max: Fury Road future. Then the powers that be went right back to letting Big Oil call the shots, increasing almost every year since the treaty was signed and--in the U.S.--producing about 50% more and today than in 2015. So of course we're blowing past our climate target. What else could anyone expect? At the same time, this is a massive milestone--quite possibly the most important one in the history of our species. The international community agreed to this 2.7°F goal because heating the planet beyond that limit will guarantee deeply terrifying consequences for human civilization--consequences that we no longer have to imagine. We're already seeing these disasters, biblical in proportion--, , , , harder and faster each year. And we are at only the very beginning of an exponential curve of catastrophe, one that will, as this recent U.N. report essentially confirms, drive us towards what could be a genuine civilizational collapse. As the oil giant Shell predicted in a that modeled what would become of the world if fossil fuels were not brought under control: "There would be more violent weather--more storms, more droughts, more deluges. Mean sea level would rise at least 30 cm. Agricultural patterns would be most dramatically changed. ... Boundaries would count for little--overwhelmed by the numbers. Conflicts would abound. Civilization could prove a fragile thing." So it was not a challenging connection to make, sitting there in the last row of folding chairs that get pulled out every year, in every synagogue, for the High Holidays' expanded attendance, while my sons played outside in the unnaturally warm September air, and I read about Abraham's decision: to saddle his donkey, travel with his son up the mountain, tie Isaac on the altar, and raise up his blade, ready and willing to sacrifice his child. And for what? Naturally, rabbis and philosophers have had a lot to say on this question over the years. It's a test of Abraham's faith in God. It's a demonstration of Abraham's love for God. Immanuel Kant rejected the whole framework, writing that God could not make such an unethical request, meaning Abraham should have refused "this supposedly divine voice." Søren Kierkegaard, in his classic work Fear and Trembling , took the opposite approach, arguing that the story represents the incomprehensibility of faith, which we must understand as transcending standard ethics. Beyond its philosophical glosses, this story--Abraham giving up what was most precious to him in obedience of God--has also become a symbol of martyrdom and sacrifice. And this is the interpretation that most sticks in my craw--because, of course, Abraham wasn't just sacrificing himself. If he wanted to be a martyr, that's his business. But Isaac was his own person, with his own consciousness, his own dreams. What right did Abraham have to steal his son's future, all so he could enjoy God's blessing and rewards? He had no right. No more than the fossil fuel industry executives who predicted civilizational collapse and, rather than warning the public, lied--and continue to lie--in order to stall climate action. No more than the MAGA politicians who insist it's all a hoax, or the corporatist Democrats who acknowledge climate change while taking fossil fuel money and direction. No more than the millionaires and billionaires in their private jets, the advertising and law firm partners raking in cash to defend Big Oil, the corporate-backed think tanks and pundits promoting and championing increased oil and gas production as a "pragmatic" approach. All of these hedonists are pursuing their own selfish rewards while offering up our children--my sons, outside in the cemetery, and yours, but also, in the case of all but perhaps the wealthiest oligarchs with the most exorbitant bunkers, their own children and grandchildren, too. What could inspire such short-sighted malevolence? Perhaps it's the too-uncritical internalization of a message threaded through the other Torah portion that's traditionally read on Rosh Hashanah, Genesis 1, where God creates the universe and gives man "dominion" over all the earth. If you think you own this world and its future, what is to stop you from burning it all to the ground? But we don't own our world. As Pope Francis pointed out in Laudato si ', "We are not God. The earth was here before us and it has been given to us." As God admonished in Leviticus, "The land is mine; for you are strangers and sojourners with me." And what of all of us strangers and sojourners? We did not create this cataclysm--that unforgivable sin lies fully at the feet of the wealthy and powerful, the fossil fuel corporations and oligarchs and their political puppets and lieutenants. But we are fully responsible for our response to the crisis. The window to avert true catastrophe is rapidly closing, and if there's one thing that should be clear by now, it's that there is no divine intervention coming to stay our sacrificer's raised blade. The knife is already plunging down towards Isaac, and we have just the blink of an eye until it connects with his exposed throat, severing all our children from the future they deserve. What will we do with that time? Will we rush in to grab Abraham's hand, knock the knife away, take to the streets and demand the rapid action necessary to save our children, bound and prostrate on the altar? Or will we remain at the bottom of the mountain, waiting with Abraham's servants for our master to conduct his profane sacrifice and return, alone, from the unhallowed heights. The beginning of a new year is a perfect time to ponder this question, and make a resolution. | | ---|---|--- P.S. name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: The AI Panic Hits Fever Pitch and Trump Trashes Paxton
body:
Plus, Gregg Hull isn't in his own running mate's ad | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/XwCTnGL2ds1?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
Two things this week we couldn't stop talking about. A researcher quit Anthropic and said the people building AI think it could end all of us inside ten years, and his own boss backed him up on it publicly. [Then closer to home,](https://us.list-manage.com/f1ht18Bb84k?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e) the Republican candidate for lieutenant governor ran an ad that somehow never mentions the guy running for governor.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/pO8gEcBbbvC?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | 🔥 **THE RESEARCHER WHO QUIT ANTHROPIC

** Jacob Coxon walked out two months before his stock vested, which means he left real money on the table to say what he said. And what he said is that the people building this stuff already believe it could end us inside about ten years. They're just a lot more honest about it in private than they are in public.Then his own boss at Anthropic got online, said Coxon's right!

Krysty thinks he's the real thing. He said flat out he'd have stayed if he believed the guardrails were coming, and that landed with her. Mark isn't buying it, because the Wall Street Journal already had the story before Coxon ever hit send.

💵 **MARK THINKS THIS IS ABOUT MONEY**
Anthropic's about to go public at something close to two trillion dollars. Mark’s read is that if Washington ends up blessing a handful of approved AI companies, those companies get legal cover and everybody else gets shoved out of the business. It's a pretty good deal if you're one of the handful.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/wWGZfXYHBvl?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | 🏛️ **THE AD WITH NO GREGG HULL IN IT**
David Gallegos is running for lieutenant governor, and this week he dropped a digital ad going after Deb Haaland on guns. Gregg Hull, the guy actually running for governor, isn't in it. Anywhere.
Here's Mark's problem with it. Most people in this state still couldn't pick Gregg Hull out of a lineup, so every dollar spent making voters familiar with David Gallegos is a dollar that didn't go toward the top of the ticket. He also doesn't think guns are the fight to pick in a New Mexico general election, and he says what he'd be running instead.

💰 **TRUMP PROMISED YOU $5,000. THEN HE WENT AFTER KEN PAXTON.**
From the stage in Dallas, five thousand dollars for every adult in America if Republicans hold the House and Senate. We vote Republican and we still think it's the wrong call, and Mark gets into what he'd rather see done with that kind of money.
Trump was also there to campaign for Ken Paxton. To help him. Which is what makes the thing he said about Paxton from that same stage so hard to believe.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/1CfDK_cunOi?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | PLUS: James Talarico went on Fox News and came out a completely different candidate, our delegation wrote to Apple and Google about keeping New Mexico on the maps, and the Atlantic still hasn't produced a single hurricane this year.

Three books. Three different lenses. One big question: Who gets to decide who has power? That question isn’t just history. It’s happening right now. name: Josh Harder
subject: What’s at stake tonight
body:
Hey Peter,

I’m reaching out with just hours left before our mid-month deadline — if we don’t hit our goal tonight, we’ll be too far behind to catch up. Frankly, that’s a scary place to be.

I just checked ActBlue, and we’re still about $3,200 short.

Falling short means we won’t have the resources to defend this seat while the GOP spends millions against us.

We risk losing the House and giving Trump two more years of unchecked power. I can’t let that happen, but I can’t stop it alone.

There are only a few hours left. Can I count on you to chip in right now? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/JHCA-09-Email-Sept2026-FR-midmonth?&refcode=E31632-20260915-midmonth2-SL-DeadlineOther&amount=25]

GOLDEN, Colo. -- On September 8, 2026, Yvonne "Missy" Woods stood in a Jefferson County courtroom in a blue blazer and wept as videos from her victims played to the court. Judge Andrew Poland sentenced the 66-year-old former Colorado Bureau of Investigation scientist to ten years in prison -- and took her into custody on the spot. For twenty-nine years, Woods was the state's star DNA witness. She worked the Kobe Bryant case. It turns out she was the most dangerous person in the building.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/87b55b3d-31a8-40b0-a990-91ccf99066c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The charges read like sabotage. Between 2008 and 2023, Woods deleted DNA quantification values, re-ran entire testing batches without documenting it, and concealed contamination. And in at least 32 sexual assault cases, she did something almost unspeakable: she deleted the values showing male DNA was present on a rape kit, then wrote the report that closes a case -- "No Male DNA Found."
Understand what those words mean to a survivor. A rape kit is not a form. It is hours of invasive, humiliating evidence collection a woman endures with her body still freshly traumatized, on the promise that science will speak for her when she cannot. When the report comes back "no male DNA found," that is the state telling her there is nothing to pursue -- no profile, no database comparison, no cold hit, no arrest. Woods handed thirty-two women that verdict fraudulently. Their attackers' DNA was there. She erased it and moved on.
The damage cuts both ways. False negatives free the guilty; false confidence imprisons the innocent. KC Harney spent 27 years in prison for a 1995 Lakewood rape he did not commit -- a conviction built partly on Woods' DNA work before retesting cleared him. He sits in that courtroom at every hearing, because the same analyst who stole his decades also handled the 1985 murder of his wife Tamara's father. And every verdict she touched as a "star witness" is now fair game for challenge.
But here is what should make every Coloradan furious: the rot does not stop at one lab bench. Say the DNA comes back positive. Say the perpetrator is caught and convicted of sexually assaulting a child. In Colorado, he can still walk out of the courtroom on probation. As former district attorney George Brauchler has documented, a man who rapes a child is eligible for probation -- and remains eligible even if he goes on to rape other children, one time each, even as their teacher, coach, or clergyman. Critics of the status quo, citing state sentencing outcomes on Attorney General Phil Weiser's watch, put the figure at 73 percent of convicted child rapists getting probation instead of prison. Republican Rep. Brandi Bradley has carried the remedy -- the "Protections Against Child Rape" bill, HB25-1073 in 2025 and SB26-111 in 2026, mandating prison for class 3 and class 4 child sexual assault. Democratic majorities have killed it three years in a row, most recently in Senate Judiciary this spring. Small wonder Colorado ranks fourth in the nation in reported sex offenses per capita -- and that over the past decade, for every ten rape reports, police made a single arrest.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72526ade-1bcc-4f36-8caa-46d5fd8ed1d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Woods scandal shows what happens before conviction; Colorado's sentencing laws show what happens after. Evidence erased, then evidence discounted.
Back to the lab. The bureau knew. A CBI internal affairs report shows a worker questioned Woods' testing all the way back in 2014. In 2018, she was accused of data manipulation and temporarily pulled from DNA casework -- then quietly put back on it. For five more years she kept processing rape kits while colleagues' concerns sat in a drawer. What finally stopped her? Not supervision. Not audit. An intern, in 2023, noticed a pattern of missing data in her work. A student spotted in months what a state agency had missed for a decade. A judge found in August that this oversight failure amounted to "outrageous government conduct."
The ledger so far: CBI opened its investigation in September 2023; Woods retired that November. In January 2025 she was charged with 102 counts -- cybercrime, perjury, attempted influence of a public servant, forgery. In June she pleaded guilty to four felonies; the rest were dropped. She got ten years. At least 1,045 of her cases are tainted, retesting will cost taxpayers over $11 million, and Denver police alone have reopened 13 sexual assault investigations.
Her motive? Prosecutors found no payoff and no framing. Woods said she was buried in work, trying to move cases along -- to "make it go away." That is exactly what she did: to the truth, and to thirty-two women whose cases went cold because a state scientist found them inconvenient. Some survivors waited over a decade past the first red flags for someone to read their results honestly. Some will never get a prosecution, because evidence degrades and statutes expire.
The lesson is bigger than one lab. Jurors treat scientists in white coats as infallible, and bureaucracies defend their stars rather than audit them. The Woods case argues for independent lab oversight, blind re-testing, and consequences for supervisors who paper over red flags. And Bradley's killed bill argues for something simpler: that when a jury does its job and the evidence proves a child was raped, the sentence should mean prison. A state that erases the DNA and then shrugs at what the DNA proves is telling its victims -- women and children alike -- to make it go away themselves.
An intern did the right thing. The adults had a decade and declined. Every woman who ever submitted a rape kit in Colorado deserved better.

This week it got harder. Donald Trump's PAC reserved $1.7 million in ads to defeat me, on top of the nearly $12 million national Republicans had already lined up against us.

body:

Josh Rogers/NHPR

At the GOP debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's running
for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant."

He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants — who
cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the
heart of our state alive — have something to be embarrassed about.

I’m not embarrassed. I’m proud.

My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65-hour
week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up
every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter —
because they do.

John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life. He was born into
the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant
serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China.

That's what John Sununu calls “honest work.”

New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor
actually looks like — who fights for small business owners, for restaurant
workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is
running to protect people like himself. I'm running for everyone else.

He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let’s make sure he
doesn’t represent us.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260915_4.ekEo2y&amount=5&refcode=em20260915-4&t=1022&akid=8938%2E582294%2EF5rYyj ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. He doesn’t get how hard
we work — and he sure as hell doesn’t think our labor is worth respecting.

I do. That’s why I’m running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

body:
Our goals are only getting bigger – especially with our last quarterly FEC deadline coming up in a couple of weeks.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1375&source=&t=1&akid=3532%2E124072%2E7iJfke) | | | |
---
Peter, let me start by saying this: If you chipped in any amount towards my $2.5 million mid-month fundraising goal, **thank you.** I am so grateful for your support.
**That said, unfortunately, we came up short last night.**
Our goals are only getting bigger from here on out – especially with our last quarterly FEC deadline coming up in a couple of weeks – so [**_I’m asking if you can give $5 or even just a few bucks to help me close my budget gap immediately. Can I count on you?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1375&amount=5&t=8&akid=3532%2E124072%2E7iJfke)
As I write this, all eyes are on North Carolina. Democrats simply _must_ win here to have any chance at retaking the Senate majority and stopping the GOP’s extreme agenda, so President Trump and his top allies have been coming after me with baseless lies.
Between the nonstop attacks and outrageous sums of dark money (over $100 million so far), recent polls show that this race is statistically tied.
**The only way we can surge ahead is with your critical grassroots support. Before my team and I meet to finalize the rest of our September budget, I promised I’d reach out to my top supporters – people like you – and see if you’re able to lend a hand.**
[**_This is a race we cannot afford to lose, Peter, and we need to hit every goal between now and Election Day to flip North Carolina and the Senate. Will you chip in $5 so we can enter this final stretch on the strongest possible footing?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1375&amount=5&t=9&akid=3532%2E124072%2E7iJfke)

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

A Special Message from our SponsorPlease note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of Free Speech Daily and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily.
The dubbed “Stop Nick Shirley Act” was made to stop me. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

Patriot,

There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means.

On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO1k2vgF0m2UgZ1A8lUX5iV4365TI6rVGerv3V6CwvFiwQ5eEa3zPOkP9Y69DsihjK2im9fBupIl4lX8kOt8h1L0xGp6vQDYImE

Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Patriot: it makes it harder for anyone — me included — to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent.

I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning.

Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General— the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it.

That's not a coincidence, Patriot. That's the system protecting itself.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO2mtGGsATffZTHA9hNOyAO4CXC1UY266da2rBwE_Afj86mRXs-2MFakdJVg-YSblnGWl4E1aW569opCQuWUvGT5QSy-qHw0Y82
Patriot, will you make a tax-deductible gift of $25, $50, or $100 today to help keep independent journalists like me in the field?

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO3icJsesRgKnH0FopMw-cMVU9WecnFqfQ-UaS8jbZFaDrpHctbcr8eKqn_kUTIN-_hfHPL44ByLKuIcInn-1brIBOGMJABTcdM
Yes — I'll Help Keep Independent Journalists in the Field

I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't — daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding.

A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right — and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions.

Here's something most people don't see, Patriot: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you.

When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did.

That’s why I’m partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place.

I’m grateful for their partnership and commitment, and
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO4oaF6qe7hwzItutaK2EonVFJMlpTinMF906tbyiUiVg-CHd4XQYkJqZTFOgvSaiyQYea48rzzZGaXgHVYpRj1DthCzij_y6Mv
every dollar you give to LMF goes directly toward keeping reporters like me in the field – helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them.

Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible, and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO5f66IDuZ2dDkGvSyvW6qhVlc5QBSuwz0FbS_QU7gVkNqMm7X4a8r1HcpDkUpkdshR90umyqez0htA8HKUqXLsHlkfoOAmQpoJ
Yes — I'll Fund Independent Investigations

Patriot, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that’s why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech — and that’s why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue!

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO6haDjO5QWghwK2toAaliBEyfPx-360GcJMJ0mGWjctdcH29PfiYxaw6Q12TOCCMNrmq_bv4aJlwjgfKlXm0AWXuF-Pa-v-Gf_
Will you help LMF keep me — and journalists like me — in the field with a gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can give today?

For the truth,

Nick Shirley

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO7XbSxFcR8ybFs5FHJZT6I4GEgBUYcEiWVTafE1MeEoSUqkIMH9Xge67R5L0h494CyHA2nBC3GVgkgtaBNCCnwnDbz-NI5Z23C
Help Support Nick’s Work

P.S. — A California assemblyman is already asking the DOJ to intervene against this law. That tells you how serious this is.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO8LdbEjwX3zQ24gAiZa8ym3lEX_XWzGEV3ILPqD9uj2gpqj2VSFFnTlPECjUBc-D9SgRgdnhIGZ7aW9h-h0Zsoi-UxnGuiIMCy
A tax-deductible gift today helps LMF keep me and other independent journalists in the field while this fight plays out.

FOLLOW US ON SOCIAL!

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO9GLB81cOCiq94i1e6Ol2F6IspTiRzop_NjZAvgsw5-5cES-VaMO6t26rTHkKS5vGXcPZdsuPVtsLxjIUWbm7xFixrgZL0BqkQ

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GeO_UvxN6ikD4BMXKOmpM8WK5Cu2EcOKXH9kftMF7ZRZ7mUunmuu5I_C1GN825t_y1M7GsdOfySuNhkGzsK-qJON4iYWWUK9jO0g

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAvq3GePAyA0-Ipd7DXuvIOTsJHyCIvnrg1TiDKI2TeZxfFWYvp0VtIPi0rRv1jqCfad4J2JVSy99vrxtP_IaFMDYd6HUqxa84F6qhcFH

ABOUTUS

Lincoln Media Foundation is a California 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation.

Our Mission is to empower the individual with the truth to hold the powerful accountable. Breaking down the barriers of disinformation and helping to level the field.

ACCESSIBILITY: Bringing content to traditionally underserved communities by making it freely available online.

COMMUNITY FOCUSED: Different communities have different priorities. We focus on the important issues that matter to the communities we reach.

DIGITAL FOOTPRINT: Leveraging digital allows us to reach more people while reducing environmental impact.

body:
No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-e-fttutdy-hhlljjcji-h/) **For Immediate Release:** September 15, 2026**Contact:** Kylie Glatfelter, Communications Director, [kglatfelter@indiana.gop](mailto:kglatfelter@indiana.gop)**If Bayh Hates Insider Dealing, Why Is He Paying For It? ****Indianapolis, Ind. **- Beau Bayh wants Hoosiers to believe he's Indiana's newest anti-corruption crusader. His recent campaign ad features Bayh lifting weights in front of an "END CORRUPTION" sign while promising to take on political insiders. There's just one problem: Bayh's own campaign is relying on the political establishment he claims to be running against. Bayh has made fighting "corruption and insider dealing" a centerpiece of his campaign for secretary of state. But reporting from IndyStar and Mirror Indy found that his campaign paid more than $30,000 to EG Strategies, the fundraising firm run by Emily Gurwitz, a longtime fundraiser and campaign staffer for Indianapolis Mayor Joe Hogsett. Gurwitz was also directly involved in the Hogsett administration's donor "wish list" controversy. According to IndyStar and Mirror Indy, she arranged for lists of campaign donors' preferred city contracts to be delivered to a top city official. So while Bayh films dramatic gym ads promising to clean up Indiana politics, his campaign team has paid tens of thousands of dollars to a longtime political insider connected to one of Indianapolis' most prominent recent ethics controversies. That leaves Bayh with a simple question to answer: How can he claim to be fighting corruption while relying on the same kind of political influence he says he'll take on? "Beau Bayh wants to lecture Hoosiers about corruption while his campaign writes checks to the same political network that has faced serious questions about influence at Indianapolis City Hall," said Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling. "If Bayh expects anyone to take his anti-corruption crusade seriously, he should explain that relationship and cut ties with it." The contradiction fits a pattern. Bayh campaigns as an outsider while carrying one of the most prominent last names in Indiana politics. He talks about ending insider dealing - yet he's paying the same political operatives to run his fundraising operation. Now, he's trying to sell Hoosiers an anti-corruption rebrand with a dramatic campaign commercial. The gym montage might be new. The political insiders aren't. If Beau Bayh wants to make corruption the centerpiece of his campaign, he should start by answering questions about the insiders helping run his own. ### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fttutdy-hhlljjcji-r/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fttutdy-hhlljjcji-y/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fttutdy-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fttutdy-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fttutdy-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fttutdy-hhlljjcji-d/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. body:
Trump hasn’t hidden his desire to have the military get involved in elections, publicly refusing to roll out deploying the National Guard to voting locations ahead of the midterms.
