| Friend,
Donald Trump to Truth Social to push Congress to pass the “Save America” Act—the most heinous voting restrictions in the history of the country.
It has already failed to pass in the Senate, with some vulnerable MAGA Senators worried the bill would be so extreme that the backlash would cause them to lose their seats to Democrats.
But Trump has a new absolutely terrifying sales pitch—it’s actually the military that wants to restrict your right to vote:
---
| [](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001SmyRXVH5dEVqugC3F-py3jDHdp3EilMoQUCNFsmTtxKC4RzWvLhgDJ71ux0IOYmrtC0QTaJNwg8ONwloBZ6A0pyF_KfqWmo0GvS27yN2c4WveMkiUXs-0EJZ8lIoRyu7hbnY-H5g6AO9y-HOKZHHCdiuAbf4IlzrMU4LIBoDcmyctpKO1M2HpOYDtNoYBB1ljAQwM6bebDwGi1J19k0EunfrUs5CPhTBDXtv0KqGedd0_Cg63tiXd0XE1Nxv1mF3EVPy7Glch5gXy-TnU1O-6g==&c=jqpQH9nlmzrjzizMT4WLMsQjkWu9dpVNIZNHOQ7ZSymY3dWEg9o6mQ==&ch=Y6O49cHK_smLCjxrErH2fFZHuIRQS1-4H7EBbzg5Ptz4Jd96UO1z_A==)
---
| Trump hasn’t hidden his desire to have the military get involved in elections. Earlier this year, he refused to rule out deploying the National Guard to voting locations ahead of the midterms.
And how does the Pentagon’s top brass feel about it? This was Pete Hegseth’s response to Trump on social media:
---
| [](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001SmyRXVH5dEVqugC3F-py3jDHdp3EilMoQUCNFsmTtxKC4RzWvLhgDJ71ux0IOYmrtC0QTaJNwg8ONwloBZ6A0pyF_KfqWmo0GvS27yN2c4WveMkiUXs-0EJZ8lIoRyu7hbnY-H5g6AO9y-HOKZHHCdiuAbf4IlzrMU4LIBoDcmyctpKO1M2HpOYDtNoYBB1ljAQwM6bebDwGi1J19k0EunfrUs5CPhTBDXtv0KqGedd0_Cg63tiXd0XE1Nxv1mF3mD-H8kn9IJrfxwuNJ6pEsw==&c=jqpQH9nlmzrjzizMT4WLMsQjkWu9dpVNIZNHOQ7ZSymY3dWEg9o6mQ==&ch=Y6O49cHK_smLCjxrErH2fFZHuIRQS1-4H7EBbzg5Ptz4Jd96UO1z_A==)
---
| These are dark, serious, and unprecedented threats.
Since the founding of this nation, the military has separated itself from partisan politics. It’s a key tenet of the separation of powers and there are multiple laws and military directives preventing personnel from being used for political purposes. But Trump and Hegseth not only seemed prepared but intending to cross that rubicon.
Trump’s assault on free and fair elections escalates every single day. While we don’t know what the full picture of his plans for November look like, the pieces are coming together and it’s not pretty. The gears are motion and he has the sycophants and crooks by his side ready and willing to do anything and everything necessary to make sure MAGA wins.
We have to rapidly build a firewall to protect our democracy from Trump. That’s why Defend Our Courts exists. We successfully defended the pro-democracy majority on the Pennsylvania and Wisconsin Supreme Court over the past year—safeguarding election integrity in critical swing states.
Now we’re expanding the scope of our mission to meet the gravity of the threats our democracy faces at this moment: Building a firewall of state Supreme Courts with the power to protect free and fair elections state by state. And leading the movement to reform the MAGA occupied U.S. Supreme Court that is enabling Trump’s dismantling of our democracy.
[This is too important. ## US Confirms Space Weapons in Orbit
Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said Monday the United States has weapons [stationed in Earth's orbit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O5CAUhE9jZ1iAfwkINnHWm25ogXl0v10MXnjdqG8_8mikOcBkn1RSqb76c9tuBgPG-29zgCaftgi1BCCCvFUwZ4oFY8oW6f8TgQwFE2mTXE6MKyamzeyEL9gG0zrtAST0LWgxL2oceyF5-9AgvPLSi2UYwANXgo9gR7cMdl5c3y8t6quPKzEJzkehOm6tVWLerRznWTrXDBwcUsrd34SRHuDDO70gd3s62qAfRGdp-l-NXBu51lq7aPfL48obuV7YyPVZ2DeZ_V9MNYC7Q2EecyFGeABzcIb0Bse-5BlGVk6zA8t7NKOalZjarN1ZMQQs09wM_H4YDJ9b6IcXvrT8CAAA__8t2ojE), the first time a Pentagon official has publicly confirmed the capability. Speaking at a defense conference in National Harbor, Maryland, Meink described the systems as on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending American forces against hostile action. He declined to say [whether they are kinetic](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFygzAQRU8DnRhJILAKFWnonDYls0iLvYmQiNiYye0zZnyDtG93_p_3P67TFShSur3Dio6XPCU89ojMWKYDYctpp5TLTPz9Q8jAERJPWupeSCtUP4FneuDUQR3cgqixrdGp4WKNaZWW9d1ZaweJXoMxJnQyACqUxlyk9l2LnarJPfOkVb2S0ijbyHmerRr8rM0w6BCqTmIgzqX5zJT4jkv8zQ8sjc9rHd2dedur9q3SY6XH4zgaoAIp7Bt4XHLxuD8_Kz2uSOlLnFycB5GTOO1e0OfEJUfxUq_0WBcXtoNipL0fqk7eVqB4FvM_93o4_RcAAP__O92CYw) and said the wording was chosen deliberately. The disclosure follows years of warnings about Chinese and Russian anti-satellite programs. A Space Force spokesperson said the capabilities can be used for [offensive and defensive purposes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO2zAQRb-G6mjwoWfBIkCgzkG6lMKQHNmT0KJCji347xda7B9sfYCLe86f63IFSrTdfsEDHa952fCoCZmxLAfCnrdKWy6e-P-TkIETbLwYZXqpJqn7BQLTC5cWmuhWRIO2QaeHceo6q41q7m5oV-MVjj4EQPBq7IKGAH6cWkAdbUPu3FOT7rVSnZ4uyns_6SF40w2DiVG0CiNxLpe_mTa-45re-YXlEvKjSe7OvFdhfwgzCzODD6fDyYSZf-dETKGegIpccwkoK4aCDOUtIfzb8pEw3rDKZ5VfyrLuEFCYuXIub2FnisL-1LZv7TAZ2xQX94NSotoPolW3B1D6PMPfbPhy5iMAAP__TRCIzA) at the direction of military commands.

## Atlantic Sets No-Hurricane Record
No hurricane has formed in the Atlantic since the season opened June 1, the [longest such stretch](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAUhJ8Gd1hw_ENcUGzjLttuaYF9HJ8VgVw4CcrbXzn3EW430kgz882_63J1FCje_ro7Wt7TErGWgMyYl4rukWKhmLIn_noSsuPgIi-gYJRqknpc3Mr0wqV3zWZ3RMCuQavNZRqGToNqDmv64eK7UeEwdZ1SvQGza3fZvYbddH5oyJ55atKjVmrQU6u895M2q4fBGNg20SvciFNu_yeKfOAe3umFuV3TvQn2YH4U0f0RMAuYa63t6svJcfoC5lMKmH-20yqPZ860uoiyoCspyg8D8VtmXFPeZEhVYpCRYhIwN9luj0ohUBmN6NXt7ih8qvmXj70sfAcAAP__tACCgg) on record since satellites began tracking storms in 1966. Five tropical storms have developed, including Arthur, Bertha, Cristobal, Dolly, and Edouard, but none reached the 74-mph threshold that defines a hurricane. The first one usually [arrives in August](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykzzFurDAQANDTmG6RPWBYFy5-Q7e_TYkGe1gmMvYGJli5fZRcIRd40nt7zA_kxPn5H3fyspY5Uz0TidAxV8JXySfnciwsH59MgpIwywwahpt2NzPMGIQvmntsol-JgLqGvBnvztrOgG427-7BEXS2v1vXDYDowhqJhrBYQhtDw_7H084MRmtrXKuXZXFmDAvYcYQYVa8pspSjfS-cZaM1fZWLjjaUvUl-E3mdqvunYFIw1VrbvIU2F8T2WS4FU0i8FwVTc_j4qpwSn8Ooev3ckdMvIn-8Xx6-AwAA___isG8l). Forecasters point to an unusually strong El Niño, which [increases wind shear](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGS3CAQRU-DMlTASGgVEDhRtk4dqhporXqNYAw9Q-3tXTs-gvNXv_57v973d6BE-eMnXOj4KHvG3hIyY907wr3kRrlUT_znQcjACTLvRhkr1Sq13SEwPXGfYIjuQDR4G9Dp5W2d55s2ajjd5Gf7NnsN4bDa6nmJJlgfojbqAGXjQO57T63aaqVmvY7Ke7_qJXgzL4uJUUwKI3Gp42ehzCce6as8sY6hXENyJ_O9idsPYTZhtt772AJhZjoowIWVAuRvVJgNKlNIKMzGJ8p_NhTk-agvCmVDaCXLz0dj-TJOX9LX8hslyIxddgQ-scqKodQozDZUF--dUqJmFzGpjwsovY7xf_Z8OvM3AAD__yF1jvk) over the Atlantic and tears apart storms before they can organize. ## **The Good**
President Trump delivered the speech of the convention on opening night, going for more than 90 minutes in front of a roaring crowd. He told Republicans to stop treating the midterms like an off-year. _" Pretend that I'm on the ballot. I'm on the ballot,"_ he said, and he promised to personally campaign in roughly three dozen battleground races before Election Day.
President Trump announced a $5,000 "Trump Dividend" for every adult American citizen if Republicans hold both chambers of Congress, which was met with cheers and sent the media into a meltdown. Trump came back for the closing night as well, alongside Vice President Vance, who delivered a message every Republican needs to hear before the election:
_" Don't give the country over to a bunch of crazy people because you happen to disagree with us on a policy issue here or there."_
That real story of the convention is that the party WAS UNIFIED. After a year that has revolved around a lot of infighting (Thomas Massie, Marjorie Traitor Greene) the entire Republican coalition showed up together.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent got one of the loudest ovations of the night when he warned that Democrats would dismantle everything the Trump administration has built. Democrat Senator John Fetterman appeared in a video endorsing Republican Dave McCormick. If he switches to the Republican Party, he will be welcomed with open arms for standing up against Islamic terrorism and supporting President Trump on key issues.
Several speakers attacked the radicals now in control of the Democrat Party, especially Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and his Hasan Piker fan club. But they didn't go far enough in denouncing or even mentioning Islam or the Islamic-communist ideology that has taken over the left, but more on that later.
The venue was packed. [The RNC put attendance at 20,000](https://substack.com/redirect/d5f578fc-54ac-4f9c-aea5-7bbfed9517b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an arena that holds around 21,000, and by the time President Trump took the stage, the lower bowl where I was standing was full. The energy was amazing. Anyone who was actually in the building could see that the MAGA movement is not going anywhere. It is organized, it is motivated, and it is ready to fight this midterm election.
## **The Bad**
The same media that spent two days pretending nobody showed up to Dallas has been lying about President Trump's crowds for ten years, and they did it again. [The Daily Beast](https://substack.com/redirect/8f36659f-74b7-44cb-b55a-44df3de92773?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [The New Republic](https://substack.com/redirect/03d13368-a5e1-483c-b809-349c9a27226d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [Rachel Maddow's blog at MS NOW](https://substack.com/redirect/36d0a07f-ed84-41b5-bae4-98bc15f80da9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) all ran with the false "half-empty" arena narrative, using photos of the upper deck taken before the keynote while people were still coming through security, and, [as attendees pointed out](https://substack.com/redirect/31809e3d-57ed-4c02-b664-a1094159a476?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with entire sections roped off for the media. Newsweek's own photographer admitted the lower level was packed an hour before the President spoke.
President Trump said in front of the crowd: _" Not only is this packed, but you have an equal number of people standing outside."_ He was right.

One reporter was kicked out of the venue for her "gotcha journalism." [Tara Palmeri](https://substack.com/redirect/14c55a07-d718-472d-9d20-1f189c7090f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the former ABC News and Politico reporter who now runs a podcast, brought three Epstein "survivors" who had been given guest passes, left the designated media area, and started ambushing people on the convention floor with questions about the Epstein files.
She cornered Republican congressional candidate Robert Burke for roughly eight minutes. Security asked whether the group was carrying signs, told her she was not in the media area, and revoked her credential. By 2:40 p.m., about 35 minutes after she walked in, she was out of the building, and according to her own account, she was told she would be arrested for trespassing if she came back. Using three abuse survivors as human props for a gotcha stunt inside the Republican Party's convention is not journalism; it is activism, and everyone in attendance was required to follow rules in exchange for a media badge, myself included.
The other bad was across the street. Democrats set up a counter-convention in Dallas [headlined by Illinois Governor JB Pritzker](https://substack.com/redirect/5729a4aa-859b-4005-912f-685d8ee95659?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who held a press conference at Dallas City Hall to call the GOP gathering "bizarre," while Texas Democrats drove digital billboard trucks in circles around the American Airlines Center.
James Talarico, the Democrat running against Ken Paxton for the U.S. Senate, was also in Dallas, where he admitted that he would vote to support packing the Supreme Court to ensure Democrat control of the judicial system forever.
_" Binding codes of conduct for our justices. It'll include term limits, and I am open to a discussion about expanding the number of justices,"_ Talarico said.

## Trump Taps Hunt for Saudi Post
President Trump [nominated Rep. Wesley Hunt](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAUhJ8GOiPbAYMLF9vQZdst0TE-BGv9g-yTkLz9FVf3DW41Go00mvn-3Zc7-ODT4y9ENPTe8pLwrAGJsCxgbSaq9YAVYQWH8WO9q2tZJJeKcc2EWmAl_8Klh9YZy50WLRoxTnoYlBK83c0wjEpPtpfTDTauUOpJjWuvNmURULvWm6uOa6GE4Dc5dqJ3Uk1CDDiu2va86Tk6T7l0tCPhG-oWPvmFpVtzbIPZiY7a3P40cm7kfJ5n9_8N6QobOV9_LgHyOUFgP57KMx4s5egTEFZ2Yg34YfszEaPMKjydZ1DAemAQLdQKLhd25EqNnNti3HH6EHxVY9PzRwQfvtfQbym-jPwKAAD__2C4icM), R-Houston, as U.S. ambassador to Saudi Arabia on Monday, a post that has lacked a full-time appointee since the end of the Biden administration and requires Senate confirmation. The 44-year-old West Point graduate flew Apache helicopters for eight years and spent two deployments in the kingdom as a diplomatic liaison. Hunt called the nomination the "honor of a lifetime" and said his family has [given more than 60 years](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAUhJ8GOiPbgAmFi9uky223RMf2IVjrH2QfQvL2K_YVtp7RaL7v67E8wAefnv8hoqb3mpeEZw1IhGUBYzJRrTtYBAsO48d4V21ZJJeK8ZkJtYAl_8JlgNZpw90sWtRius3jqJTg7aanmQ9gVgmun1ewoxy5Wnk_3CTnaMXUen3N8VkoIXgvp04MTqqbECNOdjYDbwaOzlMuHW1I-Ia6hk9-Yelsjm3QG9Fem_5fI--NvJ_n2a35LdWWj0o5XaVG3i-uK8Ua8MO2IxFLOfoEhI7tBat3mIhROeLODNockUE0UCu4XNi3T0-XI6twOM-ggPHQFu3204fgq5qagT8j-PD7if7q8qXlTwAAAP__BUaMxg) to the military. Iran has been [firing on Saudi Arabia](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAUhJ8GOpB_wODCxTZ02XZLdGyfBEsGW_ZJCG-_4r7C7T5ppNHM9--xPiDEcLz-wo6Gvs-0HnjWiERYVrA2EdWawSE48LhfNvjqyiqYUB3THVcrOAofXAdovbHMa96i4dOsx1EpztrNSKW09_PsOUOtxSwln5_aSQsapFW2DeauY5orzpkUU88HL9TM-YiT03ZgzcDQB0qlpw0Jv1Cf8UofLL1LexvNRpRrI_80YmnEcp5nf8GW0p02YrkPNWLJKQYK7kYoFFzEG6m899wR5Npt6V0pHV3B_LYxODi6E2vEqxNCqlHMQvYb7bEtxuczxBiqmpqBvXYI8WcJ_dbgx4j_AQAA__-iY4b0) and blockading its energy shipments since February, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman asked Trump to strike the Iran-backed Houthis. Trump declined to do so. Hunt leaves the House in January after two terms, following a third-place finish in March's Senate Republican primary won by Attorney General Ken Paxton. He announced the nomination with an AI-generated image of [himself in mirrored aviator sunglasses](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2upDAQhE8DGchuzI8DB5uQzaYborbdDJYMRnbPMHP7Fe8KL65Slb7v32N5YIjheP7FnQx_1rQcdJVIzJQXtDYxl3KiI3Toaf_a4IvLCwgYGqEbOSzoOLxpUVh7Y4XXsiYjx0n3_TBIUW_Gr6MSFtZV6U5o2QNNq51AEU66H4Wqg7nnhJaDlKKDsZXKwzBJ2dPotFWiUoJ84JRb3ojpg2WN3_Sm3Lq019FszGepuj8VzBXM13W1bsvpuNMK5huoghkzBxfpLlCJ9G2218EN7hZLQZ9yU_DlQ4MZbcAGQHVyBN2e21ln488rxBjKMFZKPHcM8eeaf6vsbeB_AAAA__9nMoDQ) against the Riyadh skyline.

House Appropriations Chairman Greg Bonnen of Friendswood will lead the Texas team, which is working with the Texas Space Commission on a statewide proposal. "_No state can match what Texas brings to this mission_ ," Abbott said, pointing to Johnson Space Center, the state's universities, and its commercial space industry. Speaker Dustin Burrows cited the state's 15 military installations and research universities as reasons to put the academy here. Hey friends,I'm thrilled to share with you episode 11 of the Standing Tall podcast! I can’t wait for you to hear the stories Rev. Dr. Harold Middlebrook tells in this one.[**[CLICK HERE to LISTEN NOW**]](https://us.list-manage.com/99RVkDDCvmC?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
****

[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/152HaeEl583?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

I was honored to be able to sit down with Rev. Dr. Harold Middlebrook, a Memphis-born civil rights leader who worked directly with Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., organized voter registration drives across the South in the 1960s, and was present at the Lorraine Motel the day Dr. King was assassinated.

The Rev. Harold Middlebrook stands directly behind the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. during the Memphis sanitation workers' strike in March 1968. Also pictured are the Rev. Jesse Jackson, upper right, and Dr. H. Ralph Jackson, left.

His life spans from a 10th-grade voter registration drive in Memphis to decades of ministry here in Knoxville, and in this conversation he draws some striking, sobering lines between what he fought for then and what we're facing again now.We get into the poll tax and how voter suppression actually worked, why local elections like school boards matter just as much as national ones, and his very direct case for why waiting until Election Day is a risk nobody needs to take.This one is a genuine piece of living history, and I hope it gives you as much perspective as it gave me.

**🗳️Yesterday was National Voter Registration Day!** If you're not registered, or you've moved and need to update your info, today's the day. It takes five minutes and it matters. **Head to**[**proudvoter.org**](https://us.list-manage.com/Jm0DM4S9J_u?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**to check your status or get registered.** Rev. Middlebrook said it best in this episode: getting registered doesn't mean anything if you don't follow through and vote. _**So let's start with step one, today.**_

Thank you for being here,Gloria

Nobody answers.
Yesterday, at a Senate Judiciary hearing, Kash Patel announced the FBI may send agents to the polls this November:

The public charge rule is back. It takes effect Friday -- and half the country's attorneys general spent Monday racing to the courthouse to stop it.
This Friday -- September 18, 2026 -- one of the oldest principles in American immigration law snaps back into force. The Department of Homeland Security's new public charge rule goes live, and the Democratic Party's answer was to sprint into federal court before the ink dried.
On Monday, at least 23 states and the District of Columbia filed suit against DHS in Manhattan federal court -- New York AG Letitia James leading the charge, with Minnesota's Keith Ellison announcing his addition the same morning. New York City's Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced his own lawsuit. A coalition of activist groups, backed by a white-shoe Manhattan law firm, piled on with a second complaint.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/23d1d154-a813-43f4-aef5-cc4d91023c8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
What, exactly, are they suing to stop? The enforcement of a rule that predates the light bulb, the telephone, and Ellis Island itself.
**What happens Friday**
The rule rescinds Biden's 2022 regulation, which expressly took food stamps, Medicaid, and housing benefits out of the public-charge analysis entirely. Starting Friday, USCIS officers weighing green-card applications will apply a broader, totality-of-the-circumstances test: age, health, family status, financial resources, education, skills -- and yes, receipt of means-tested benefits like SNAP, non-emergency Medicaid, and government housing assistance.
Applications submitted on or after September 18 face the new scrutiny; benefits received before Friday are judged under the old, looser standard. Officers can also demand public-charge bonds from marginal applicants. Expect green cards to be declined at far higher rates -- and remember, under existing law, a green-card holder who becomes a public charge within five years of entry is already deportable.
And before the hysteria begins: refugees, asylees, and humanitarian categories like VAWA, U and T visas are exempt. This was never about punishing the persecuted. It's a filter for self-sufficiency.
**The numbers**
By the estimates rolled out with the rule, taxpayers stand to save roughly $13 billion a year, with as many as 5.6 million migrants potentially losing access to taxpayer-funded benefits. That's not a rounding error. That's a refund for the American worker -- the people actually paying into the system the program drains.
**The history Democrats hope you don 't read**
The public charge doctrine was not dreamed up at Mar-a-Lago. Congress wrote it into the Immigration Act of 1882, barring entry to "any person unable to take care of himself or herself without becoming a public charge." In 1996, bipartisan welfare reform reaffirmed the principle in federal law: aliens "generally should not depend on public resources," and the availability of benefits should not be an incentive to migrate to the United States.
The narrowing was the deviation. A 1999 bureaucratic guidance memo quietly shrank "public charge" to mean someone primarily dependent on cash handouts. Biden's 2022 rule went further still, declaring that food stamps, Medicaid, and housing benefits simply don't count. DHS's rule -- announced in July, published in the Federal Register on July 20 -- rescinds the 2022 regulation and restores the standard Congress actually enacted.
So when the lawsuits claim DHS "exceeded its statutory authority," the argument is upside down. The rule doesn't exceed the statute -- it *applies* the statute, 144 years later, exactly as Congress wrote and re-wrote it.
**The meltdown, translated**
The states' legal theory: the rule violates the Administrative Procedure Act because it "exceeds DHS's statutory authority" and "departs from the longstanding meaning" of public charge. Read that twice. The longstanding meaning is the 1882 one. It was the 1999-to-2022 dodge that departed from it. The plaintiffs are asking a court to freeze the deviation in place and call the restoration a violation.
It won't be easy. Since Loper Bright retired Chevron in 2024, courts owe no deference to an agency's clever reinterpretations -- they read the statute itself. The statute here is old, plain, and twice reaffirmed by Congress. On the merits, Democrats are arguing against the text of federal law. That's why the real strategy is venue shopping: file in Manhattan, find a friendly district judge, and win a nationwide injunction at the buzzer.
**My prediction**
I'll say it plainly: I would not be remotely surprised if a single Obama-appointed judge somewhere in a blue circuit halts the policy nationwide right before the finish line. That's the playbook -- it's exactly how district judges froze the last public-charge rule in 2019.
But look at how that round ended. The Supreme Court let the 2019 rule take effect almost everywhere in the country while the litigation ran. If this fight climbs the same ladder -- district court, circuit courts, then SCOTUS -- the plaintiffs will be arguing that non-citizens are entitled to taxpayer benefits, before a Court that has spent years reminding agencies that statutes mean what they say. The text is on one side. The meltdown is on the other.
**The Point**
No foreigner has a right to come to America and live off the taxpayer's back. A green card is a privilege extended to people who can stand on their own feet -- not an enrollment form for the welfare state. If Democrats want to spend their fall in court defending food stamps for visa applicants, that's their prerogative. They can explain it to voters in November.
Friday, the law takes effect. As it should have all along.

Democrats Are Suing to Stop America From Enforcing a Law Older Than the Statue of Liberty | | | Sep 16 | | | | | | | | | | | | The public charge rule is back. It takes effect Friday -- and half the country's attorneys general spent Monday racing to the courthouse to stop it. This Friday -- September 18, 2026 -- one of the oldest principles in American immigration law snaps back into force. The Department of Homeland Security's new public charge rule goes live, and the Democratic Party's answer was to sprint into federal court before the ink dried. On Monday, at least 23 states and the District of Columbia filed suit against DHS in Manhattan federal court -- New York AG Letitia James leading the charge, with Minnesota's Keith Ellison announcing his addition the same morning. New York City's Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced his own lawsuit. A coalition of activist groups, backed by a white-shoe Manhattan law firm, piled on with a second complaint. | | ---|---|--- What, exactly, are they suing to stop? The enforcement of a rule that predates the light bulb, the telephone, and Ellis Island itself. What happens Friday The rule rescinds Biden's 2022 regulation, which expressly took food stamps, Medicaid, and housing benefits out of the public-charge analysis entirely. Starting Friday, USCIS officers weighing green-card applications will apply a broader, totality-of-the-circumstances test: age, health, family status, financial resources, education, skills -- and yes, receipt of means-tested benefits like SNAP, non-emergency Medicaid, and government housing assistance. Applications submitted on or after September 18 face the new scrutiny; benefits received before Friday are judged under the old, looser standard. Officers can also demand public-charge bonds from marginal applicants. Expect green cards to be declined at far higher rates -- and remember, under existing law, a green-card holder who becomes a public charge within five years of entry is already deportable. And before the hysteria begins: refugees, asylees, and humanitarian categories like VAWA, U and T visas are exempt. This was never about punishing the persecuted. It's a filter for self-sufficiency. The numbers By the estimates rolled out with the rule, taxpayers stand to save roughly $13 billion a year, with as many as 5.6 million migrants potentially losing access to taxpayer-funded benefits. That's not a rounding error. That's a refund for the American worker -- the people actually paying into the system the program drains. The history Democrats hope you don 't read The public charge doctrine was not dreamed up at Mar-a-Lago. Congress wrote it into the Immigration Act of 1882, barring entry to "any person unable to take care of himself or herself without becoming a public charge." In 1996, bipartisan welfare reform reaffirmed the principle in federal law: aliens "generally should not depend on public resources," and the availability of benefits should not be an incentive to migrate to the United States. The narrowing was the deviation. A 1999 bureaucratic guidance memo quietly shrank "public charge" to mean someone primarily dependent on cash handouts. Biden's 2022 rule went further still, declaring that food stamps, Medicaid, and housing benefits simply don't count. DHS's rule -- announced in July, published in the Federal Register on July 20 -- rescinds the 2022 regulation and restores the standard Congress actually enacted. So when the lawsuits claim DHS "exceeded its statutory authority," the argument is upside down. The rule doesn't exceed the statute -- it applies the statute, 144 years later, exactly as Congress wrote and re-wrote it. The meltdown, translated The states' legal theory: the rule violates the Administrative Procedure Act because it "exceeds DHS's statutory authority" and "departs from the longstanding meaning" of public charge. Read that twice. The longstanding meaning is the 1882 one. It was the 1999-to-2022 dodge that departed from it. The plaintiffs are asking a court to freeze the deviation in place and call the restoration a violation. It won't be easy. Since Loper Bright retired Chevron in 2024, courts owe no deference to an agency's clever reinterpretations -- they read the statute itself. The statute here is old, plain, and twice reaffirmed by Congress. On the merits, Democrats are arguing against the text of federal law. That's why the real strategy is venue shopping: file in Manhattan, find a friendly district judge, and win a nationwide injunction at the buzzer. My prediction I'll say it plainly: I would not be remotely surprised if a single Obama-appointed judge somewhere in a blue circuit halts the policy nationwide right before the finish line. That's the playbook -- it's exactly how district judges froze the last public-charge rule in 2019. But look at how that round ended. The Supreme Court let the 2019 rule take effect almost everywhere in the country while the litigation ran. If this fight climbs the same ladder -- district court, circuit courts, then SCOTUS -- the plaintiffs will be arguing that non-citizens are entitled to taxpayer benefits, before a Court that has spent years reminding agencies that statutes mean what they say. The text is on one side. The meltdown is on the other. The Point No foreigner has a right to come to America and live off the taxpayer's back. A green card is a privilege extended to people who can stand on their own feet -- not an enrollment form for the welfare state. If Democrats want to spend their fall in court defending food stamps for visa applicants, that's their prerogative. They can explain it to voters in November. Friday, the law takes effect. As it should have all along. Enjoyed this? Subscribe and share it with someone who thinks "enforce the law" is a radical position.* Thanks for reading! This post is public so feel free to share it. _With an election coming up on November 3:**vote NO on Proposition A**. Voting NO strikes down an egregiously gerrymandered map that the Missouri legislature passed last year._1
_Here 's_ _a link to[People Not Politicians](https://substack.com/redirect/beb714fd-97ad-41d3-9ea4-1d84159a8d18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Richard von Glahn's organization that is leading the effort to defeat Proposition A._
* * *
When Missouri politics is a national headline, it's seldom anything good. But these past few weeks have been particularly bruising.
Yesterday, I spoke with Richard von Glahn. Over the past week, his case has been in front of the United States Supreme Court twice, in front of the Missouri Supreme Court three times, and in lower federal courts a few times just for good measure.2
Why? He was the plaintiff in a case that sought to uphold Missourians' right to initiate a veto referendum--which, in this case, would suspend the newly gerrymandered map that the Missouri legislature passed last year pending a statewide vote.
So why all the drama? Well, there's much more on that in our conversation.
### Topics from my conversation with Richard von Glahn
* _0:00 - 3:00_: Introduction, Richard's background, and his involvement in democracy issues.
* _3:01 - 7:06_: How Missouri's Secretary of State tried to forcibly implement a new map--without any authority to do so.
* _7:07 - 15:39_: A recap of last week's news, when the whiplash of Missouri redistricting became national news. (Or, what happens when elected Republicans sue other elected Republicans--even when they're all in cahoots.)
* _15:40 - 20:53_: What happens when the legislature commits its energy to unpopular policies?
* _20:54 - 28:11_: How do you get Republicans to vote against Proposition A?
* _28:12 - 30:44_: If Proposition A fails, will the legislature try this gambit again?
* _30:45 - 37:22_: Does this change the paradigm of redistricting in Missouri forever? What happens after the next census when Missouri is _required_ to redraw its map?
* _37:23 - 41:30_: Isn't it weird to run primaries and general elections in different districts?
* _41:31 - 43:44_: Besides voting no, what else can people do to defeat Proposition A?

We talk about a few different people, policies, and ballot measures; I've defined a bunch of them in the footnotes.3
One thing to keep in mind: **this isn 't a ruling on the constitutionality of gerrymanders**. Neither the Missouri Supreme Court nor the U.S. Supreme Court has changed its position on that. This was a very narrow ruling on the procedures of Missouri ballot measures, a ruling that was necessary because Secretary of State Denny Hoskins consistently refused to do his job.

### Remind me what all the gerrymandering fuss is about?
Last September, the Missouri legislature [redrew its already gerrymandered congressional map](https://substack.com/redirect/eac6470a-d311-4e83-b501-cb1d18f8b326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). With the new map, Missouri would likely have elected seven Republicans and one Democrat (rather than six Republicans and two Democrats), something the legislature accomplished by splitting Kansas City across three different heavily Republican districts.
But Missouri allows its citizens to [initiate what's called a veto referendum](https://substack.com/redirect/c7d26428-4caa-4eee-9940-eebf8d52cc6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): if enough signatures are gathered within 90 days, legislation is suspended pending a statewide vote.
[People Not Politicians](https://substack.com/redirect/beb714fd-97ad-41d3-9ea4-1d84159a8d18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) did just that, [gathering 300,000 signatures statewide](https://substack.com/redirect/5d1da3d8-318d-46c5-b636-1720e2277312?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), well over the threshold needed to suspend the legislation and trigger a statewide vote.
With elected officials who cared to follow the law, that would've been that. But Hoskins, [whose bad faith and](https://substack.com/redirect/520ace08-5c4d-4bde-8e06-199ce65039f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [incompetence I've](https://substack.com/redirect/ecf4b4a3-0d73-45c4-9b62-a458b6610aa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [written about before](https://substack.com/redirect/40e463a1-fbbc-4741-baf1-34f7c9d904e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), decided to play a game of chicken. He figured that if he slow-rolled things enough--throwing out signatures with flimsy justification, refusing to certify the ballot measure, frivolously questioning its constitutionality--the [Purcell principle](https://substack.com/redirect/3d42cadc-8d9b-4a5b-88b7-a73be12b7069?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) would kick in and make it impossible for courts to intervene.
His willful delays and noncompliance created the absolute mess we've seen unfold over the last month. You may have followed the whiplash last week, as Missouri see-sawed from one congressional map to another just weeks before the election. If you want the full rundown, that's in the footnotes.4
But the issue is now (almost certainly) settled: our congressional map in this election won't have changed from 2024. Richard and I discussed what this means for the rule of law, Missouri, and gerrymandering.
### A (constitutional) crisis of their own making
[Hoskins](https://substack.com/redirect/5fd43ee9-8f64-4557-944a-b628b415e86e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Attorney General Catherine Hanaway](https://substack.com/redirect/501837c4-3453-4efd-a089-ae496e626111?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), also a Republican, both referred to this whole situation as a "constitutional crisis."5
It's an absurd claim. Hoskins spent months intentionally slowing things down; Hanaway publicly acknowledged that "[delay works in our favor](https://substack.com/redirect/be2be24c-f122-4e2f-b0de-cdb345daaba9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." Then they all but ignored court orders until Hoskins was held in contempt.
This isn't a constitutional crisis; in the end, the rule of law won, though we got there as chaotically as possible. But to the extent that you _do_ consider this a constitutional crisis, they're the only ones to blame.6
What we should worry about, though, is the willingness that elected officials have to subvert the law either by slow-rolling their obligations or by ignoring courts altogether.
I've been reading a [few](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9db8fd-6cdd-4775-a27d-b2d444aa7ae1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [different](https://substack.com/redirect/5162c553-c539-4986-8476-98bee44eb2cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [articles](https://substack.com/redirect/60f01892-f6b1-49d7-abad-122dc318eb10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [lately](https://substack.com/redirect/8adc15e3-89b6-4357-9de0-ae553a10e53f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [about](https://substack.com/redirect/6416a71e-f95d-4c2a-852a-e45784692d96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) what this means heading into the midterm elections. **Chaos, delay, and confusion are part of the strategy, and that 's frightening**.
To [quote Quinton Lucas](https://substack.com/redirect/e3d2646a-fadd-42cf-bf1f-b12708a73ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the mayor of Kansas City: "Usually in politics, we ask ourselves if someone's actually being nefarious or incompetent. Here is just a magical mix of both."
But for now, despite the best efforts of Missouri's lawmakers, the rule of law held. Now it's on us, as voters, to take the first step towards defeating gerrymandering by voting NO on Proposition A.

Importantly: voting no also keeps most of Kansas City in one congressional district, rather than [slicing it across three districts](https://substack.com/redirect/5c82489b-46e5-41eb-ae6b-ffc5375e4040?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Kansas City's welfare and growth are absolutely essential for the state; it needs its own representative.
2
If you law nerds want to be pedantic:
* I think it's technically multiple different cases, but they all came from this same veto referendum effort, so I'll count it.
* The math of what counts is a little squishy--does Denny Hoskins' contempt hearing count?--but the numbers should give you some sense of the week he's had.

3
Here's some of what we spoke about:
* **[Denny Hoskins](https://substack.com/redirect/15a7e489-db52-4856-94bd-e3d09f4794b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** : Missouri's Secretary of State, first elected two years ago.
* **[Catherine Hanaway](https://substack.com/redirect/7bcf0656-762e-4472-b1f4-54fd1ff22bb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** : Missouri's Attorney General, first appointed (not elected, because she was filling a vacancy) last year.
* **[Proposition A](https://substack.com/redirect/8d49b2cc-a8e7-4d82-aea6-af646e062d04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** : The ballot measure in question; a NO vote strikes down the legislature's gerrymandered congressional map.
* **[Amendment 3](https://substack.com/redirect/4de416e8-c025-4701-8289-63eb2caf9f9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** : This will also be on the ballot in November, and it would strike down legalized abortion in the state after voters approved it two years ago.
* **[Amendment 4](https://substack.com/redirect/a6bcac29-8519-4514-a557-a4c7e84946df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** : The legislature tried to make it [functionally impossible to pass future citizen-initiated ballot measures](https://substack.com/redirect/74ca0a47-c7f9-4d76-95bd-7c618924f701?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The effort, which was on the August ballot, failed spectacularly; the "yes" vote was under 20%.
* **[Amendment 5](https://substack.com/redirect/6d419f81-aff2-4cf4-81b1-4caecd5e502c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** : The legislature tried to repeal the state's income tax, which would in practice [increase taxes for 80% of Missourians](https://substack.com/redirect/44fe34d7-d8d8-412a-bdad-c98146b9a6e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This was also on the August ballot and also failed spectacularly; the "yes" vote was under 17%.
* **[2018"right-to-work" referendum](https://substack.com/redirect/4c63e5d5-f53d-466c-a15a-88ea41e86173?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**: The state's last veto referendum; it was voted down handily. The "yes" vote was only 32.5%.
* **[Veto referendum](https://substack.com/redirect/4f9c3e74-0ce7-4e1c-8a1d-db6a7c688ad1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** : Here's a description from Ballotpedia on how it works in Missouri:

> A **veto referendum** is a [citizen-initiated ballot measure](https://substack.com/redirect/b8b05634-3381-4c79-b041-047c751cf4d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that asks voters whether to uphold or repeal an enacted law. This type of ballot measure is also called _statute referendum_ , _popular referendum_ , _people 's veto_, or _citizen 's veto_. There are 23 states that allow citizens to initiate veto referendums.
> In Missouri, the [number of signatures required](https://substack.com/redirect/681f82bd-f020-4220-89ba-6b31a94807f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a veto referendum is based on the number of votes cast for governor in the state's most recent gubernatorial election. In two-thirds of Missouri's congressional districts, proponents must collect signatures equal to 5% of the gubernatorial vote for veto referendums. A simple majority vote is required for voter approval.
One other point: here's an article that I wrote last year:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/54d17187-2620-4d61-a969-66032c5c2121?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [The week Missouri stopped caring](https://substack.com/redirect/54d17187-2620-4d61-a969-66032c5c2121?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/profile/12425779-ben-samuels)| | *
---|---|---
| September 10, 2025
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/54d17187-2620-4d61-a969-66032c5c2121?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It's worth noting that most or all of these efforts have been beaten back, though not without great difficulty. Challenging though it may be, we do have ways to stand up for what we believe in.
4
If you need a refresher on what's likely the final battle of this year's national redistricting war:
* _August 19_ : A Cole County judge [rules that the newly gerrymandered map can stand](https://substack.com/redirect/59ba658c-1ab7-4858-9c0c-36e588ca28e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). New map in use.
* _September 3_ : The Missouri Supreme Court [reverses that decision](https://substack.com/redirect/db2069e7-3dde-4ab6-93e6-e56158cf4dc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Old map in use.
* _September 8_ : The U.S. Supreme Court [declines to reverse](https://substack.com/redirect/f44f0d21-9612-472e-b71a-2e52e7530864?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Missouri Supreme Court's decision. Old map in use.
* _September 8, a few minutes later_ : A district court judge, [noting in his opinion](https://substack.com/redirect/e3d2646a-fadd-42cf-bf1f-b12708a73ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he was aware of the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling, orders Missouri to revert to the new map anyway. Unclear which map is in use.
* _September 8, later that evening_ : Hoskins ignores the U.S. Supreme Court ruling and [defers to the district court ruling](https://substack.com/redirect/e7b803ac-dc2e-41b4-8a0c-5ca0e91b689a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The Missouri Supreme Court [questions whether Hoskins is in contempt](https://substack.com/redirect/ee04f21d-238d-453e-bafc-e1144d207d67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Unclear which map is in use.
* _September 9_ : The Eighth Circuit Court [refuses to stay the district court's order](https://substack.com/redirect/c12a219f-33d1-4b18-bd94-d93b3645c631?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) but leaves unaddressed the question of the U.S. Supreme Court's earlier ruling. Unclear which map is in use.
* _September 10_ : The [U.S. Supreme Court, again, sides with the Missouri Supreme Court](https://substack.com/redirect/5114c758-749f-4329-8dac-77ff9e419a98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with no dissents. Old map in use.
* _September 10, an hour or so later_ : Hoskins' legal team, in front of the Missouri Supreme Court, [refuses to say whether it would honor the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling](https://substack.com/redirect/8fc89b39-55b1-491e-89e2-8e5b3a7ca6a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Unclear which map is in use.
* _September 10, a few hours later_ : Finally, after the Missouri Supreme Court tells Hoskins to "not venture far from Jefferson City," Hoskins [gives in to the law](https://substack.com/redirect/3438f7f1-8701-4b73-aba7-7f6724831572?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and reverts to the old map. The Missouri Supreme Court ruled that [Hoskins had been in contempt of court](https://substack.com/redirect/8fc89b39-55b1-491e-89e2-8e5b3a7ca6a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) but had purged the contempt by following the court's orders. Old map in use.

Redistricting shouldn't be so complicated that it requires day-by-day timestamps and color-coding, especially this close to an election. Welcome to Missouri!
5
Others, including [Governor Mike Kehoe](https://substack.com/redirect/5e4ffe1f-14c4-4669-91cb-987db75ac709?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), used similar language, though not that exact phrasing.
6
By the way, Hoskins' former director of election integrity is accusing him of the cardinal sin of election administration: [tampering with election results](https://substack.com/redirect/a199b739-c952-4892-9103-2aa71efb5e24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

subject: What I saw in Gaza is the very core of why I’m running.

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_ahh_email-26q3?refcode=x_26q3_gaza_int3_acq [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_ahh_email-26q3?refcode=x_26q3_gaza_int3_acq]
Hi friend,
I’ve worked across the world helping patients survive combat and disaster zones, both as a combat trauma surgeon and as a volunteer surgeon. But my experience in Gaza in 2024 is at the very core of why I’m running for Congress.
I treated children pulled from rubble and people who survived bombings, only for the majority of them to die within 48 hours due to malnutrition and a lack of medical supplies—an intentional act of genocide funded by our tax dollars. I still struggle to process what I witnessed. And I saw our leaders in Washington deploy military resources in Gaza, Venezuela, and Iran—while telling us we don’t have the money to take care of our communities here at home.
It’s this hypocrisy that made me want to run for Congress. Our government is spending our tax dollars to fund these atrocities and enable genocides, while Americans are dying without healthcare, getting price-gouged at the grocery store, and struggling with the rising gas prices.
None of this is accidental. It’s the result of leaders who are voting without consequence, captured by elite interests, and making decisions in their own self-interest instead of yours.
And last month, voters right here in NJ-12 sent a message of their own.
Despite racist and smear efforts to shape this race, our grassroots campaign won the Democratic primary for New Jersey's 12th Congressional District. That victory showed something important: people are tired of politics that serve powerful interests while everyday families and vulnerable communities are left behind.
But challenging the status quo is never easy. The interests that benefit from our broken system aren't going away, and neither are the obstacles standing in the way of real change.
We need representatives who will fight for peace, human dignity, accountability, and working families. We need champions of peace, stability, and humanitarianism in Congress. I intend to be one of them.

Friend 🐾,

I’m barking in your inbox today because I’ve been one busy pup! My mom brought me along to a very special place: **Chaco Canyon!**
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16410?refcode=jtk1394-fr-nd&t=2&akid=12496%2E400544%2EeV_QOH)
I got to explore, take in all the new smells, and spend some time outside with my mom. But I know Chaco isn’t just a great place for a walk. It’s a sacred place that means so much to my mom, Tribal communities, and generations of New Mexicans.
**Chaco holds a special place in my mom’s heart. She’s spent years fighting to protect it and the other sacred lands that make New Mexico so special. And as Governor, she’ll keep fighting to make sure these places are here for generations to come._But she can’t do it alone_. ****[Will you paw-lease chip in $5 or $10 today to give my mom the resources she needs to win this election and keep protecting New Mexico?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16410?refcode=jtk1394-fr-nd&t=3&akid=12496%2E400544%2EeV_QOH)**

I may be just a pup, but even I know there’s something special about this place. I watched my mom take it all in, and I could tell Chaco means more to her than just a beautiful place to visit.
It reminded her of all the time she spent outside with her dad. She grew up running through the desert with her cousins and fishing with him. Those memories taught her that we have a responsibility to take care of the places we call home.

_And that’s why she’s so worried about what’s happening right now._
Donald Trump is moving to slash protections for the lands surrounding Chaco and reopen them to mining and oil and gas drilling. **That means putting a place that has been sacred to Indigenous peoples since time immemorial at risk.**

**My mom says Chaco is not for sale.**

body:
And here is the part every conservative must understand:

| | | |

Fellow Conservative: In 1991, the mob came for Clarence Thomas. They smeared him. They tried to destroy his name, his reputation, and his honor. As Justice Thomas himself has put it, critics in Washington _"don't bomb you, necessarily, but they bomb your reputation or your good name or your honor."_ **He refused to cave.** And because he did, he became one of the four giants of the modern Supreme Court -- alongside Justices Scalia, Alito, and Rehnquist. Senator Ted Cruz has just released a remarkable new book: _**Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas**_ , built on exclusive interviews with the Justice himself.

---
|
---
---
|
---
It tells the story of a man who rose from grinding poverty in Pin Point, Georgia -- raised by a grandfather he calls _"the single greatest human being I've ever met"_ -- to become, in Cruz's words, the justice _"more willing to go back to the original Constitution... and to overturn precedent" than any other in history._

There's a moment in the book that says everything. When Justice Scalia told Thomas he was _"tilting at windmills"_ by trying to overturn bad precedent, Thomas shot back: _"Nino, windmills are dangerous."_

That is the kind of courage we need on the federal bench. And here is the part every conservative must understand:

**Clarence Thomas only reached the Supreme Court because the Senate confirmed him by just two votes.**

Presidents nominate judges. But the Senate confirms them. Every originalist on the bench, and every one we hope to see there, depends on having conservative senators willing to fight. When we lose the Senate, we lose the courts. It's that simple.

That's the mission of the Senate Conservatives Fund: electing principled conservatives to the U.S. Senate so we can confirm the next generation of Clarence Thomases, and stop the Left from ever again turning a confirmation hearing into a character assassination.

So today, we want to put Senator Cruz's book in your hands.

subject: We URGENTLY need your help (re: Trump rally in NC)
body:
President Trump is going out of his way to help Whatley defeat me.
| | | | |
---
Peter, we’re following up on Roy’s alert from yesterday:
**President Trump just touched down in Gastonia, NC ahead of his rally with Roy’s MAGA opponent, Michael Whatley.**
We know he’s going to tell a lot of lies, but that’s not the only reason we’re worried.
It took just shy of $100 million for the GOP to cut Roy’s slim lead in the polls down to a statistical tie. After tonight, we expect a surge in dark money to run ads broadcasting the president’s attacks statewide – and unless we build the grassroots resources to respond ASAP, it could erase Roy’s lead entirely.
**That’s why we’re setting a $100,000 rapid-response goal to ensure we can fight back as soon as President Trump takes the stage at 7:00 p.m. tonight.[_The stakes could not be higher, so please rush any amount you can right now to help us immediately push back against the President’s lies, win in North Carolina and flip the Senate majority blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1505&amount=5&t=2&akid=3580%2E124072%2Ey3NRX7)
Thank you – keep reading if you missed Roy’s original update.
Team Cooper
\---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: **Roy Cooper** <info@e.roycooper.com>

Subject: Urgent update to share with you, Peter.

---
**President Trump is coming to North Carolina tomorrow to hold a massive MAGA rally alongside my GOP opponent, Michael Whatley** – and we have less than 24 hours to prepare for all the attacks about to be hurled our way.
[**_Will you rush a contribution right now toward my $2.5 million mid-month goal? Meeting it by tonight’s deadline is the only way we’ll have the resources to fight back against whatever comes next._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1505&amount=5&t=4&akid=3580%2E124072%2Ey3NRX7)

The president and the GOP know that if we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will lose out on our shot to take back the Senate majority.
**That’s why they’re pulling out all the stops to defeat our people-powered movement:** holding rallies, spreading lies and misinformation about me and investing millions of dollars to crush our momentum. With President Trump having just poured $5 million from his own campaign war chest into this race, the GOP is now investing more than $100 million so far to defeat me.
**Tomorrow’s Trump visit will give the green light to MAGA megadonors across the country to flood North Carolina with _even more_ dark money – all because Senate control is at stake in this race.**
There’s no way I can fight back – let alone flip this seat blue – without the support of people like you, Peter. This is an all-hands-on-deck moment, so I’m personally asking:
[**_Please, will you make a well-timed donation of $5 or any amount right now to help us close the gap on our crucial mid-month goal and ensure I can respond to President Trump’s oncoming attacks?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1505&amount=5&t=9&akid=3580%2E124072%2Ey3NRX7)

subject: Think AI Doesn’t Affect You? Think Again.
body:
Jobs are only part of the story. We found what else the AI boom could change.

| | |
---

**Good Morning!** Think AI doesn't have much to do with you? **You may want to watch this.** Artificial intelligence is being called one of the [**biggest stories in the world**](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJysz0Fu6yAUheHVmFksuMZgBgze4GXUdBq1E4ThEtNgE9nXibL7KlWX0AV8R-c_n9zJ55KXy7uf0VKqLtWwb27Bx1aQCFdHU16uPseK20I-JQz0rDtN2QEHdeDmINSvEizahAjYMbRCD6ZXWsmeTVYpLZMP0qNRgGbodYiQ_DiMgFEkybJ9rXEjlJBcQ9fG5AfQ3gTe9YgjNJJjzFTX9qvmhSZM5VnvuLahzqzYiei2Nd2_Bo4NHF8H93bEBo7eXd_O83_8PH-w1cbbI5eSN6UbyS-zz-XH0x-k3y18BwAA___k33EK)--but the impact goes far beyond ChatGPT and Silicon Valley. [**Could AI threaten your job?**](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJysz0Fu6yAUheHVmFksuMZgBgze4GXUdBq1E4ThEtNgE9nXibL7KlWX0AV8R-c_n9zJ55KXy7uf0VKqLtWwb27Bx1aQCFdHU16uPseK20I-JQz0rDtN2QEHdeDmINSvEizahAjYMbRCD6ZXWsmeTVYpLZMP0qNRgGbodYiQ_DiMgFEkybJ9rXEjlJBcQ9fG5AfQ3gTe9YgjNJJjzFTX9qvmhSZM5VnvuLahzqzYiei2Nd2_Bo4NHF8H93bEBo7eXd_O83_8PH-w1cbbI5eSN6UbyS-zz-XH0x-k3y18BwAA___k33EK) Why could it be affecting your electric bill and water supply? And who decided massive data centers could start showing up near American communities? **More importantly, is anyone actually in charge of what happens next?** We dug past the predictions and hype to find the facts--and uncovered **one number buried in the data that helps explain why AI feels like a crisis to some Americans and a non-event to others.** It's probably not the number you'd expect. ([See what we found](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJysz0Fu6yAUheHVmFksuMZgBgze4GXUdBq1E4ThEtNgE9nXibL7KlWX0AV8R-c_n9zJ55KXy7uf0VKqLtWwb27Bx1aQCFdHU16uPseK20I-JQz0rDtN2QEHdeDmINSvEizahAjYMbRCD6ZXWsmeTVYpLZMP0qNRgGbodYiQ_DiMgFEkybJ9rXEjlJBcQ9fG5AfQ3gTe9YgjNJJjzFTX9qvmhSZM5VnvuLahzqzYiei2Nd2_Bo4NHF8H93bEBo7eXd_O83_8PH-w1cbbI5eSN6UbyS-zz-XH0x-k3y18BwAA___k33EK)) **➤** In our first **_Flyover Focus_** , we follow three Americans--a recent college grad, a business owner, and a rancher--to see who's already feeling the AI boom, who isn't, and what could be coming next. ([Watch _Flyover Focus_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJysz0Fu6yAUheHVmFksuMZgBgze4GXUdBq1E4ThEtNgE9nXibL7KlWX0AV8R-c_n9zJ55KXy7uf0VKqLtWwb27Bx1aQCFdHU16uPseK20I-JQz0rDtN2QEHdeDmINSvEizahAjYMbRCD6ZXWsmeTVYpLZMP0qNRgGbodYiQ_DiMgFEkybJ9rXEjlJBcQ9fG5AfQ3gTe9YgjNJJjzFTX9qvmhSZM5VnvuLahzqzYiei2Nd2_Bo4NHF8H93bEBo7eXd_O83_8PH-w1cbbI5eSN6UbyS-zz-XH0x-k3y18BwAA___k33EK))

clean_body: Jobs are only part of the story. We found what else the AI boom could change. | | | Good Morning! Think AI doesn't have much to do with you? You may want to watch this. Artificial intelligence is being called one of the the impact goes far beyond ChatGPT and Silicon Valley. Why could it be affecting your electric bill and water supply? And who decided massive data centers could start showing up near American communities? More importantly, is anyone actually in charge of what happens next? We dug past the predictions and hype to find the facts--and uncovered one number buried in the data that helps explain why AI feels like a crisis to some Americans and a non-event to others. It's probably not the number you'd expect. () ➤ In our first Flyover Focus , we follow three Americans--a recent college grad, a business owner, and a rancher--to see who's already feeling the AI boom, who isn't, and what could be coming next. () If you like what you see, catch The Flyover Podcast , the news you need seven days a week. body:
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8941%2E582294%2EHcePgs)
I’m sorry to tell you this, but it’s true:
**_New Hampshire is shifting in MAGA’S favor._**
FIRST: National Republicans gained a 3-to-1 spending advantage over us on the airwaves.
THEN: Back-to-back polls dropped showing John Sununu taking the lead over Chris for the first time in this campaign.
NOW: **Inside Elections and the Cook Political Report have shifted their rating of this race to a Toss Up.**

He wants to eliminate U.S. borders, wants free healthcare for illegals, to abolish ICE, to defund the police, “redistribute all the wealth,” and called the nuclear family a “violent” way to structure society.
---
|

| [Stop the Socialists](https://us.list-manage.com/qq5ukHFj2fz?e=62ddd24c19&c2id=03279232eb9d9ae6defa587a8b1aeaf0)

[ I need your help. Please donate whatever you can today, $5, $10, $25, $50, $100, or even $250.](https://us.list-manage.com/uc_B8tm3aiK?e=62ddd24c19&c2id=03279232eb9d9ae6defa587a8b1aeaf0)
**There’s just 48 days until the election and what you do today matters. I hope I can count on you.**

Friends -
First and foremost, I want to thank you for the support you've given me through all of my campaigns.
As you know, I am no fan of having to send out these emails and text messages. Sometimes I have a hard time wrapping my head around the idea that people actually contribute in response to them.
But hundreds of thousands of people have -- and there's no telling what the outcome of my previous races may have been if they ignored messages like this.
Today, I am asking you to join them. Here's why:
The outcome of this election will determine whether we are able to put a check on President Trump during the final two years of his term. We have to take back the House and the Senate.
Taking those majorities back will run through Michigan, where we have a Senate seat we must defend and a few key House races we can flip from red to blue. And I am also being asked to travel to help elect Democrats in red and purple places that Donald Trump won, and where I know we can flip.
All that takes resources, so I am asking people who care to step up and help as the election heats up.

As you know, I am no fan of having to send out these emails and text messages. Sometimes I have a hard time wrapping my head around the idea that people actually contribute in response to them. But hundreds of thousands of people have -- and there's no telling what the outcome of my previous races may have been if they ignored messages like this. Today, I am asking you to join them. Here's why: The outcome of this election will determine whether we are able to put a check on President Trump during the final two years of his term. We have to take back the House and the Senate. Taking those majorities back will run through Michigan, where we have a Senate seat we must defend and a few key House races we can flip from red to blue. And I am also being asked to travel to help elect Democrats in red and purple places that Donald Trump won, and where I know we can flip. All that takes resources, so I am asking people who care to step up and help as the election heats up. If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly: | | ** | | | | | | | ** Thank you again for your continued support. It means a lot to me. On August 21, 2026, I delivered a short speech at the inaugural Freedom Summit in Manchester, New Hampshire. During the course of my comments, I explored the link between America's promise of equal opportunity and the United States' unrivaled capacity to innovate. I argued that creative destruction (and the ability to improve the future) is only possible because America is a land that protects individual rights and thereby enables people to think differently and pursue new ideas. I highlight two New Hampshire success stories (Planet Fitness and Stonyfield Farms) before reminding the audience that we must all work tirelessly to practice and protect these freedoms. The session concludes with a brief conversation with successful entrepreneur and venture capitalist Jeremy Hitchcock.

body:
But what does it actually mean to be a PA WFP member? | | | Peter, Have you ever wondered what it actually means to be a member of the PA Working Families Party? Maybe you’ve donated to WFP, volunteered on a campaign, come to an event, or followed our work for years. There are lots of ways to be part of what we do. But you might still be wondering: What does it mean to actually become a _member_? What comes with it? And what do members actually do? **That’s what we’re talking about during our September Membership Drive.** [**If you’re ready to take part, you can join as a dues-paying PA WFP member with a recurring contribution of $10 or more a month or make a one-time contribution through our September Membership Drive link here.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqt-Go8R3mlvuiS8nmh_Gz7hV4yABEiE-TeLBb6M6MKOT4qCYjZezrReO6zG0IZ1FsyVkGWolbDTRfBWcvlD5_Q1QoPyhTxWetF7HXvjNjUAkc4hY5IqEjNzdeR594dv8Rn0pv3PxbcgO9SoYgCDaKp5Y2tt6NHxB2QMbcz1vohh5pkQjxQ2ZigAGK0A-bWvkCA6WuVdUxZFCWN2swF7buIh1_YhgFb-Ai-rc7MaHRmkSExmKDH0-XG9YUwHHMvqDHubyyOwu0Vo6KIcXLkEcOOyAxQt1kGRQBfaDlIiZmFTk9uOCJmqToI64JQFV-O8z4GBButp4IaSpEbzxuRTCc6ubtzjtFCqQh5TlbCk7rqIhvMCx1GbS3rvwTNLWF1Eguo/4u3/YeB3iNmVQpWjdtZzjgpsiQ/h0/h001.2wFymd_FNqnZZ9Qe9iyMz3bIKZ1H9Ngv3rU_ImOMi4M) And as a small thank-you for supporting our September Membership Drive, we’ll send you a little something: 💛 New monthly contributors at $10 or more will receive a PA WFP magnet. 💛 One-time contributors of any amount will receive a PA WFP sticker. **[Become a dues-paying member »](Link?link_id=1&can_id=12471c8e444f80358077c9724aea85a0&source=email-our-annual-membership-drive-is-here&email_referrer=email_3403643&email_subject=our-annual-membership-drive-is-here-_&&)** **So, what does membership actually look like?** It means having more ways to plug into the party and the work we’re building together. PA WFP members can participate in endorsement interviews, help identify potential candidates, join gatherings and organizing efforts, and weigh in on certain decisions about the direction of the party. **And yes, there’s an actual membership card.** Members also get updates about major WFP news and invitations to our monthly online WFP Assembly, where members from across the country come together. There are opportunities to participate in some of WFP’s bigger decisions too, including our presidential endorsement. Some members want to be deeply involved. Others show up when and where they can. There isn’t one right way to be a member. The point is having more opportunities to stay connected, participate, and have a hand in building the party over time. **Membership is also one of the ways people help sustain the work they’re part of.** Dues-paying membership starts at $10 a month ($120 a year). When members contribute month after month, those dues create a steady base of support for work that happens throughout the year, not just when Election Day is around the corner. Here in Pennsylvania, that means organizing in communities, identifying and recruiting candidates, training people to run, supporting campaigns and elected officials, and building relationships that carry from one election into the next. And those election cycles move quickly. We’re focused on 2026 right now, but after November, the work continues into 2027, including Philadelphia’s municipal elections, when every district and at-large City Council seat will be up again. The work for those races starts long before Election Day. Finding candidates, building relationships, organizing in communities, and preparing for what comes next all take time. Put those pieces together, and that’s really what membership is: a way to stay connected, take part in the party, and help sustain the work we’re building together from one election to the next. clean_body: But what does it actually mean to be a PA WFP member? | | | Peter, Have you ever wondered what it actually means to be a member of the PA Working Families Party? Maybe you’ve donated to WFP, volunteered on a campaign, come to an event, or followed our work for years. There are lots of ways to be part of what we do. But you might still be wondering: What does it mean to actually become a member? What comes with it? And what do members actually do? That’s what we’re talking about during our September Membership Drive. And as a small thank-you for supporting our September Membership Drive, we’ll send you a little something: 💛 New monthly contributors at $10 or more will receive a PA WFP magnet. 💛 One-time contributors of any amount will receive a PA WFP sticker. Link?linkid=1&canid=12471c8e444f80358077c9724aea85a0&source=email-our-annual-membership-drive-is-here&emailreferrer=email3403643&emailsubject=our-annual-membership-drive-is-here-&& So, what does membership actually look like? It means having more ways to plug into the party and the work we’re building together. PA WFP members can participate in endorsement interviews, help identify potential candidates, join gatherings and organizing efforts, and weigh in on certain decisions about the direction of the party. And yes, there’s an actual membership card. Members also get updates about major WFP news and invitations to our monthly online WFP Assembly, where members from across the country come together. There are opportunities to participate in some of WFP’s bigger decisions too, including our presidential endorsement. Some members want to be deeply involved. Others show up when and where they can. There isn’t one right way to be a member. The point is having more opportunities to stay connected, participate, and have a hand in building the party over time. Membership is also one of the ways people help sustain the work they’re part of. Dues-paying membership starts at $10 a month ($120 a year). When members contribute month after month, those dues create a steady base of support for work that happens throughout the year, not just when Election Day is around the corner. Here in Pennsylvania, that means organizing in communities, identifying and recruiting candidates, training people to run, supporting campaigns and elected officials, and building relationships that carry from one election into the next. And those election cycles move quickly. We’re focused on 2026 right now, but after November, the work continues into 2027, including Philadelphia’s municipal elections, when every district and at-large City Council seat will be up again. The work for those races starts long before Election Day. Finding candidates, building relationships, organizing in communities, and preparing for what comes next all take time. **Wednesday, September 16, 2026**
Slithering shapes in the ground always remind me of that rattler, coiled and ready. The dogs encircled it, barked, grunted. I ran for the pitchfork, but time failed.
Ernesto was the worst off. Ulysses and Lorenzo took their hits. Their faces swelled. Their blood dripped. They secured the safety of the chicks nearby.
There is a hard truth in the bite: with some predators you cannot reason. I walk the dogs on chains now. A tactical adjustment for their safety. In the halls of power, as in the fields, you must recognize the snake and adjust your armor.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Now, Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

# **Bill Maher slams Macklemore, Democrats over "genocide" claims on Gaza**
Bill Maher **[criticized the musician Macklemore for calling the Gaza war a"genocide"](https://substack.com/redirect/47225ea5-3dc8-4c6f-b049-52ed641dbffc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during a September concert opening for Ed Sheeran, arguing the characterization is false and that Democrats broadly embracing the term marks one of the party's worst moments in decades.
[| | | | | StandWithUs
---
@StandWithUs
Bill Maher on the genocide lie.
| 1:15 PM * Sep 12, 2026 * 955K Views237 Replies * 1.47K Reposts * 6.68K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/0662b2d2-ef1e-466e-b757-762793676d4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **What Maher said:** "I think Macklemore spoke for all clueless celebrities when he said, 'I know enough to know this is a genocide,'" Maher continued. "Actually, you don't know s--. It's not. It's not a genocide. It's a counterattack in a war."

* **Maher argued that mislabeling the conflict as genocide has fueled a global rise in antisemitism,** saying such rhetoric gives people "permission" to direct hatred at Jews.
* **PR expert Jason Mudd said Macklemore 's stance represents a "calculated risk" **that could alienate segments of his audience, noting the rapper -- recently dropped from Sheeran's tour lineup -- should weigh the career and reputational consequences of taking such a polarizing public position.

# **Kirk family files legal claim against Utah Valley University over security failures**
Charlie Kirk's family**[filed a notice of claim against Utah Valley University,](https://substack.com/redirect/b7517980-f2be-422b-9285-689cbe157cc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** alleging foreknowledge of security failures, including denying a request for additional officers and failing to secure rooftop access, which led to his assassination during a campus speaking event last September.

---](https://substack.com/redirect/8be5a9ec-1a72-4e03-830a-833023a23fe4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The filing claims TPUSA had warned campus police about rooftop access near the shooting location** and was told it would be handled, yet the Losee Center roof, where the alleged shooter fired from, remained unsecured despite known student access to the area.
* **Attorneys argue the university created a "foreseeable danger"** by holding the event outdoors surrounded by elevated buildings, understaffing security relative to the roughly 3,000 attendees, and failing to monitor security cameras in real time -- factors they say directly contributed to Kirk's death.

Rep. Brandon Gill **[shut down reporter Natasha Del Toro,](https://substack.com/redirect/e55af1c8-8614-47ce-95a6-3c3d65b0494d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** who identified herself only as working for "Fault Lines," to disclose her employer after she questioned him about deaths in ICE custody; after roughly 30 seconds of repeated questioning and refusal to identify which outlet she worked for, she confirmed her program airs on Al Jazeera English.

Future Oversight Committee Chairman Brandon Gill absolutely cooks an Al Jazeera reporter: "You guys can get lost."
| 8:20 PM * Sep 15, 2026 * 662K Views439 Replies * 1.25K Reposts * 11.9K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/e55af1c8-8614-47ce-95a6-3c3d65b0494d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Gill told the reporter to "get lost"** once she revealed the affiliation, accusing her of trying to obscure it.
* **The exchange came the same day Gill announced his bid to chair the House Oversight Committee,** a move that would significantly expand the 32-year-old freshman congressman's influence within the GOP.

Piddington, a small Oxfordshire village, **[voted overwhelmingly](https://substack.com/redirect/df0cdc40-936f-423d-b850-7ce0a7651583?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (285-26, with 92% turnout) in a symbolic, legally nonbinding referendum to declare itself an independent "Principality" in protest of government plans to convert a nearby former army base into an asylum center housing up to 3,500 migrants.

In good hands

| Peter,
Throughout my life, my hands have done a lot of different things!
---
[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)
---
They comforted hearts and healed wounds when I was a Nurse Practitioner.
---
[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.-5iwusjqbHlQ)
---
They flew helicopters to protect our freedom when I served in the Navy.
---
[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.-1-kVkH7s7nHwWNuapPRw)
---
They packed lunches, held hands, and instilled our values as a Mom to my four kids.
---
[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)
---

| Hi friends,Kelly and I are back on the road and have had some great talks with folks about energy, agriculture, commercial air service, leadership, and the issues facing our communities.We were moved by how many groups across Wyoming took time last week to remember September 11. Twenty-five years later, we remember those we lost, those who answered the call to serve, and the importance of coming together as Americans.We received good news for Wyoming energy with the EPA’s action to roll back federal greenhouse gas regulations on power plants. Regulatory whiplash has consequences here in Wyoming, and our energy industries and the people who work in them deserve to have certainty about the future. Wyoming knows well how to responsibly develop our resources and provide reliable, affordable energy - we've been doing it for generations.We’re taking that same get-to-work approach with the Healthcare Strike Team. People across Wyoming are sharing what is working, what isn’t, and where we can make a difference. Last week I spoke at the Wyoming Hospital Association Annual Meeting and was able to provide some early insights from responses to our survey. If you haven’t signed up or shared your thoughts yet, I hope you will. We need Wyoming people at the table as we work toward practical solutions. Learn more by clicking [here](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M2NB044JRWW4P6P9QNK9599V_1).And we are still campaigning. Kelly and I are back out on the road, attending events and meet-and-greets, and talking with folks as we work toward November. We’ll keep showing up, listening, and doing the work.Thanks for following along. And if you have a friend or neighbor who might want to follow along too, please forward them this newsletter and invite them to join us.Riding for Wyoming,Eric

#

Look -- we get it.
You probably didn’t wake up today thinking you’d make a donation to help end the gun violence crisis in our country. But give us just one minute to make the case for why your donation to GIFFORDS is so important — especially right now.
It has to do with one thing: The U.S. Postal Service.
**As we write this, the Trump Administration is trying to change the rules to let the USPS deliver guns directly to your mailbox — with no extra background checks, licensing, or training. We need your help to speak out.**
Since 1927, the United States Postal Service has been barred from carrying or delivering handguns as mail — with exceptions for members of the military, law enforcement, or licensed gun manufacturers or dealers.
Donald Trump is pushing to change that. Earlier this year, his Department of Justice issued a memo saying that they would no longer enforce this ban. Now, the USPS is proposing a change to their existing regulations...which could drop any day.
If this rule goes into effect, it would mean people who shouldn’t have a gun will be able to go around state and federal laws and get a gun mailed to them.
This change also means that gun traffickers have a new way to move firearms through America’s communities. At a time when gun violence is the #1 killer of kids and teenagers in our country, this rule would make us all less safe.
Friends, you have helped us so much fighting back against extremist legislation and passing gun safety laws. Now, we need your support again to push back on this proposed rule.
[**Please, will you donate $3 to help GIFFORDS PAC today? Our average online donation is around $27. Some give more, others give less. What matters most is that you are taking action today in the fight to make our communities safer.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260916-1-b&t=1&akid=11821%2E3935704%2EzwFaDy)

We need your help to speak out. Since 1927, the United States Postal Service has been barred from carrying or delivering handguns as mail — with exceptions for members of the military, law enforcement, or licensed gun manufacturers or dealers. Donald Trump is pushing to change that. Earlier this year, his Department of Justice issued a memo saying that they would no longer enforce this ban. Now, the USPS is proposing a change to their existing regulations...which could drop any day. If this rule goes into effect, it would mean people who shouldn’t have a gun will be able to go around state and federal laws and get a gun mailed to them. This change also means that gun traffickers have a new way to move firearms through America’s communities. At a time when gun violence is the #1 killer of kids and teenagers in our country, this rule would make us all less safe.
