**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
** September 16, 2026**Posterboy for Corruption Greg Landsman Hid $1.5 Million in Stocks While Posing as Ethics Crusader****CINCINNATI, OH** — [A new report](https://us.list-manage.com/SzbTfa8_S_i?e=3f87e575ad&c2id=83ae238fa0f76420f201b2501cd8e566) from Washington Free Beacon revealed that Greg Landsman failed to disclose up to $1.5 million in stock holdings during his first run for Congress and did not correct the record until nearly three years later. Per the report, when Landsman first ran for Congress in 2022, he reported just six stock holdings worth between $90,000 and $300,000. His amended disclosure, filed almost three years after the original, shows he actually held 54 stock positions worth as much as $1.5 million, generating stock income at least 18 times higher than originally disclosed. His net worth rose to as much as $3.5 million, tripling what it was before he entered office less than 4 years ago.This is not the first time Landsman’s financial hypocrisy has been exposed. In 2024, Landsman was busted for failing to report more than 87 stock transactions within the legally required window, violating the STOCK Act. The report comes on the heels of Landsman’s recent TV ad on ‘[fighting corruption](https://us.list-manage.com/dLK4jJkBird?e=3f87e575ad&c2id=83ae238fa0f76420f201b2501cd8e566)’ where he says, “No member of Congress should trade stocks. So I led by example and got rid of my stocks” _“The hypocrisy and arrogance of Greg Landsman know no bounds. He has run his campaign talking about stopping corruption and claiming he is leading the charge to end congressional stock trading, while covering up his own stock trading and_[ _voting against legislation to stop the corrupt practice_](https://us.list-manage.com/Tiinv89ewh4?e=3f87e575ad&c2id=83ae238fa0f76420f201b2501cd8e566) _. Landsman promises that he will clean up Washington, but in less than 4 years in Washington, he has become a corrupt politician entrenched in the swamp,”_**Conroy said.**_**** “When you run ads blatantly lying to voters, it shows not only dishonesty but total contempt for the people you represent. This district and its voters deserve a representative who’s honest with them, not one who lies to them while lining his own pockets.”_
**###**

body:
#
Billionaire stadium owner, Robert Kraft, did not like Macklemore, a Grammy winning rapper, saying “Free Palestine” on stage — so he made calls and the artist got pulled off of Ed Sheeran’s tour.
This is not just about a single musical act. This is about how a small handful of powerful people, like stadium owners, can threaten someone’s livelihood in order to prevent an entire massive issue from being spoken about — in this case, the genocide in Gaza.
But it doesn’t stop there.
Oligarchs and billionaires could just as easily prevent people from speaking out about AI, workers’ rights, or any issue they don’t like. That is what makes this a dangerous precedent. This moment is a test of how far the very powerful can go in censoring speech.
And that’s why it’s important that we speak out about it. That we make clear that this is an abuse of power. And that we keep the focus on Robert Kraft and the way he’s using his influence to try to control what can and cannot be talked about in America.
I am going to fight to ensure freedom of speech — guaranteed to us in the First Amendment — is protected from oligarchs and billionaires who want to silence any form of dissent or peaceful protest.
In solidarity,
Alexandria
**One last thing before you go...**
Alexandria will always speak out and fight against the billionaires who are trying to control our democracy. But she can’t do this work all on her own, she needs a movement alongside her.

name: Christina (personal)
subject: Sick happens
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CHRISTINA BOHANNAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
| Peter, sometimes, sick happens.

You can work hard, take care of your family, follow the rules — you can do everything right, and you and your family could still be at the mercy of anything from a cold to a life-threatening disease or accident.

When I was in high school, my dad got sick with emphysema. Almost overnight, the strong dad I knew — the man who spent his days on construction sites, showed me how to shoot a gun and drive a tractor, and always taught me the value of hard work — was suddenly fighting for his life. His health insurance was canceled just when he needed it most, and my family was forced to make impossible choices between paying for his medicine or paying for everything else.

Sadly, I know that's a grief so many Iowans are familiar with. It's devastating to be consumed with worry about the person you love while simultaneously dreading what their next trip to the doctor, prescription, or hospital bill will mean for your family. And it doesn't have to be a life-threatening illness. A broken bone on the playground, a bad bout of the flu, or complications during pregnancy can be enough to upend a family's finances and shatter its sense of security.

I believe that when we face the challenges of life, we should be able to afford to go to the doctor or hospital. But Mariannette Miller-Meeks has made that so much harder – by voting to cut funding to rural hospitals, kick hundreds of thousands of Iowans off Medicaid, and double or triple Iowans’ insurance premiums.

**I'm running to make sure families don't have to live with the kind of fear mine did and to protect the care that so many people rely on every day.

If we're going to bring true, lasting change to our district, we all need to be in this together. That starts with chipping in to my campaign to ensure we have the resources to defeat Miller-Meeks this November. clean_body: | Peter, sometimes, sick happens. You can work hard, take care of your family, follow the rules — you can do everything right, and you and your family could still be at the mercy of anything from a cold to a life-threatening disease or accident. When I was in high school, my dad got sick with emphysema. Almost overnight, the strong dad I knew — the man who spent his days on construction sites, showed me how to shoot a gun and drive a tractor, and always taught me the value of hard work — was suddenly fighting for his life. His health insurance was canceled just when he needed it most, and my family was forced to make impossible choices between paying for his medicine or paying for everything else. Sadly, I know that's a grief so many Iowans are familiar with. It's devastating to be consumed with worry about the person you love while simultaneously dreading what their next trip to the doctor, prescription, or hospital bill will mean for your family. And it doesn't have to be a life-threatening illness. A broken bone on the playground, a bad bout of the flu, or complications during pregnancy can be enough to upend a family's finances and shatter its sense of security. I believe that when we face the challenges of life, we should be able to afford to go to the doctor or hospital. But Mariannette Miller-Meeks has made that so much harder – by voting to cut funding to rural hospitals, kick hundreds of thousands of Iowans off Medicaid, and double or triple Iowans’ insurance premiums. I'm running to make sure families don't have to live with the kind of fear mine did and to protect the care that so many people rely on every day. If we're going to bring true, lasting change to our district, we all need to be in this together. That starts with chipping in to my campaign to ensure we have the resources to defeat Miller-Meeks this November. NATIONAL [West Point Taxes Raised to Fund School Bureaucracy](https://us.list-manage.com/eLKnZLNCTAI?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) West Point board approves school tax levy increase to cover budget shortfall [Continue reading →](https://us.list-manage.com/qqOfuKeoTFJ?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) [Moss Point Board Adopts FY2027 Budget, Trims Millage Rate](https://us.list-manage.com/njG55ZzgNa0?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) The Moss Point Board of Aldermen unanimously adopted a Fiscal Year 2027 budget and a companion tax levy resolution during a special called public hearing Sept. 9, 2026.[Read →](https://us.list-manage.com/8DeFWfRaLMD?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) [Massive Property Tax Hike on Seniors](https://us.list-manage.com/9FFKojhpRR6?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) Oktibbeha property values rise 24.9% after reassessment[Read →](https://us.list-manage.com/kEUdyMqQAl7?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) [Hitachi Energy to invest $528 million in Copiah County transformer plant, adding 654 jobs](https://us.list-manage.com/3WlINJPJt15?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) Another day, another half a billion investment announced.[Read →](https://us.list-manage.com/13oRME1uZII?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) | Explore Mississippi In Depth
---
[ Tax Dollars -> See how Mississippi spends every dollar you send to Jackson.](https://us.list-manage.com/Ml7m3L0A7eL?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)[ Schools -> How does your local school really measure up?](https://us.list-manage.com/PaDBcKNTeCh?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)[ Mississippi Wins -> The wins putting Mississippi ahead of the pack.](https://us.list-manage.com/13BwnCZKTEz?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)[ Energy -> What's really driving the cost of your energy.](https://us.list-manage.com/11AFIq1ylPY?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)

Around Mississippi [Jackson sales tax commission hears paving dispute, bridge-design delay and $4 million Woodrow Wilson plan](https://us.list-manage.com/IN5hOWLUAPB?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) JACKSON -- [Jackson parking meter contract has brought in no revenue this year; official says it could be ended but warns of litigation](https://us.list-manage.com/3UkKslFdSG9?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) JACKSON -- At a Sept. 10 budget hearing, Jackson's chief administrative officer told the City Council the city's parking meter contract could be nullified but that doing so carries a risk of litigation, after a councilman questioned why the contract shows zero revenue for the fiscal year. [Local School District Failing Special Needs Kids](https://us.list-manage.com/kuqn02YUA0X?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) COLUMBUS -- The Columbus Municipal School District is operating under two active state corrective action plans after a Mississippi Department of Education monitoring visit found widespread noncompliance in its special-education program, the district's special programs director told the school board Monday. [Taxpayer Money Used to End Bus Walkout](https://us.list-manage.com/FJwCAdCji2z?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) JACKSON -- State Capital Faces Budget Crunch Uses Money for "Strike Support" [Jackson council opens FY2027 budget talks on $337M plan as councilwoman challenges revenue math and CFO says city still owed up to $9M on water arrangement](https://us.list-manage.com/YxbdP7d7ADJ?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) JACKSON -- The Jackson City Council began formal deliberations Sept. 10 on a roughly $337 million FY2027 budget, with debate centered on the $113.5 million general fund; a councilwoman pressed finance staff for actual rather than forecast tax collections, and the city's CFO said $7 million to $9 million is still outstanding from before the water system's new payment schedule. [Greenwood Leflore school board approves $38.5 million high school contract](https://us.list-manage.com/1Bqdj2npZqA?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) GREENWOOD -- The Greenwood Leflore Consolidated School District Board of Trustees voted at a special call meeting September 9, 2026, to approve a $38,530,828 construction contract with Thrash Commercial Contractors for the district's new high school. [Brookhaven Police Department receives $118,000 in grants for equipment upgrades](https://us.list-manage.com/Dnz_trUH2nk?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) BROOKHAVEN -- The department has secured two grants totaling $118,000 for e-citation technology, radios and badges, though a local matching share still must be confirmed. [New Police Force Budget Approved](https://us.list-manage.com/XMSuKtspFlJ?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3) DIAMOND HEAD -- Diamond Head budgets $1.5 million for new municipal police department

We are now officially less than **one month** away from the start of early voting in North Carolina!
We are entering the final stretch of the campaign, and our team isn't slowing down. We're going to continue talking with North Carolinians in every corner of the state about the issues that matter to them. And it also means we need to make sure that every voter also has a plan to cast their ballot.
We are getting closer and closer to a phase of the campaign referred to as GOTV: **Get Out The Vote**. It's where months of conversations about the stakes of this race and the importance of flipping this seat blue turn into votes.
Our team is knocking doors, making calls and showing up in communities across the state to make sure every voter has a plan and knows exactly what their options to vote are this November.
If you're in North Carolina -- you can find an early voting polling location and hours [here](https://substack.com/redirect/fa6b8885-d105-4657-9043-8a04d2a68179?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Even if you're not registered yet, you can do it during early voting on the same day you vote.
And if you want to make sure we can keep talking with voters and helping them make a plan to vote through Election Day, **[I hope you consider chipping in $5, or whatever you can, to help us finish out this campaign strong.](https://substack.com/redirect/7eb446dd-06c9-4b42-b563-cb785cddcd3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Early voting starts in 29 days. Election Day is in 48 days.
Let's go!

P.S. Did you know that yesterday was also National Voter Registration day? If you have a minute, here's some quick voter information:

* Learn how to register to vote [HERE](https://substack.com/redirect/8ccc8660-7e9c-43dd-8263-ae6df6540db4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Want to register by mail? Fill out the [form](https://substack.com/redirect/0f9db0d5-278c-4f41-a9c1-7eacd6eaddea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), download and then mail it out.

body:
This is a critical moment for public lands

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/69Z2RwYOKLqJnlUMB5wBiQ~~/AAUS1hA~/o2jUp5fAcYPSx3qZhlxsWQ5IgpEhCX1Sm1d_D5vNrLIoOLwk0OjNyyfppIy5hElkZD9EASvRlhXGLrpGK6aIfNHIa-OaJmPba1HYPc2gBUarzi0PTnhAQZpcJxfUO8Rz)
| | | | Peter, In central Montana, along the Middle Fork of the Judith River, it got so bad that side-by-sides and off-highway vehicles (OHVs) were crossing the water in 27 different spots. The sediment runoff from the tires was so severe that it literally choked out the native cutthroat trout. The fish population collapsed by 90%. It took years of hard work from a coalition of anglers, state agencies, and responsible OHV riders to rebuild the riverbanks, designate appropriate motorized trails, and bring the fish back. But the politicians in Washington just decided that collaborative conservation isn't profitable enough for their corporate donors. **So they are preparing to unleash a massive, unregulated free-for-all across our national forests.** For decades, the rule for motorized vehicles on federal land has been simple and effective: trails are "closed unless designated open." If a trail is meant for side-by-sides, it is clearly marked. Otherwise, it is reserved for hikers, anglers, and wildlife. Now, the administration is officially proposing to flip that rule completely upside down. They want to make every single trail, riverbed, and backcountry acre "open unless designated closed." They are essentially declaring that anyone can drive a dirt bike or a four-wheeler up any hiking trail, into any sensitive creek, and across any fragile ecosystem unless an understaffed federal agency somehow manages to physically post and maintain a closure sign. [**This is a critical moment for us to fight back. Will you pitch in $10 today to our rapid-response war chest to help us stop this free-for-all before the damage is permanent?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/7K0kVXzCqi_P9UxZADuI1Q~~/AAUS1hA~/I6Q8uyNXGFeegtYkz6EgWNX6SHorQXnX77YHNTwFngSOFPhpRoLffjRpTsjEfPpewJae_DEdq92BcPNWPRrPG1U2ReQOVSN09pkhkP2tRFAR6Rug0h58SVlHoERAvjV8FtKPH2qDIglNwTNN2nm-D1inR1c-UyAKS32pjYQwrxenhtDpmnP1vVbR5Cya-2ARWRZPOaqz7qtIllDwVtjfbmapHYc-LNCZytAlCEbfBgs8bRgg_XefKI8dFm9GQLN3) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/klkK_JYXS7EyfcrxjDTTlg~~/AAUS1hA~/el6akulE_5ToJAKXQ0XMuDNfBcadt3AUDWyILhjq8pDPUYP3N0LjhVnGVvqENUDlJYU7fgmjStiJypGycz7QJwuDTLJ7cNj5TyyMp3fFuIrKReXTyG39ccQojsSin6rhRXKsSNFem3CX0zKBIzMtvBacTwc_W-tmKBRYUysTyIODwv_9697AlBribGmY_jD-7pD-TuKIO5W051YTQRA03Mdjxe1tUDWBqZaIYeEJmdx7tchWpNgIeWUiSPPfPHw5) ** They are doing this right on the heels of their proposal to repeal the Roadless Rule, which would strip protections from 45 million acres of untouched wilderness just to appease the timber lobby. The politicians rubber-stamping these rollbacks think they can rewrite the rules and turn our wild spaces into an unregulated industrial playground without any political consequences. They are betting that the American public is too exhausted to fight back before the public comment deadlines hit in a matter of weeks. **We are going to prove them wrong.** At Public Land Warriors, we are launching a targeted, inescapable digital ad blitz to ensure that every hunter, angler, and hiker knows exactly which politicians are trying to open our pristine trout streams and backcountry trails to unchecked destruction. We are going to make this corporate land-grab a massive electoral liability with less than two months until Election Day. [**Will you chip in $10, $25, or $50 today to help us fund the backlash and hold them accountable at the ballot box?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/klkK_JYXS7EyfcrxjDTTlg~~/AAUS1hA~/el6akulE_5ToJAKXQ0XMuDNfBcadt3AUDWyILhjq8pDPUYP3N0LjhVnGVvqENUDlJYU7fgmjStiJypGycz7QJwuDTLJ7cNj5TyyMp3fFuIrKReXTyG39ccQojsSin6rhRXKsSNFem3CX0zKBIzMtvBacTwc_W-tmKBRYUysTyIODwv_9697AlBribGmY_jD-7pD-TuKIO5W051YTQRA03Mdjxe1tUDWBqZaIYeEJmdx7tchWpNgIeWUiSPPfPHw5) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/klkK_JYXS7EyfcrxjDTTlg~~/AAUS1hA~/el6akulE_5ToJAKXQ0XMuDNfBcadt3AUDWyILhjq8pDPUYP3N0LjhVnGVvqENUDlJYU7fgmjStiJypGycz7QJwuDTLJ7cNj5TyyMp3fFuIrKReXTyG39ccQojsSin6rhRXKsSNFem3CX0zKBIzMtvBacTwc_W-tmKBRYUysTyIODwv_9697AlBribGmY_jD-7pD-TuKIO5W051YTQRA03Mdjxe1tUDWBqZaIYeEJmdx7tchWpNgIeWUiSPPfPHw5) ** They think they can quietly hand the keys to our forests over to the highest bidder. Palestinian-American journalist Naqaa Hamed. Courtesy: Hamed's family.
RAMALLAH, Occupied West Bank--Palestinian-American journalist and Drop Site News contributor Naqaa Hamed was arrested by Israeli authorities at a checkpoint on Tuesday as she was returning from a reporting assignment in the occupied West Bank, according to her colleagues and family. She spent the night in Israeli custody and is being interrogated about her journalistic work, a lawyer who spoke to Hamed on the phone told the family.
Hamed, 38, was detained near the village of Tuqu in Bethlehem as she and two other Palestinian journalists reporting for Turkish news outlet TRT were driving back from the southern West Bank after working on a report about escalating Israeli settler attacks in Masafer Yatta.
"It was three female soldiers who ushered our car to stop," Wisam Karam, a cameraperson on assignment for TRT who was in the car with Hamed, told Drop Site. "They demanded we hand over our identification cards and they photographed each ID as well as took our pictures." After a short while, the soldiers ordered the team to get out of the car and follow them to a military watchtower nearby. "We were forced to sit on the ground for around 45 minutes, and in that time Naqaa was taken by the female soldiers to the side," Karam said. When she was returned to join her colleagues on the ground, Hamed said she was questioned about her work and what stories she was working on, according to Karam. Around 15 minutes later, the soldiers asked Hamed to collect her phone and laptop and she was taken into custody. Karam and the other journalists working with them were released and told to leave the area; soldiers refused to provide any additional information on Hamed.
Hamed is a freelance journalist who has worked for various international outlets, including Drop Site News (read her reports on Israeli settler attacks and expanding settlements in the West Bank [here](https://substack.com/redirect/f82aae40-9d66-44de-bfed-912456dd4e75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [here](https://substack.com/redirect/bb745958-471e-4638-a207-630625f920c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). Over the past several weeks, Israeli settlers have targeted Hamed with a wave of incitement on Telegram channels and in Hebrew media following her coverage of an Israeli siege on families in the village of Qusra, according to her colleagues. Hamed is from the village of Beitin, northeast of Ramallah, holds American citizenship, and is married with three young children. Hamed's family contacted the U.S. embassy in Jerusalem about her arrest but has yet to hear back.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2d2efcda-12a1-48ff-9f91-d55209a91ec3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Palestinian-American journalist Naqaa Hamed. September 11, 2025. Courtesy: Hamed's family.
Israeli news outlet Ynet [cited](https://substack.com/redirect/38fcb4aa-95d0-4f30-b19d-399add6236ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) unidentified Israeli military sources as saying Hamed is "suspected of cooperating with an enemy entity and may also be under suspicion of espionage." The Israeli military spokesperson declined to comment when asked by Drop Site about her case and instead deferred questions to the Israeli police.
Hamed's detention is part of an escalating wave of arrests of Palestinian journalists by Israeli authorities. Nearly 40 journalists are currently in Israeli detention, according to the Palestinian Prisoners Society (PPS), all of whom were arrested since the start of Israel's genocidal assault on Gaza nearly three years ago. Over half the journalists behind bars are being held in administrative detention, a mechanism that allows Israeli authorities to imprison people indefinitely without charge or trial.
Last month, Israeli forces [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/6bbf4578-e28c-4cfb-b99f-b20f81c65ceb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinian journalist and Drop Site contributor Mohamed Awad, 38, from his home in Bitunia, blindfolding and handcuffing him before taking him into custody. He was later sentenced to three months in administrative detention.
"The targeting of Palestinian journalists is part of a systematic policy aimed at erasing the truth and suppressing the Palestinian narrative," PPS said in a statement.

You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me.
I thought so too, _until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the _**next few days.**__

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
Election Day is less than 50 days away, and these are the places that can benefit most from financial support right now.
#
Hi there,
There are fewer than 50 days left until Election Day. This is when campaigns are in make-or-break mode. And with so much noise out there about hundreds of candidates, it can be hard to understand where your dollars and time can make the biggest difference in winning back Congress and key state legislatures to swing the national balance of power.
**Which is why we’re excited to announce that the[Immediate Impact Fund is back.](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&refcode=em20260916-2792&t=1&akid=2792%2E1562180%2EVdch21)**
[****](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&refcode=em20260916-2792&t=2&akid=2792%2E1562180%2EVdch21)
**If you want to have an instant impact on the closest races this year, the Immediate Impact Fund is the place to give.** Your donation will go directly to the Democratic candidates, state parties, and caucus committees that will benefit most from an infusion of cash, right now.
We first introduced the Immediate Impact Fund during the 2018 midterm elections, and every cycle since, it has been one of the key ways that this community has helped Democrats beat Republicans to win majority-making swing seats.
The Immediate Impact Fund is informed by Swing Left’s political team, which is in daily conversations with campaigns for House, Senate, and governors’ races, as well as Democratic State Parties and downballot races. They chose these races based on rigorous analysis, including the latest polling data, fundraising reports, and direct conversations with campaigns about what they need revenue for right now.
As we move closer to November 3rd, our team will continuously monitor spending, polling, and campaign field reports. Each Wednesday, as races shift, the Swing Left political team will share an update straight to your inbox on the Immediate Impact Fund with a refreshed slate of candidates and entities where your dollars will go furthest.
This week, the Immediate Impact Fund includes a dozen campaigns and entities, including six must-win U.S. House races like **Arizona's 2nd**. Polls show that former Navajo Nation President Jonathan Nez is in a neck-and-neck race with his Republican incumbent opponent in a massive, rural district. Indigenous voters are the key to victory for Nez, but they face unique barriers to voting on the Navajo reservation, where voters must travel long distances to vote with limited transportation, lack Internet access, have spotty mail service, and other obstacles. As a result, the campaign needs enormous resources to reach and mobilize voters.
It also includes two must-flip Senate races—one of which is **Iowa, where Democratic candidate Josh Turek’s** opponent ended the quarter with nearly three times as much cash, making immediate grassroots funding vital so he has the resources to talk to voters in every corner of the state.
**When you give to the Immediate Impact Fund today, you give these frontline campaigns, state parties, and caucus committees the funds they need to stay competitive in the lead-up to the midterms.**
**[If you want to make a difference in the races and places that need support the most right now, donate to the Immediate Impact Fund today. Your contribution will go directly to the 12 races, caucus committees, and state parties in our initial slate.](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&refcode=em20260916-2792&t=3&akid=2792%2E1562180%2EVdch21)**
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&refcode=em20260916-2792&t=4&akid=2792%2E1562180%2EVdch21)**
Thank you for supporting these critical races–we’ll be in touch with more soon.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260916-1&t=5&refcode2=2792_1562180_Vdch21&akid=2792%2E1562180%2EVdch21)

Meet Donald
Trump’s latest crony nominee: Courtney Coker.

Like all of Trump’s judicial nominees, Coker isn’t up for a lifetime seat
on the bench because of his qualifications. He’s up for it to be another
rubber stamp for Trump’s agenda.

In a scathing letter to the Senate Judiciary Committee, Alliance for
Justice warned that Coker has “weaponized the full force of the federal
government to inflict lasting harm on immigrants, workers, and communities
of color.”

His record is horrific. Coker helped plan the 2019 Mississippi ICE raids —
detaining nearly 680 workers on the first day of school and leaving
children to come back to empty homes. He also pushed Project EJECT, a
discriminatory program targeting majority-Black neighborhoods in Jackson
with harsh federal sentencing.^1

As if that wasn’t bad enough, his Senate questionnaire tells the whole
story: zero legal writings, zero policy speeches, and zero basic legal
qualifications. This is a lifetime appointment — and he hasn't done the
work to earn a single day of it.

But Trump doesn’t care about qualifications. He cares about whether his
people are loyal to him instead of the law, and he’s not going to stop
unless we do something about it.

At Demand Justice PAC, we’re building the movement to expose these
extremist nominees, pressure the Senate to hold them accountable, and
restore balance and independence in our judiciary.

In a scathing letter to the Senate Judiciary Committee, Alliance for Justice warned that Coker has “weaponized the full force of the federal government to inflict lasting harm on immigrants, workers, and communities of color.” His record is horrific. Coker helped plan the 2019 Mississippi ICE raids — detaining nearly 680 workers on the first day of school and leaving children to come back to empty homes. He also pushed Project EJECT, a discriminatory program targeting majority-Black neighborhoods in Jackson with harsh federal sentencing.^1 As if that wasn’t bad enough, his Senate questionnaire tells the whole story: zero legal writings, zero policy speeches, and zero basic legal qualifications. This is a lifetime appointment — and he hasn't done the work to earn a single day of it. But Trump doesn’t care about qualifications. He cares about whether his people are loyal to him instead of the law, and he’s not going to stop unless we do something about it. At Demand Justice PAC, we’re building the movement to expose these extremist nominees, pressure the Senate to hold them accountable, and restore balance and independence in our judiciary. [ ]We can’t let nominees like Coker fly through confirmation without a fight — will you chip in $5 to power Demand Justice PAC’s movement to protect our courts? [**Will you add your name now and tell Congress to protect access to medication abortion before the courts take it away?**](https://us.list-manage.com/7W1dM_ogpSb?e=a7b299e420&c2id=1b040b68f1d062d0c966c24dae99fcb4)

---
| | This comes on the heels of new reporting that deaths involving ectopic pregnancies have nearly doubled nationally since the U.S. Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade. The increase has been even steeper in states with severe restrictions, where fear and confusion around those laws have contributed to dangerous delays in care.

**If you think Washington is insulated from these bans, you’re wrong.

** Idaho has lost more than a third of the doctors who practiced obstetrics since its near-total ban took effect. Labor and delivery units have closed, leaving some Gem State families hours from care, and pushing more patients across the border to Eastern Washington communities.

Getting medication by mail matters most when the nearest provider is hours away. Banning it would force patients to take time off from work, drive for hours in all sorts of weather, and place even more pressure on struggling rural hospitals.

We have seen that here at home where East Adams Rural Healthcare in Ritzville came within weeks of closing this year and is giving up inpatient care to survive. Newport Hospital is under strain from “charity care” patients from Idaho. **Rural hospitals like these cannot absorb a growing regional health care crisis alone.

** As the regional refugee coordinator in Afghanistan and Pakistan, I saw a vast divide between urban and rural care, especially for women and girls. I also saw that failing to maintain separation of Church and State resulted in harm to young women. I did not expect to come home and see it happening here.

**If the courts take away mail and pharmacy access, Congress must act. We need representatives who understand that reproductive freedom – and the survival of rural health care - are inseparable.****
Add your name and tell Congress to protect medication abortion access nationwide.**

Carmela

**Local Businesses and Community Organizations Endorse Morri Elliott for San Juan Unified School District Board**
---
| | **CARMICHAEL, CA** — Morri Elliott, candidate for the San Juan Unified School District Board of Education, Trustee Area 3, today announced the endorsements of the Sacramento Association of REALTORS, Slavic American Chamber of Commerce, Cal-Asian PAC and North State Building Industry Association. The endorsements reflect growing support from business and community organizations across the Sacramento region for Elliott’s focus on strong schools, career and college readiness, and preparing students for success after graduation.Elliott, a public school educator with more than 20 years of experience and a father of three, including two children attending San Juan Unified schools, is running to strengthen academic achievement, expand career and college pathways, and ensure students have access to the opportunities they need to succeed.“Strong schools are essential to creating thriving neighborhoods and vibrant communities,” said Judy Covington, Chair of the Local Candidate Recommendation Committee for the Sacramento Association of REALTORS. “Morri Elliott brings the experience, qualifications, and commitment needed to help San Juan Unified continue building on its success. His dedication to students and families makes him the right choice to serve Trustee Area 3.”Elliott said the support of local business and community organizations highlights the important connection between strong schools, a strong workforce, and healthy communities.“I’m grateful to earn the support of the Sacramento Association of REALTORS, Slavic American Chamber of Commerce, Cal-Asian PAC,” Elliott said. “As a father, coach, and educator, I am deeply invested in the future of our community. Our schools play a critical role in preparing young people for college, careers, and life, and I will be a strong advocate for academic excellence and expanded opportunities for every student.”The organizations join a growing coalition of community leaders, educators, public safety organizations, and elected officials supporting Elliott’s campaign for San Juan Unified School District Trustee Area 3.**About Morri Elliott:** Morri Elliott is a public school educator with more than 20 years of experience and a father of three, including two children attending San Juan Unified schools. He is running for the San Juan Unified School District Board of Education, Trustee Area 3, to bring real classroom experience, collaborative leadership, and a focus on expanding opportunities for all students.For more information, visit[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/eZ3mMpLd187?e=4bbfb0c664&c2id=80039a69d18906750dd60e2699be4374)[www.votemorri.com](https://us.list-manage.com/RVNbqXuw9u0?e=4bbfb0c664&c2id=80039a69d18906750dd60e2699be4374).

**Wednesday, September 16, 2026 -**_**** Saudi Arabia claims Ansarallah launched drone toward Mecca; group calls claim a "worn-out lie." Ansarallah says it struck Saudi Aramco in Yanbu, targeted Khamis Mushait airbase, and downed F-15 fighter jet. U.S. urges travelers to reconsider Saudi Arabia travel over missile and drone threat. Israeli forces demolish homes as settlers burn property, destroy water supplies across occupied West Bank. Trump administration approves $2.8 billion Israel arms package including 40,000 bombs. Israeli forces blow up homes, abduct man in southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire." Lebanon seeks new international force for south after UN peacekeepers leave. House again votes to end U.S. war in Iran. Aaron Guckian wins Republican nomination for governor of Rhode Island. U.S. says FBI prevented Russian plot to kill dissidents. Ed Sheeran's supporting acts quit tour after Macklemore removed over pro-Palestine remarks. EU proposes making Canada the bloc's first "associate member." India summons Pakistan's top diplomat after naval collision in Arabian Sea. At least 67 killed in collapse at gold mine in Sudan. Ukraine launches new offensive north of key Donetsk fortress belt. China warns U.S. deployment of weapons in orbit could fuel a space arms race._

* * *
# Yemen
* **Saudi Arabia claims Ansarallah launched drone toward Mecca; group calls claim a "worn-out lie": **Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Ansarallah south of Mecca at 6:50 p.m. Tuesday, before it entered the prohibited airspace around the city, Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said.
* Al-Maliki described it as the second attempted attack on Mecca, Islam's holiest city, citing a ballistic missile launch in July 2017.
* Ansarallah political bureau member Hizam Al-Assad rejected the Saudi account, calling the claim that the group targeted Mecca "a worn-out lie that has been used before."
* **Ansarallah says it struck Saudi Aramco in Yanbu, targeted Khamis Mushait airbase:** Yemen's Ansarallah [said](https://substack.com/redirect/231e88bc-e1aa-4aa5-ae51-01b56f87b005?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday that its forces launched dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu, claiming "direct and precise hits" that caused major fires and widespread destruction.
* In a second operation, the group said it targeted the Khamis Mushait airbase with several ballistic missiles.
* Earlier, Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet over Yemen's Marib governorate. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities.
* Ansarallah said the attacks were in response to more than 450 Saudi airstrikes across Yemen over the past week and vowed to continue operations "deep inside Saudi territory."
* **U.S. urges travelers to reconsider Saudi Arabia travel over missile and drone threat:** The U.S. State Department [placed](https://substack.com/redirect/795492a6-c85b-4371-aef5-43c2bfc10000?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Saudi Arabia under a Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" advisory on Wednesday, citing the threat of Iranian and Ansarallah missile and drone attacks.
* The Yemen border remains under the highest Level 4 "Do Not Travel" warning, while U.S. government employees face additional travel restrictions near the border and in Qatif, Jizan, Asir and Najran.
* **Ansarallah told U.S. it would limit attacks to Saudi ships, uphold ceasefire with Washington, Reuters reports:** U.S. officials [met](https://substack.com/redirect/f75df389-e0fa-4001-9b95-2b09e0bb4e0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) representatives of Yemen's Ansarallah at the U.S. Embassy in Muscat on Sunday, Reuters reported, citing sources familiar with the meeting. Oman reportedly helped organize the talks.
* According to Reuters, Ansarallah told U.S. officials it remained committed to the 2025 ceasefire and would not attack American or Israeli ships, or other commercial vessels, except those belonging to Saudi Arabia.
* The Trump administration designated Ansarallah a "foreign terrorist organization" in March 2025, but later negotiated a ceasefire with the group in May after two months of U.S. bombing.
* Senior Ansarallah official Mohammed Al-Bukhaiti had earlier rejected Trump administration claims of direct talks, telling Sky News that any communication with Washington is conducted through Oman.
* **U.S.-Ansarallah ceasefire remains intact despite Saudi-Yemen fighting, Huckabee says:** U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee [said](https://substack.com/redirect/95005ef2-6d95-4b2d-bfa2-f32b0a6baced?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the ceasefire between Washington and Yemen's Ansarallah remains in place despite the escalating fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen.
* "The U.S. and the Houthis still have a ceasefire. That's a good thing," Huckabee told Newsmax, adding that the fighting has "not really gone across the region."
* **U.S. approves potential $5 billion bomb sale to Saudi Arabia:** The Trump administration [notified](https://substack.com/redirect/3688831b-b715-499f-b824-94b8057290f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Congress of a proposed arms sale to Saudi Arabia that includes more than 10,000 2,000-pound and 500-pound bombs and 10,004 extended-range JDAM guidance kits, which convert unguided bombs into precision-guided weapons.
* Boeing would serve as the principal contractor for the proposed transfer, which comes amid renewed Saudi airstrikes in Yemen.
* It is not yet a finalized contract. Congress has a 30-day review period following the September 4 notification.

# Iran
* **Iran claims it downed 52nd US MQ-9 Reaper:** Iran's Revolutionary Guard [said](https://substack.com/redirect/4cf6906d-ee29-4836-92ce-c565a6468bba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it intercepted and destroyed another U.S. MQ-9 Reaper over Qeshm Island Wednesday morning, claiming it was the 52nd such drone downed.
* An MQ-9 costs roughly $30 million or more depending on its configuration and equipment. Reports have put the U.S. Air Force's operational MQ-9 inventory at around 135 aircraft after falling by more than 25%.
* **China says it is willing to "safeguard" Iran's rights amid mediation efforts: **Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said Beijing is willing to "safeguard Iran's legitimate rights and interests" during talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Beijing on Wednesday, as China seeks to mediate the Iran-U.S. war.
* "We urge Washington and Tehran to engage in substantive consultations on outstanding issues," Wang said, calling on both sides to rebuild a negotiating framework based on the consensus reached since the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. Both countries should "act rationally and with restraint," Wang added.
* The meeting comes a week before Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to travel to Washington for talks with U.S. President Donald Trump.
* **U.S. spent $33.4 billion on Iran war in first four months, Pentagon watchdog says:** The U.S. [spent](https://substack.com/redirect/f259172a-d63e-4596-a6fe-1fdf01e83e31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an estimated $33.4 billion on Operation Epic Fury through June 29, including $22.3 billion in expended munitions and $3.7 billion in equipment losses, according to a Pentagon Inspector General report to Congress.

* **U.S. diesel prices hit record high above $6.30 a gallon:** Average U.S. diesel prices [rose](https://substack.com/redirect/2212e5c9-d1c5-45a0-9cb3-ec9c0f3af864?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a record $6.31 per gallon on Wednesday, according to the American Automobile Association, surpassing Tuesday's record of $6.27 and the previous historic high of about $5.82 set in 2022.
* Diesel averaged below $3.50 a gallon at the start of last year but has surged alongside global oil prices.

# Other International News
* **EU proposes making Canada the bloc 's first "associate member":** European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said in a public statement the European Union would [pursue](https://substack.com/redirect/b85eba46-6c6e-43b8-8b35-c8e908d0f55b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) associate EU membership for Canada, as both sides seek closer economic and security ties amid worsening relations with the United States and growing competition with China.
* The status does not currently exist in EU law and its meaning remains undefined, but von der Leyen said cooperation could include defense-industrial integration, technology, manufacturing, critical raw materials, supply chains and the Arctic.
* Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has said Ottawa is seeking a "unique alliance" with Europe rather than full EU membership. More detailed discussions are expected at an EU-Canada summit in Montreal next month.
* **India summons Pakistan 's top diplomat after naval collision in Arabian Sea:** India [summoned](https://substack.com/redirect/1659d26a-c438-49b3-8ee1-665e67721c7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Pakistan's top diplomat after Pakistani naval units collided with an Indian naval vessel in international waters in the northern Arabian Sea on Tuesday.
* No major damage was reported, but New Delhi called the incident "unacceptable and unprofessional" and urged Pakistan to follow existing bilateral agreements meant to prevent dangerous military encounters.
* Pakistan has not yet publicly commented on the naval collision.
* **At least 67 killed in collapse at gold mine in Sudan:** At least 67 miners were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/5b37429a-2410-458f-b984-06a9986082d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after a series of adjoining shafts collapsed at the al-Zara gold mine in West Kordofan, with more than 70 people reported dead or missing and some miners potentially still trapped underground.
* Local monitoring groups said no specialized rescue teams had reached the remote site, leaving residents to dig with basic tools despite unstable sandy ground. A survivor who emerged two days after the collapse reportedly said others were still alive below ground.
* The Sudan Doctors Network, a medical group tracking the war in Sudan, provided the death toll and said it could increase as rescuers continued to search for people trapped under the rubble.
* **Ukraine launches new offensive north of key Donetsk fortress belt:** Ukrainian forces have begun a new [offensive](https://substack.com/redirect/8d54e264-a7e4-4400-b1fe-f588fce2e774?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) operation in northern Donetsk aimed at pushing Russian troops back from the core of Ukraine's remaining defensive line in the region.
* A senior Ukrainian commander claimed the operation had already cleared Russian infiltration groups from around 75 square kilometers, recaptured additional territory and restored control over several villages, though independent monitors have not been able to confirm these figures.
* **Bank of Japan set to raise rates to a 31-year high over inflation pressures:** The Bank of Japan is expected to [raise](https://substack.com/redirect/dabc3bf2-d6ff-4771-a903-1527733d4860?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its interest rate from 1% to 1.25% this week, the highest level since the mid-1990s, as Japan continues moving away from decades of ultra-low interest rates.
* The expected hike reflects persistent inflation pressures from high oil prices, a weak yen and rising import costs, and would follow tightening by other major central banks. The BOJ ended its long-running stimulus program in 2024 and has raised rates several times since.
* Officials are believed to see room for additional increases and the bank is trying to avoid either weakening the yen following pressures on energy prices from the Iran War.
* **China warns U.S. deployment of weapons in orbit could fuel a space arms race:** Beijing called on Washington to [halt](https://substack.com/redirect/8049ba97-663a-4a14-84f5-b0c786caa337?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its military buildup in space one day after U.S. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said the United States has "on-orbit space control weapons" capable of defending U.S. forces against hostile action.
* China's Foreign Ministry said in a statement that Beijing opposes the weaponization of space and warned that U.S. deployments could undermine strategic stability.
* The U.S. has long developed counter-space systems, but Meink's statement suggested the deployment of weapons directly in orbit rather than relying only on ground-based systems or defensive measures.
* **Former Philippines leaderDuterte appears at ICC ahead of crimes against humanity trial:** Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte [appeared](https://substack.com/redirect/8ec347e5-db83-4657-b201-e57d549559ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in person at the International Criminal Court in The Hague for the first time in more than a year, as judges prepared for the expected November start of his trial on charges of murder and attempted murder tied to his prosecution of a "war on drugs."
* Prosecutors allege Duterte was involved in dozens of killings carried out by police and government-linked death squads during his years as mayor of Davao and later as president. Duterte denies the charges.
* Duterte was arrested in the Philippines and transferred to The Hague in March 2025. His lawyers unsuccessfully sought to have the case halted on medical grounds and challenged the ICC's jurisdiction after the Philippines withdrew from the court in 2019.

Drop Site Daily: September 16, 2026 | | | Sep 16 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Gaza Civil Defense teams recover bodies from a collapsed building on September 16, 2026 in the Al-Sinaa area west of Gaza City, Gaza. Photo by Omar Ashtawy/Getty Images. Wednesday, September 16, 2026 -** Saudi Arabia claims Ansarallah launched drone toward Mecca; group calls claim a "worn-out lie." Ansarallah says it struck Saudi Aramco in Yanbu, targeted Khamis Mushait airbase, and downed F-15 fighter jet. U.S. urges travelers to reconsider Saudi Arabia travel over missile and drone threat. Ansarallah told U.S. it would limit attacks to Saudi ships, uphold ceasefire with Washington, Reuters reports. Iran claims it downed 52nd U.S. MQ-9 Reaper. U.S. spent $33.4 billion on Iran war in first four months, Pentagon watchdog says. U.S. diesel prices hit record high above $6.30 a gallon. Twenty-one Palestinians killed as Israeli-damaged building collapses in Gaza; dozens remain under rubble. Israeli attacks kill six Palestinians, including two children, in Gaza on Tuesday. Israeli forces demolish homes as settlers burn property, destroy water supplies across occupied West Bank. Trump administration approves $2.8 billion Israel arms package including 40,000 bombs. Israeli forces blow up homes, abduct man in southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire." Lebanon seeks new international force for south after UN peacekeepers leave. House again votes to end U.S. war in Iran. Aaron Guckian wins Republican nomination for governor of Rhode Island. U.S. says FBI prevented Russian plot to kill dissidents. Ed Sheeran's supporting acts quit tour after Macklemore removed over pro-Palestine remarks. EU proposes making Canada the bloc's first "associate member." India summons Pakistan's top diplomat after naval collision in Arabian Sea. At least 67 killed in collapse at gold mine in Sudan. Ukraine launches new offensive north of key Donetsk fortress belt. China warns U.S. deployment of weapons in orbit could fuel a space arms race. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Saudi Arabia claims Ansarallah launched drone toward Mecca; group calls claim a "worn-out lie": Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Ansarallah south of Mecca at 6:50 p.m. Tuesday, before it entered the prohibited airspace around the city, Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said. Al-Maliki described it as the second attempted attack on Mecca, Islam's holiest city, citing a ballistic missile launch in July 2017. Ansarallah political bureau member Hizam Al-Assad rejected the Saudi account, calling the claim that the group targeted Mecca "a worn-out lie that has been used before." Ansarallah says it struck Saudi Aramco in Yanbu, targeted Khamis Mushait airbase: Yemen's Ansarallah Wednesday that its forces launched dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu, claiming "direct and precise hits" that caused major fires and widespread destruction. In a second operation, the group said it targeted the Khamis Mushait airbase with several ballistic missiles. Earlier, Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet over Yemen's Marib governorate. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities. Ansarallah said the attacks were in response to more than 450 Saudi airstrikes across Yemen over the past week and vowed to continue operations "deep inside Saudi territory." U.S. urges travelers to reconsider Saudi Arabia travel over missile and drone threat: The U.S. State Department Saudi Arabia under a Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" advisory on Wednesday, citing the threat of Iranian and Ansarallah missile and drone attacks. The Yemen border remains under the highest Level 4 "Do Not Travel" warning, while U.S. government employees face additional travel restrictions near the border and in Qatif, Jizan, Asir and Najran. Ansarallah told U.S. it would limit attacks to Saudi ships, uphold ceasefire with Washington, Reuters reports: U.S. officials representatives of Yemen's Ansarallah at the U.S. Embassy in Muscat on Sunday, Reuters reported, citing sources familiar with the meeting. Oman reportedly helped organize the talks. According to Reuters, Ansarallah told U.S. officials it remained committed to the 2025 ceasefire and would not attack American or Israeli ships, or other commercial vessels, except those belonging to Saudi Arabia. The Trump administration designated Ansarallah a "foreign terrorist organization" in March 2025, but later negotiated a ceasefire with the group in May after two months of U.S. bombing. Senior Ansarallah official Mohammed Al-Bukhaiti had earlier rejected Trump administration claims of direct talks, telling Sky News that any communication with Washington is conducted through Oman. U.S.-Ansarallah ceasefire remains intact despite Saudi-Yemen fighting, Huckabee says: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee the ceasefire between Washington and Yemen's Ansarallah remains in place despite the escalating fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen. "The U.S. and the Houthis still have a ceasefire. That's a good thing," Huckabee told Newsmax, adding that the fighting has "not really gone across the region." U.S. approves potential $5 billion bomb sale to Saudi Arabia: The Trump administration Congress of a proposed arms sale to Saudi Arabia that includes more than 10,000 2,000-pound and 500-pound bombs and 10,004 extended-range JDAM guidance kits, which convert unguided bombs into precision-guided weapons. Boeing would serve as the principal contractor for the proposed transfer, which comes amid renewed Saudi airstrikes in Yemen. It is not yet a finalized contract. Congress has a 30-day review period following the September 4 notification. Iran Iran claims it downed 52nd US MQ-9 Reaper: Iran's Revolutionary Guard it intercepted and destroyed another U.S. MQ-9 Reaper over Qeshm Island Wednesday morning, claiming it was the 52nd such drone downed. An MQ-9 costs roughly $30 million or more depending on its configuration and equipment. Reports have put the U.S. Air Force's operational MQ-9 inventory at around 135 aircraft after falling by more than 25%. China says it is willing to "safeguard" Iran's rights amid mediation efforts: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said Beijing is willing to "safeguard Iran's legitimate rights and interests" during talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Beijing on Wednesday, as China seeks to mediate the Iran-U.S. war. "We urge Washington and Tehran to engage in substantive consultations on outstanding issues," Wang said, calling on both sides to rebuild a negotiating framework based on the consensus reached since the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. Both countries should "act rationally and with restraint," Wang added. The meeting comes a week before Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to travel to Washington for talks with U.S. President Donald Trump. U.S. spent $33.4 billion on Iran war in first four months, Pentagon watchdog says: The U.S. an estimated $33.4 billion on Operation Epic Fury through June 29, including $22.3 billion in expended munitions and $3.7 billion in equipment losses, according to a Pentagon Inspector General report to Congress. The figure does not include the cost of repairing U.S. military infrastructure damaged by Iranian strikes, which damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at American bases across eight countries. The report also says dozens of U.S. aircraft were damaged or destroyed. Separately, the Congressional Budget office estimated that the Iran war has cost more than $38 billion, projecting it to cost an additional $2 to $3 billion monthly. The budget office projected inflation will be 0.5 percentage points higher than expected heading into 2027 due to the war. U.S. diesel prices hit record high above $6.30 a gallon: Average U.S. diesel prices to a record $6.31 per gallon on Wednesday, according to the American Automobile Association, surpassing Tuesday's record of $6.27 and the previous historic high of about $5.82 set in 2022. Diesel averaged below $3.50 a gallon at the start of last year but has surged alongside global oil prices. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, six Palestinians were killed and 71 injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,795 killed, with 174,869 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,381 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,757, while 831 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Twenty-one Palestinians killed as Israeli-damaged building collapses in Gaza; dozens remain under the rubble: At least 21 Palestinians, including 12 children, were killed and 14 others injured after a residential building damaged by Israeli attacks and sheltering displaced families overnight in Gaza City, the Strip's Health Ministry told Drop Site. More than 100 people, including 50 children, are estimated to have been sheltering in the building, with rescuers struggling to reach survivors amid a severe shortage of specialized machinery due to Israeli restrictions. "We can still hear the voices of people alive beneath the rubble," Gaza's rescue chief said. Rescue crews warned that more than 2,000 damaged buildings across Gaza are at risk of collapse while still housing large numbers of displaced Palestinians. At least 50 people have been killed in collapses of buildings damaged during Israel's attacks on the Gaza Strip. Israel has refused to allow reconstruction materials into Gaza despite signing a ceasefire agreement nearly a year ago. Israeli attacks kill six Palestinians, including two children, in Gaza on Tuesday: Israeli forces a 15-year-old Palestinian boy and a Civil Defense paramedic in Gaza City's Sheikh Radwan neighborhood on Tuesday, according to Healthcare Workers Watch. The group said an Israeli drone first struck a man, then fired a second missile as the paramedic attempted to rescue the wounded person. shows the boy rushing to help the wounded paramedic when the second strike killed them both. In Khan Younis, Israeli forces three strikes on tents sheltering displaced families in Al-Mawasi, killing two Palestinians, including a child, and wounding 14 others. Israeli forces demolish homes as settlers burn property, destroy water supplies across occupied West Bank: Hebron: Israeli forces a two-story home south of Yatta housing eight people, most of them children, on Wednesday, WAFA reported. In Al-Tuwani, Masafer Yatta, armed settlers under Israeli military protection burned a home and agricultural room and spray-painted racist slogans. Israeli forces also closed the Ibrahimi Mosque to Palestinians until Thursday evening and imposed restrictions that halted classes at one nearby school and disrupted another. Jericho: Israeli forces five homes and a prayer space in Al-Jiftlik, north of Jericho. Ramallah: Settlers Palestinian land west of Ni'lin for a third day, digging and carving roads. Israeli forces also raided several homes and field-interrogated the deputy mayor and two municipal workers. Tubas: Settlers water lines, emptied a water well used by residents, and destroyed crops in northern Yarza. In Tammun, Israeli forces detained seven members of one family, including two children, and beat family members in an effort to pressure another son to surrender. Salfit: Israeli forces a pastoral community west of Deir Ballut, home to more than 20 Palestinians for over 20 years. " It was an execution": Israeli forces kill Palestinian man during West Bank home raid: Israeli forces shot and killed 54-year-old Ziad Jaber during a predawn raid on his family's home in Al-Bireh in the occupied West Bank on Tuesday. His brother Ramadan told Drop Site contributor Mutasem Sqf ElHait that soldiers blew open the family's door and, about a minute later, he heard Ziad scream. The family was prevented from reaching him for around an hour and a half. "The only thing we saw was the blood," Ramadan said. The Palestinian Prisoners' Society said Jaber was struck by two bullets in a "field execution." Watch the dispatch from Sqf ElHait . Journalist Naqaa Hamed arrested by Israel: Palestinian-American journalist and Drop Site News contributor Naqaa Hamed was arrested by Israeli authorities at a checkpoint on Tuesday as she was returning from a reporting assignment in the occupied West Bank for Turkish broadcaster TRT, according to her colleagues and family. She spent the night in Israeli custody and is being interrogated about her journalistic work, a lawyer who spoke to Hamed on the phone told the family. Over the past several weeks, Israeli settlers have targeted Hamed with a wave of incitement on Telegram channels and in Hebrew media following her coverage of an Israeli siege on families in the village of Qusra, according to her colleagues. Hamed is from the village of Beitin, northeast of Ramallah, holds American citizenship, and is married with three young children. Hamed's family contacted the U.S. embassy in Jerusalem about her arrest but has yet to hear back. Read more about her arrest. AP: Trump administration approves $2.8 billion Israel arms package including 40,000 bombs: The Trump administration a $2.8 billion arms package for Israel that includes 40,000 bombs, the New York Times reported. The package includes 20,000 2,000-pound Mk84 bombs and 20,000 BLU-117 general-purpose bombs. Congress has been informally notified of the pending sale. Most of the package would be paid for through U.S. foreign military financing, meaning American taxpayer funds provided to Israel would be used to purchase the weapons from the United States. Malaysia detains Israel-bound shipments: Malaysian authorities three containers headed for Israel at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas on August 19 as authorities investigated their cargo, Bloomberg reported, less than two weeks after another Israel-linked shipment was stopped at the same port. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim wrote in a on X Tuesday that Malaysia would not allow the country to "be used as a conduit for any shipment that supports or contributes to Israel's military capabilities and its atrocities against Palestinians and other innocent lives," adding that suspicious shipments would be investigated and "decisive action" taken where violations are found. Madrid festival suspends Allianz sponsorship after celebrities announce boycott over Israel ties: Madrid's Festival of Ideas its sponsorship agreement with German insurance giant Allianz after celebrities said they would boycott the event over the company's financial ties to Israel, the Times of Israel reported. "Allianz is today the world's largest buyer of Israeli state bonds and, therefore, an essential financial backer of the ongoing genocide," the signatories said, demanding the festival reject funding from companies that "collaborate with the State of Israel in the destruction of the Palestinian people." Organizers said the festival and Allianz agreed to suspend the sponsorship. Lebanon Israeli forces blow up homes, abduct man in southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire": Tyre (Sour): Israeli forces powerful explosions in Mansouri, south of Tyre, on Wednesday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Hasbaya: Israeli forces Halta, blew up a home, and abducted a resident before withdrawing from the town. The area was also hit by three Israeli artillery shells. Lebanon seeks new international force for south after UN peacekeepers leave: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun for a temporary international force to prevent a security vacuum in southern Lebanon after UN peacekeepers' mandate expires at the end of the year. "What matters is that there is no vacuum," Aoun told AFP, saying the force could be European, American, Arab, Asian or another UN mission until the Lebanese army can deploy. Aoun departed for Paris on Wednesday and will join French President Emmanuel Macron and Jordan's King Abdullah II on Thursday to open a preparatory meeting for an international conference supporting the Lebanese army and Internal Security Forces. Aoun also called for a security agreement with Israel to "end the state of hostility," saying negotiations were the only alternative to war. He reiterated that Hezbollah's disarmament was "neither negotiable nor open to discussion," but said it should be achieved without confrontation or "a new civil war." More than 80% of Bint Jbeil destroyed by Israeli attacks, municipality report finds: More than 80% of Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon has been completely destroyed by Israeli attacks between 2023 and 2026, according to a new municipal based on aerial imagery, field surveys, and residents' testimonies, Al-Akhbar reported. More than 2,000 buildings--at least 5,000 housing units--were leveled, including over 500 buildings in the city center alone, according to the report. The municipality also documented the complete destruction of 11 of the city's 14 educational institutions, more than 500 shops, electricity and water networks, and extensive damage to hospitals and medical facilities. More than 70% of the agricultural sector was directly damaged. U.S. News House again votes to end U.S. war in Iran: The U.S. House of Representatives for the third time to direct President Donald Trump to end the U.S. war in Iran. Democrats were joined by seven Republicans:** Reps. Tom Barrett(Mich.), Warren Davidson(Ohio),Brian Fitzpatrick(Penn.),Thomas Massie(Ky.), Nancy Mace (S.C.), Mariannette Miller-Meeks (Iowa), andZach Nunn(Iowa). Aaron Guckian wins Republican nomination for governor of Rhode Island: Aaron Guckian , former head of the Rhode Island Dental Association, defeated Elaine Pelino , a former model, in a close primary for the Republican nomination, the AP . Guckian will face Helena Foulkes , a former CVS executive who defeated Gov. Dan McKee in the Democratic primary last week. U.S. says FBI prevented Russian plot to kill dissidents: Five people were charged in New York with plotting to assassinate a Russian dissident who was living in Washington, D.C., the AP . James Barnacle Jr. , head of New York's FBI office, said the network of Russian intelligence operatives "conspired to intimidate, threaten, or murder people on U.S. soil and around the world." Ed Sheeran 's supporting acts quit tour after Macklemore removed over pro-Palestine remarks: All of Ed Sheeran 's scheduled supporting acts his Loop tour after Macklemore was removed for declaring "Free Palestine" and condemning Israel's genocide. Finneas , Aaron Rowe , Lukas Graham , and Beoga withdrew, citing the silencing of artists speaking for Palestine. Finneas said, "Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed." Sheeran claims he is "not complicit," saying promoters and stadiums removed Macklemore. Macklemore said billionaire Robert Kraft rallied venue owners to threaten the tour with cancellation if he remained. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News EU proposes making Canada the bloc 's first "associate member": European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said in a public statement the European Union would associate EU membership for Canada, as both sides seek closer economic and security ties amid worsening relations with the United States and growing competition with China. The status does not currently exist in EU law and its meaning remains undefined, but von der Leyen said cooperation could include defense-industrial integration, technology, manufacturing, critical raw materials, supply chains and the Arctic. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has said Ottawa is seeking a "unique alliance" with Europe rather than full EU membership. More detailed discussions are expected at an EU-Canada summit in Montreal next month. India summons Pakistan 's top diplomat after naval collision in Arabian Sea: India Pakistan's top diplomat after Pakistani naval units collided with an Indian naval vessel in international waters in the northern Arabian Sea on Tuesday. No major damage was reported, but New Delhi called the incident "unacceptable and unprofessional" and urged Pakistan to follow existing bilateral agreements meant to prevent dangerous military encounters. Pakistan has not yet publicly commented on the naval collision. At least 67 killed in collapse at gold mine in Sudan: At least 67 miners were after a series of adjoining shafts collapsed at the al-Zara gold mine in West Kordofan, with more than 70 people reported dead or missing and some miners potentially still trapped underground. Local monitoring groups said no specialized rescue teams had reached the remote site, leaving residents to dig with basic tools despite unstable sandy ground. A survivor who emerged two days after the collapse reportedly said others were still alive below ground. The Sudan Doctors Network, a medical group tracking the war in Sudan, provided the death toll and said it could increase as rescuers continued to search for people trapped under the rubble. Ukraine launches new offensive north of key Donetsk fortress belt: Ukrainian forces have begun a new operation in northern Donetsk aimed at pushing Russian troops back from the core of Ukraine's remaining defensive line in the region. A senior Ukrainian commander claimed the operation had already cleared Russian infiltration groups from around 75 square kilometers, recaptured additional territory and restored control over several villages, though independent monitors have not been able to confirm these figures. Bank of Japan set to raise rates to a 31-year high over inflation pressures: The Bank of Japan is expected to its interest rate from 1% to 1.25% this week, the highest level since the mid-1990s, as Japan continues moving away from decades of ultra-low interest rates. The expected hike reflects persistent inflation pressures from high oil prices, a weak yen and rising import costs, and would follow tightening by other major central banks. The BOJ ended its long-running stimulus program in 2024 and has raised rates several times since. Officials are believed to see room for additional increases and the bank is trying to avoid either weakening the yen following pressures on energy prices from the Iran War. China warns U.S. deployment of weapons in orbit could fuel a space arms race: Beijing called on Washington to its military buildup in space one day after U.S. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said the United States has "on-orbit space control weapons" capable of defending U.S. forces against hostile action. China's Foreign Ministry said in a statement that Beijing opposes the weaponization of space and warned that U.S. deployments could undermine strategic stability. The U.S. has long developed counter-space systems, but Meink's statement suggested the deployment of weapons directly in orbit rather than relying only on ground-based systems or defensive measures. Former Philippines leaderDuterte appears at ICC ahead of crimes against humanity trial: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte in person at the International Criminal Court in The Hague for the first time in more than a year, as judges prepared for the expected November start of his trial on charges of murder and attempted murder tied to his prosecution of a "war on drugs." Prosecutors allege Duterte was involved in dozens of killings carried out by police and government-linked death squads during his years as mayor of Davao and later as president. Duterte denies the charges. Duterte was arrested in the Philippines and transferred to The Hague in March 2025. name: Justin Riemer - RITE President
subject: RITE President Testifies on NJ Voter Fraud in House Judiciary Subcommittee
body:
6,600 non-citizens improperly registered to vote in NJ between June 2023 and June 2024 |
---
| |
---
| **RITE President Testifies on NJ Voter Fraud in House Judiciary Subcommittee**
---
|
---
| _RITE President Justin Riemer testifies about NJ voter fraud_
---
| | **(Washington, D.C.) –** New Jersey officials recently confessed that about 6,600 people who told the state they were not American citizens were registered to vote anyway, and at least 340 of them went on to cast votes. The mistaken registrations, which occurred between June 2023 and June 2024, were detected two years ago but never publicly admitted until July 2026.

Justin Riemer, President of Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (“RITE”), a non-profit organization that supports litigation to protect election security, testified about the issue Tuesday before the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Oversight in a hearing titled, “[Restoring Election Integrity: Oversight of Voter Fraud in New Jersey](https://us.list-manage.com/1jjVaITizap?e=ea91f782ea&c2id=bf38de461872f35bd013169f413b699e).”

Riemer explored the details of the New Jersey fiasco and offered suggestions for what Congress can do to address the problem:

_“[Congress] should pass real citizenship-verification requirements: the SAVE America Act would bar a state from registering those who do not present documentary proof of citizenship — and because the New Jersey applicants presented none, it would have kept them off the rolls.

“But even narrower reforms directed specifically at DMV registration would plug a huge hole, such as requiring state agencies like DMVs to offer registration only to those who provide proof of citizenship, or at least prohibiting agencies from offering registration to those who provide documentation evidencing they are noncitizens.

“Congress should also require states to use the Department of Homeland Security’s SAVE system to identify noncitizens already on the rolls and to codify the Trump administration’s efforts to make it free and expand its capabilities.”_

In addition, Riemer said Congress could also:

* Amend the Help America Vote Act to verify citizenship using the license and Social Security data states already collect.
* Require states to develop programs to remove noncitizens just as they must for the deceased and nonresidents.
* Clarify that pre-election “blackout” periods restricting certain list maintenance activities do not apply to noncitizen removals.

Riemer’s written testimony can be found [here](https://us.list-manage.com/pKz6XnFfo0a?e=ea91f782ea&c2id=bf38de461872f35bd013169f413b699e), and his oral testimony is [here](https://us.list-manage.com/oH4IQaiMm7c?e=ea91f782ea&c2id=bf38de461872f35bd013169f413b699e).

| 🚨The alarm bells are ringing, Friend!🚨
Everything we've done to put Americans FIRST has been unraveled by one ruling from the Supreme Court...
And now, it's time to take matters into our own hands to restore the bond between our nation and its people and ensure the sacred rights held for true U.S. citizens are only going to true U.S. citizens!
Which sounds like common sense, Friend - trust me, I know.

That means everyone who was born here, regardless of the circumstances or if their parents ever even plan to become true American citizens, will be just as much of a U.S. citizen as you and me, Friend.

body:
Help ensure Texas voters are registered to vote and are prepared to vote early.
#
Peter,
**First:** Texas Republicans placed 1.2 million voters on the voter suspense list and removed some voters from the rolls.
**Then:** Tarrant County, one of the largest counties in Texas with 31% of the population being Latino, slashed 92 polling places.
**Now:** With the Texas voter registration deadline less than a month away on October 5th, **we need to ensure Texas voters are informed and prepared to vote early.**
Being on this voter suspense list doesn’t mean a voter's registration is purged, but it _does_ mean local election offices need an updated address before October 5th — or those voters could face being turned away at the polls.
_We are running out of time to spread the word before the voter registration deadline, so we’re coming directly to you, Peter._
We can’t allow a single eligible voter to be sidelined. **Voto Latino is organizing across Texas every single day to clear up confusion, help voters update their addresses, register new voters, and drive record turnout this fall.**

subject: Just in time for Sea Otter Awareness Week – catch up on these aquatic icons!
body:
You otter learn more about these charismatic critters!
You otter learn more about these charismatic critters!
