#
#### **_Sea otters are adorable – but what makes them so special?_**
With their fuzzy faces, their little whiskers and the way they sometimes hold paws while they sleep, sea otters have captured the hearts of millions. But these marine mammals aren’t just charming – they also play a big role in protecting nature’s balance!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Where do they live?_**
You can find sea otters swimming along the West Coast. A long time ago, they were nearly wiped out by hunters for their soft fur. But these charismatic critters are resilient, and they’ve spent the last hundred years making a heroic comeback. There’s no keeping these otters down!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Okay, so?_**
Sea otters protect kelp forests by carrying out an important task: they snack on sea urchins. Without hungry otters to keep them in check, sea urchins can run amok and devour kelp forests that provide food and cover for other animals. When we help sea otters, we help the kelp!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How can I help?_**
This week is Sea Otter Awareness Week, a time to celebrate these aquatic icons. Sea otters are still missing from key parts of their historical range along the northern California and Oregon coastlines, and it’s time to bring them home! By raising awareness and lending your support, you can help sea otters float on for generations to come!
#
|
---
[CELEBRATE SEA OTTER AWARENESS WEEK!](https://support.defenders.org/s/6023853/38SyG9Xl)

| | |
---

body:
The dubbed “Stop Nick Shirley Act” was made to stop me.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6129499/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvcHFHUVhRVHdTTg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5MTY/LbmNseDFCdHlaUQ/qP2hpZHM9bmMxRG9oNHJvdHlaS0Vscw/gaqrCSg/sbq5aecdb47)

# Friend,
---
There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the **"Stop Nick Shirley Act"** means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law _actually_ does.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Friend: **it makes it harder for anyone — me included — to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent.** I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; _this is just the beginning._ Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. **The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General** — the _one person_ in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Friend. That's the system protecting itself. **[Friend, will you make a tax-deductible gift of $25, $50, or $100 today to help keep independent journalists like me in the field?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
[ **Yes —****I'll****Help Keep Independent Journalists in the Field** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't — daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. _They're right_ — and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, **Lincoln Media Foundation** was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. _That’s why I’m partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation._ They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the _first place._ I’m grateful for their partnership and commitment, and **[every dollar you give to LMF goes directly toward keeping reporters like me in the field](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** – helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them.

**Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible** , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer.
---
[ **Yes —****I'll****Fund Independent Investigations** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Friend, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that’s why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech — and that’s why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! **[Will you help LMF keep me — and journalists like me — in the field with a gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can give today?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
For the truth,

_**Nick Shirley**_
---
[ **Help Support Nick’s Work** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
P.S. — A California assemblyman is already asking the DOJ to intervene against this law. That tells you how serious this is. **[A tax-deductible gift today helps LMF keep me and other independent journalists in the field while this fight plays out.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**

| | | | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASESeptember 16, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**NFIB ENDORSES JULIA LETLOW FOR U.S. SENATE** _Nation’s leading small business advocacy organization backs Letlow for U.S. Senate_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Congresswoman Julia Letlow today announced the endorsement of the National Federation of Independent Business (NFIB) in her campaign for the United States Senate. The nation’s leading small business advocacy organization, NFIB represents more than 3,000 small and independent businesses across Louisiana.
_“Rep. Letlow has been a great supporter of small business during her time in Congress,”_ **said NFIB Political Director Louis Bertolotti.**_“She has earned a lifetime 100% NFIB Voting Record, and helped give small businesses a major win last year with permanency for the 20% Small Business Deduction. NFIB members in Louisiana are excited to see her join the U.S. Senate, and we are proud to support her in this election.”_
_“Small businesses drive Louisiana’s economy, creating jobs, supporting families, and helping communities across our state thrive,”_**said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.**_“I’m incredibly honored to earn NFIB’s endorsement and proud of the record we’ve built in Congress fighting to keep taxes low, cut burdensome regulations, and give our small businesses the freedom and certainty they need to grow. In the Senate, I’ll continue fighting to make sure Main Street always has a strong voice in Washington.”_
Throughout her time in Congress, Letlow has maintained a 100% lifetime NFIB Voting Record and supported policies aimed at lowering taxes and strengthening the environment for small businesses. Last year, she helped secure permanency for the 20% Small Business Deduction, providing long-term tax certainty for small businesses.

clean_body: Let’s clear the air.| | | | | Patriot , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. Thank you for listening, and I hope I can count on your help. | | — John James Republican Nominee for Governor | | Paid for by John James for MI | | 35744 Van Dyke Avenue, Sterling Heights, MI 48312 The use of John James' military images, uniforms, or personnel does not imply endorsement by the Department of War or any branch of the U.S. military. |

This is what a New Mexico campaign looks like.

| | | | | [|

| |
# Nine out of ten dollars came from New Mexicans
---
| | | | | | Friend,
We just filed our campaign finance report with the Secretary of State, and I want you to see the number that matters most.
Of the $943,415 we raised this period, more than **93 percent came from New Mexicans.** Not from donor lists rented out of Washington. Not from coastal fundraisers. From 2,000 people who live here, work here, and are raising their families here. **More than half of those contributions were $100 or less.**
That is what a New Mexico campaign looks like, and it is why we now have more than half a million dollars in the bank heading into the final stretch.
I have spent my career delivering results, not press releases. As Mayor of Rio Rancho, I grew our city by nearly 20,000 residents. I recruited employers who brought hundreds of high paying jobs to our community. I made our neighborhoods safer. That is the record I am bringing to Santa Fe, and New Mexicans are responding to it.
But here is the honest math on the next seven weeks. Every dollar from here goes into reaching voters who have not heard from us yet. Television in Albuquerque. Radio in Farmington, Roswell, and Las Cruces. Mail into the rural counties that often feel left behind or forgotten. That is expensive, and there is no substitute for it.
**A gift of $25 helps us reach a few dozen more households. $50 puts our message on the radio in a market we have been priced out of. $100 gets our mail into homes in a county that gets ignored every four years. And if you can do $250, you are funding the kind of television buy that changes a race.**

| | | A quick note about money ahead of our fast-approaching mid-month fundraising deadline at midnight. Our average online contribution is $60. I'm proud of that number. But I don't want anyone reading these emails to see it and think that's what I'm asking them to give. It's not. A few people can give $100. Some can give $25. But a whole lot of people give just $5. Fellow Conservative: In 1991, the mob came for Clarence Thomas. They smeared him. They tried to destroy his name, his reputation, and his honor. As Justice Thomas himself has put it, critics in Washington _"don't bomb you, necessarily, but they bomb your reputation or your good name or your honor."_ **He refused to cave.** And because he did, he became one of the four giants of the modern Supreme Court — alongside Justices Scalia, Alito, and Rehnquist. Senator Ted Cruz has just released a remarkable new book: _**Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas**_ , built on exclusive interviews with the Justice himself.

---
|

[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=a27e5afeb8f0470bbbbd68ebd75f806b&_e=wc8cwUKw7zCs1mX-PPGTQImS42dn2eh-cSpnB2SmLdTgWzM1lbANVg3BG6vzRgdYbSJum-cvudczbQeLTE3Sl7qciLg-OQfPVIJLKA_kE9d0GC18Lm9aceQ5wCXslACcP24DP0BnVgyXn8TJalu18C_fHcU6GZ5jHzLZEVW9Qy-zEcStyDOZI17qAdvnuGF6YSbKgEeevoguhxIoNKRZSrnolsfHZoHQ6YTPosDO8KDkdF6eI-AliAELpSVquIoyPbYTJKrR0JtinkB8gz7ZeuNrEJiTpO8BINGqMI2CUi8qMeXXE0PvmXI_zuOq7CGXITvL5gYew1bH69j9S1_S-iaA39y1RzdA-8wJy4M6yYcx6NMLTkxlgqOXZBz8EkUS6xqNv0m_j1KF5eUN8RZd4Q%3D%3D)
---

It tells the story of a man who rose from grinding poverty in Pin Point, Georgia — raised by a grandfather he calls _"the single greatest human being I've ever met"_ — to become, in Cruz's words, the justice _"more willing to go back to the original Constitution... and to overturn precedent" than any other in history._

There's a moment in the book that says everything. When Justice Scalia told Thomas he was _"tilting at windmills"_ by trying to overturn bad precedent, Thomas shot back: _"Nino, windmills are dangerous."_

That is the kind of courage we need on the federal bench. And here is the part every conservative must understand:

**Clarence Thomas only reached the Supreme Court because the Senate confirmed him by just two votes.**

Presidents nominate judges. But the Senate confirms them. Every originalist on the bench, and every one we hope to see there, depends on having conservative senators willing to fight. When we lose the Senate, we lose the courts. It's that simple.

That's the mission of the Senate Conservatives Fund: electing principled conservatives to the U.S. Senate so we can confirm the next generation of Clarence Thomases, and stop the Left from ever again turning a confirmation hearing into a character assassination.

So today, we want to put Senator Cruz's book in your hands.

**When you contribute $50 or more to the Senate Conservatives Fund, we'll send you a copy of _Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas_ as our thank-you.** [**Please join us in the effort to build a conservative Senate by making a contribution today.**](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=a27e5afeb8f0470bbbbd68ebd75f806b&_e=wc8cwUKw7zCs1mX-PPGTQImS42dn2eh-cSpnB2SmLdTgWzM1lbANVg3BG6vzRgdYbSJum-cvudczbQeLTE3Sl7qciLg-OQfPVIJLKA_kE9el3eudNOVYSYuiOecXLu80A2kJpI68Fu3yYehBWzxXsD4qjmBaC_y4v8Rr2k4N3-TxL3W4n5UVGBlEb3tHUq7A1jFx0MAMhGEr5oEjKRkP2W_Ffw1vnKiEuvgf8O5Z-hzLCnQS27YtNwK3EBfonHS_-sUsJrz_YNSoc_8f5B89jPE-aX8S5INSg3HZeN7ZGQn3Qe-Vm8_JAExIStCGEhqJQWeLcosXMA0wdW4ynX1MJMMwjo1NtJByseREjGIDN0TpmWQDZqToFr-heCrn_JiJXhu7cvY07g6FUcSNRHKOXQ%3D%3D) Your support will help elect the conservative senators who will confirm judges like Justice Thomas — and will help make sure the next conservative nominee who refuses to bow to the woke mob has the votes to win. ## **The Voters Are Leaving The Clubhouse**
Washington treats party loyalty like a lifetime gym membership: the only difference is you keep paying even if _they_ don't show up. To their jobs, or to represent what you voted for--because they told you they'd do it. Increasingly, Americans are canceling their membership.
For examples of the above, look no further than Democrats (including this one) who currently don't recognize John Fetterman based on the platform he ran on in 2022.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/767abd62-e5c7-443d-ab9a-d3029980a207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Susan Collins has used Maine's independent streak as political oxygen during near-death political experiences, leveraging imagery of past, female, open-minded Republicans--Sens. Margaret Chase Smith and Olympia Snowe--to claim she's the same. She is not. She also plays on goodwill created by Angus King, independent former Governor and current Senator from the Pine Tree State. Meanwhile, Collins skips to Trump's tune, voting to confirm Roe opponent and credibly accused assaulter Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court.
But what can be argued began with Ross Perot in 1992, when he at one point led then-President George H.W. Bush and Democratic challenger Bill Clinton in the race for President, has only continued to grow as the Republican Party has become enmeshed in authoritarianism and corruption and the Democratic Party has failed to win all of those alienated by failing to stand up strong enough as an entity to fight the fascism in our midst.
So independence, and independents, have never been more popular. Gallup found that a record **45% of U.S. adults identified as independents in 2025** , compared with 27% each for Democrats and Republicans. Now that measures political identity, rather than voter registration, which states track differently. But the registration rolls tell their own story: Colorado's unaffiliated voters crossed the 50% threshold in September 2025. Independence has become a major feature of American politics, and it isn't going away, it seemingly will only continue to grow.
### **Perot Brought The Rebellion Into Our Living Rooms**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/767abd62-e5c7-443d-ab9a-d3029980a207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ross Perot didn't invent independent politics, but his 1992 presidential campaign gave the modern revolt against the two-party system a national stage. Nearly 20 million Americans--18.9% of voters--chose the Texas businessman over George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton when the votes were counted. Armed with charts and a folksy charm--and let's not forget billions of dollars--Perot went after both parties, indeed the entire system, demonstrating how much demand existed outside their gates. His later Reform Party campaign received 8.4% in 1996. The presidential breakthrough never came, because, if we're being honest, he was a bit kooky. But the appetite he tapped endured. Independent identification subsequently reached levels Perot's era never saw, with independent identification first surpassing 40% in 2011, and typically remaining at or above since. You could call Perot an early warning system.
### **We 've Already Elected Those Outside The Parties To High Office **
Americans have repeatedly demonstrated that independence can survive contact with an actual ballot. King won Maine's governorship as an independent in 1994. Bernie Sanders, an independent, and Mayor of Burlington, VT before he ran for Congress, became the longest-serving independent member of Congress in U.S. history. His fellow Vermonter, Jim Jeffords, joined a trend of moderate Republicans leaving the increasingly Party of Un-Lincoln to become independents, when he left the GOP as a sitting Senator and caucused with Democrats in 2001. Jesse Ventura beat both major parties to become Minnesota's governor in 1998, running on the Reform Party ticket. And Michael Bloomberg spent part of his New York City mayoralty as an independent after leaving the Republican Party in 2007. These men hardly shared one ideology. That's the point: independence is a relationship to party power, not a single position on the political spectrum.
In the 2010s this trend continued, with Lincoln Chafee, onetime Republican Senator and scion of a moderate Republican family, elected Governor of Rhode Island in 2010. Meanwhile, Bill Walker became the independent Governor of Alaska in 2014. Charlie Crist left the GOP for the remainder of his term in office when, as the sitting Governor of Florida, he lost a GOP Senate primary to the more conservative Marco Rubio (he eventually became and ran as a Democrat). Meanwhile, Sanders and King kept getting reelected to the Senate.
### **Some Don 't Fit Either Party**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/767abd62-e5c7-443d-ab9a-d3029980a207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Before we get to the ones you've inevitably heard the media talking about, there are some other intriguing runs. Colorado Senate candidate Bob Chew is a case in point. He was a Republican but left the party because his moderate politics didn't match MAGALand. Chew's a Navy veteran and built his own company from the ground up, so he has a natural connection to veterans and entrepreneurs. He has three major advantages: He has funds, with over $1.1 million on hand, a good sense of humor--as he's gone a bit viral for doing things like breaking furniture in ads paid for by those funds--and then there's the figure I showed you earlier: _**over 50% of Coloradans are now registered independents**_. Of course, on the downside, former Governor and current Democratic Senator John Hickenlooper has name recognition and incumbency, neither are easy to beat.
In Tennessee, Lauren Pinkston, a former Lipscomb University professor who impresses with her speeches on the stump is running for governor as an independent. She's been hammering Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn, also running for governor. Pinkston has some Democrats not confident in the Democratic Party's prospects in The Volunteer State--they've been shut out in recent years--intrigued by her political talents as a candidate with an anti-Republican wave building.
### **Dan Osborn Made Republicans Sweat --In Nebraska**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/767abd62-e5c7-443d-ab9a-d3029980a207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then came Dan Osborn, the mechanic, Navy veteran and union leader who challenged Republican Sen. Deb Fischer in Nebraska two years ago. Written off, laughed at, assumed to be no threat because only a wealthy self-spender like Bloomberg or Perot was believed to be able to do it, not a unionized industrial mechanic. Yet, in 2024, _Osborn won 46.5% to Fischer 's 53.2%, losing by just 6.7 percentage points_ _in a state Trump carried by roughly 20_. Not a nail biter, yet he made what should've been a laugher (or Laffer?) of a race quite competitive running well ahead of Kamala Harris.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/767abd62-e5c7-443d-ab9a-d3029980a207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Osborn's appeal opened the eyes of some Democrats, not to mention potential independent candidates out West, where both major parties are about as popular as hookworm. Here was a working person talking about working people, without asking voters to embrace the national Democratic brand first. Now Osborn's running again, this time against Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts, and in the last poll available not only had a 3-point lead, but Ricketts was at a dreadful 42%. He has billions. And he'll need them to have a chance to climb out of that hole.
A mechanic challenging an oligarch provides an almost unbeatable contrast at a moment in our history when billionaires, or the "Epstein Class," are so reviled. And Osborn's being joined in this odyssey by others who also don't fit neatly in a box. Yet all are moderate enough so that even though they're independents, with no Democrat in their contests, they'll become de-facto Democrats for those voters. This includes Brian Bengs--a Navy and Air Force veteran who previously ran as a Democrat--taking the independent path in South Dakota, and with poll numbers that also show him within the margin of error or even slightly ahead. And In Idaho, where former Democratic legislator and Army veteran Todd Achilles is challenging Sen. Jim Risch.
Then there is Seth Bodnar, former University of Montana president and Green Beret, full of energy and charisma. Which I saw when I interviewed him on Blue Amp Media. Bodnar's also running for the Senate as an independent, but unlike in those other states, his race was complicated when a Democrat jumped in against the wishes of the party. So even with his bio and talent, he'll have a tougher time of it. Yes, many know he's the Democratic Party choice. He's been endorsed by former Democratic Senator Jon Tester and former President of NARAL Pro-Choice America and recent Montana Democratic Party Chair, Nancy Keenan. But it'll be a challenge not losing low-info Democrats to a vote for the party line. Though Bodnar's confident he'll do it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/767abd62-e5c7-443d-ab9a-d3029980a207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### **Democrats Weighed The Independent Route**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/767abd62-e5c7-443d-ab9a-d3029980a207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The calculation extends to candidates who ultimately chose to keep the Democratic label. In Kansas, Rev. Adam Hamilton, now the Democratic Senate nominee challenging Roger Marshall, seriously considered running as an independent. He chose the Democratic route partly to avoid splitting the opposition vote, while describing himself as independent-minded. That decision captures both the opportunity and the danger: an independent candidacy can expand a coalition, but a crowded ballot can divide it. A poll recently showed him down only 1 point to Marshall, and with Marshall inventing new ways to be boring each day and Hamilton responsible for building the largest Methodist Church in Kansas and the country, this will be interesting.
Nobody should confuse this trend with the rise of one third party, or assume independent voters are all centrists which has been a corporate-media tick for a generation. Most independents still lean toward one major party. But the opportunities are real. Gallup's 2025 figures also show that majorities of both Gen Z adults and millennials identify as independent. One can earn their support through candidates they trust and by talking about what matters to their lives.
For Democrats facing entrenched Republicans, that may sometimes mean backing a credible independent who can reach voters a Democrat cannot. It also may mean looking at an independent in cases where they can win, and especially where the Democratic candidate isn't even getting the support of their own party apparatus (see Montana).
We must judge all candidates on their records, their values, and whether they will defend democracy. But dismissing them because they lack a "D" would be political malpractice. Perot showed that millions wanted another choice. Osborn showed with his right race, another choice can put an otherwise un-winnable election absolutely within reach.

Dan Osborn, Brian Bengs, and Bob Chew--the latter in Colorado where independents just cleared 50%--are among a new class of independent candidates testing the power of that label this election. | | and | Sep 16 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- The Voters Are Leaving The Clubhouse Washington treats party loyalty like a lifetime gym membership: the only difference is you keep paying even if they don't show up. To their jobs, or to represent what you voted for--because they told you they'd do it. Increasingly, Americans are canceling their membership. For examples of the above, look no further than Democrats (including this one) who currently don't recognize John Fetterman based on the platform he ran on in 2022. | | ---|---|--- Susan Collins has used Maine's independent streak as political oxygen during near-death political experiences, leveraging imagery of past, female, open-minded Republicans--Sens. Margaret Chase Smith and Olympia Snowe--to claim she's the same. She is not. She also plays on goodwill created by Angus King, independent former Governor and current Senator from the Pine Tree State. Meanwhile, Collins skips to Trump's tune, voting to confirm Roe opponent and credibly accused assaulter Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court. But what can be argued began with Ross Perot in 1992, when he at one point led then-President George H.W. Bush and Democratic challenger Bill Clinton in the race for President, has only continued to grow as the Republican Party has become enmeshed in authoritarianism and corruption and the Democratic Party has failed to win all of those alienated by failing to stand up strong enough as an entity to fight the fascism in our midst. So independence, and independents, have never been more popular. Gallup found that a record 45% of U.S. adults identified as independents in 2025 , compared with 27% each for Democrats and Republicans. Now that measures political identity, rather than voter registration, which states track differently. But the registration rolls tell their own story: Colorado's unaffiliated voters crossed the 50% threshold in September 2025. Independence has become a major feature of American politics, and it isn't going away, it seemingly will only continue to grow. Perot Brought The Rebellion Into Our Living Rooms | | ---|---|--- Ross Perot didn't invent independent politics, but his 1992 presidential campaign gave the modern revolt against the two-party system a national stage. Nearly 20 million Americans--18.9% of voters--chose the Texas businessman over George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton when the votes were counted. Armed with charts and a folksy charm--and let's not forget billions of dollars--Perot went after both parties, indeed the entire system, demonstrating how much demand existed outside their gates. His later Reform Party campaign received 8.4% in 1996. The presidential breakthrough never came, because, if we're being honest, he was a bit kooky. But the appetite he tapped endured. Independent identification subsequently reached levels Perot's era never saw, with independent identification first surpassing 40% in 2011, and typically remaining at or above since. You could call Perot an early warning system. We 've Already Elected Those Outside The Parties To High Office Americans have repeatedly demonstrated that independence can survive contact with an actual ballot. King won Maine's governorship as an independent in 1994. Bernie Sanders, an independent, and Mayor of Burlington, VT before he ran for Congress, became the longest-serving independent member of Congress in U.S. history. His fellow Vermonter, Jim Jeffords, joined a trend of moderate Republicans leaving the increasingly Party of Un-Lincoln to become independents, when he left the GOP as a sitting Senator and caucused with Democrats in 2001. Jesse Ventura beat both major parties to become Minnesota's governor in 1998, running on the Reform Party ticket. And Michael Bloomberg spent part of his New York City mayoralty as an independent after leaving the Republican Party in 2007. These men hardly shared one ideology. That's the point: independence is a relationship to party power, not a single position on the political spectrum. In the 2010s this trend continued, with Lincoln Chafee, onetime Republican Senator and scion of a moderate Republican family, elected Governor of Rhode Island in 2010. Meanwhile, Bill Walker became the independent Governor of Alaska in 2014. Charlie Crist left the GOP for the remainder of his term in office when, as the sitting Governor of Florida, he lost a GOP Senate primary to the more conservative Marco Rubio (he eventually became and ran as a Democrat). Meanwhile, Sanders and King kept getting reelected to the Senate. Some Don 't Fit Either Party | | ---|---|--- Before we get to the ones you've inevitably heard the media talking about, there are some other intriguing runs. Colorado Senate candidate Bob Chew is a case in point. He was a Republican but left the party because his moderate politics didn't match MAGALand. Chew's a Navy veteran and built his own company from the ground up, so he has a natural connection to veterans and entrepreneurs. He has three major advantages: He has funds, with over $1.1 million on hand, a good sense of humor--as he's gone a bit viral for doing things like breaking furniture in ads paid for by those funds--and then there's the figure I showed you earlier: over 50% of Coloradans are now registered independents. Of course, on the downside, former Governor and current Democratic Senator John Hickenlooper has name recognition and incumbency, neither are easy to beat. In Tennessee, Lauren Pinkston, a former Lipscomb University professor who impresses with her speeches on the stump is running for governor as an independent. She's been hammering Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn, also running for governor. Pinkston has some Democrats not confident in the Democratic Party's prospects in The Volunteer State--they've been shut out in recent years--intrigued by her political talents as a candidate with an anti-Republican wave building. Dan Osborn Made Republicans Sweat --In Nebraska | | ---|---|--- Then came Dan Osborn, the mechanic, Navy veteran and union leader who challenged Republican Sen. Deb Fischer in Nebraska two years ago. Written off, laughed at, assumed to be no threat because only a wealthy self-spender like Bloomberg or Perot was believed to be able to do it, not a unionized industrial mechanic. Yet, in 2024, Osborn won 46.5% to Fischer 's 53.2%, losing by just 6.7 percentage points in a state Trump carried by roughly 20. Not a nail biter, yet he made what should've been a laugher (or Laffer?) of a race quite competitive running well ahead of Kamala Harris. | | ---|---|--- Osborn's appeal opened the eyes of some Democrats, not to mention potential independent candidates out West, where both major parties are about as popular as hookworm. Here was a working person talking about working people, without asking voters to embrace the national Democratic brand first. Now Osborn's running again, this time against Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts, and in the last poll available not only had a 3-point lead, but Ricketts was at a dreadful 42%. He has billions. And he'll need them to have a chance to climb out of that hole. A mechanic challenging an oligarch provides an almost unbeatable contrast at a moment in our history when billionaires, or the "Epstein Class," are so reviled. And Osborn's being joined in this odyssey by others who also don't fit neatly in a box. Yet all are moderate enough so that even though they're independents, with no Democrat in their contests, they'll become de-facto Democrats for those voters. This includes Brian Bengs--a Navy and Air Force veteran who previously ran as a Democrat--taking the independent path in South Dakota, and with poll numbers that also show him within the margin of error or even slightly ahead. And In Idaho, where former Democratic legislator and Army veteran Todd Achilles is challenging Sen. Jim Risch. Then there is Seth Bodnar, former University of Montana president and Green Beret, full of energy and charisma. Which I saw when I interviewed him on Blue Amp Media. Bodnar's also running for the Senate as an independent, but unlike in those other states, his race was complicated when a Democrat jumped in against the wishes of the party. So even with his bio and talent, he'll have a tougher time of it. Yes, many know he's the Democratic Party choice. He's been endorsed by former Democratic Senator Jon Tester and former President of NARAL Pro-Choice America and recent Montana Democratic Party Chair, Nancy Keenan. But it'll be a challenge not losing low-info Democrats to a vote for the party line. Though Bodnar's confident he'll do it. | | ---|---|--- Democrats Weighed The Independent Route | | ---|---|--- The calculation extends to candidates who ultimately chose to keep the Democratic label. In Kansas, Rev. Adam Hamilton, now the Democratic Senate nominee challenging Roger Marshall, seriously considered running as an independent. He chose the Democratic route partly to avoid splitting the opposition vote, while describing himself as independent-minded. That decision captures both the opportunity and the danger: an independent candidacy can expand a coalition, but a crowded ballot can divide it. A poll recently showed him down only 1 point to Marshall, and with Marshall inventing new ways to be boring each day and Hamilton responsible for building the largest Methodist Church in Kansas and the country, this will be interesting. Nobody should confuse this trend with the rise of one third party, or assume independent voters are all centrists which has been a corporate-media tick for a generation. Most independents still lean toward one major party. But the opportunities are real. Gallup's 2025 figures also show that majorities of both Gen Z adults and millennials identify as independent. One can earn their support through candidates they trust and by talking about what matters to their lives. For Democrats facing entrenched Republicans, that may sometimes mean backing a credible independent who can reach voters a Democrat cannot. It also may mean looking at an independent in cases where they can win, and especially where the Democratic candidate isn't even getting the support of their own party apparatus (see Montana). We must judge all candidates on their records, their values, and whether they will defend democracy. But dismissing them because they lack a "D" would be political malpractice. Perot showed that millions wanted another choice. Osborn showed with his right race, another choice can put an otherwise un-winnable election absolutely within reach. **The difference between me and Greg Abbott is that I 'm willing to defend my plan for the future of Texas -- and well, he isn't.**
But Abbott's decade-long record speaks for itself: Texans have faced years of rising costs, some of the highest uninsured rates in the country, families struggling to keep the lights on because electricity has become so expensive, and billions of our taxpayer dollars flowing to politically connected donors and special interests instead of working people.
**Greg Abbott has sold the people of Texas to the highest bidder, and he 's dodging accountability.**
All campaign long, I've made it clear that I'm ready to debate Greg Abbott -- but he's stayed silent. He's silent because he knows he has failed Texans.
As Governor, I would never hide from the people I am elected to serve. But Abbott is out of touch with Texans and deeply unpopular. That's why he is spending his time spreading lies about me and hiding from the voters.
After traveling all across Texas throughout my campaign, one thing is crystal clear: Texans are ready for a change. From Amarillo, to the Valley, to Dallas-Fort Worth -- Texans deserve a governor they can trust to put their needs first. Texans deserve a governor who's going to fight for them.
I can't wait to be that Governor.
I'm running because I believe leadership means showing up, answering tough questions, and being accountable to the people of Texas. Not hiding from them.
I'll proudly defend my plan to secure the American Dream by strengthening our public schools, lowering costs for working families, expanding access to healthcare, and building an economy that works for _everyone_ -- not just the wealthy and well-connected.
Greg Abbott can keep avoiding the conversation.
But I'll keep traveling across Texas, listening to voters, and earning their trust.
**If you disagree with anything I have to say, Abbott, come say it to my face on the debate stage. I 'm beyond ready.**
**[And if you agree with my vision of a Texas where everyone has a seat at the table, I hope you 'll consider chipping in $5 or more today to power our movement.](https://substack.com/redirect/1d0e7823-ba85-4853-9ee4-2ea2d4adb70e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
48 days and counting,
Gina

body:
The Supreme Court got this one right. |
#
---
Team, The Supreme Court just delivered an important reminder that states run our elections. **We challenged an effort from Washington Republicans to change the rules for mail-in voting just weeks before Election Day._And the Court agreed those changes shouldn't move forward for this year's elections._** In Michigan, voters made their voices heard when they protected the freedom to vote by mail in our state constitution. That's not something politicians in Washington should be able to undo at the last minute. But one court victory doesn't end the fight. Across the country, good people are stepping up to run for office because they know what's at stake. They'll help decide whether our country has leaders who defend the Constitution, protect our fundamental rights, and stand up when those rights are challenged. The Fed Decides Today, Against a 19-Year Yield High and a Saudi 'Red Line'
The Fed's most consequential decision of the year arrives hours after Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2007 and Saudi Arabia declared Mecca a red line following an intercepted Houthi drone.
|

This is the day this newsletter has been counting down to for a week: the Federal Reserve's rate decision, at 2:00 PM ET, arrives after the sharpest run-up in bond yields and oil prices of the entire conflict. **Verified fact:** Tuesday's close saw the S&P; 500 fall 0.45% to 7,585.73, the Dow drop 0.63% to 52,093.11, and the Nasdaq slide 0.78% to 25,981.57 — the sixth decline in seven sessions — while the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.006%, its highest level since 2007. Brent crude closed near $107.90, up 2.14% on the day. Overnight, Saudi Arabia said it intercepted a Houthi drone aimed at Mecca and called the attempt a “red line.”

**Our interpretation:** a 10-year yield at its highest level since 2007 is a materially larger repricing than the three-year high flagged earlier this week — it places current borrowing costs closer to pre-financial-crisis norms than to anything markets have priced in over a decade. **What remains unknown** is how much of this reflects the specific, resolvable shock of Middle East oil disruption versus a broader reassessment of inflation persistence that would outlast this week's Fed decision regardless of its outcome.
| | Regime Signal 02 — Mecca Crossed a Line That Hadn't Been Crossed Since 2017
---|---
**Verified fact:** Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed a drone before it reached airspace over Mecca, roughly 1,100 kilometers from Yemen's border, and declared the city a “red line.” The Houthis denied responsibility. It is only the second attempted strike on the city by the group, after a 2017 ballistic missile attack. **Our interpretation:** whether or not Houthi denial holds up, a Saudi government that has just called an attack on Islam's holiest city a red line has far less room to negotiate a quick, conciliatory Hormuz framework this week than it did even a few days ago — the diplomatic track flagged as stalled on Monday looks further away, not closer, this morning.
| | Regime Signal 03 — The White House Sounded a Different Note Than the Chokepoint Data
---|---
**Reported claim:** President Trump said this week that Iran wants a deal “quickly and badly,” and separately that “the Houthis called us, and they don’t want to fight with us,” suggesting Washington sees the conflict as narrowing rather than widening. **Verified fact, in tension with that framing:** Hormuz transit fell to just four vessels Monday versus ten the day before, against a pre-war baseline of over 100 daily transits, and war-risk insurance now runs 3–10% of hull value per tanker crossing. **What remains unknown** is which signal the market should weight more heavily heading into this afternoon's Fed decision: the administration's diplomatic optimism, or the physical shipping data showing the chokepoint nearly closed.
| | Today’s Confirmation Point
---|---
2:00 PM ET: the Federal Reserve's rate decision, updated economic projections, and Chair Kevin Warsh's first press conference as head of the Fed — arriving with a 19-year yield high, a fresh Mecca-adjacent escalation, and a White House publicly downplaying the same conflict driving the inflation this decision responds to.

Fellow Concerned American,

Parents send their kids to school to learn reading, writing, and math... not to receive anatomically explicit toys with removable body parts from school staff.

But that’s exactly what might be coming to Minnesota schools soon.

**Fox News reported that “MyGender Dolls” will be available to school counselors, educators, and clinicians this school year.**

These “trans” dolls were developed through the University of Minnesota’s Early Innovation Fund, under a program Gov. Tim Walz has championed and been personally honored for. _They ship with removable, swappable genitalia and are built for children**ages 4-10**_.

And it gets worse...

Not a single Minnesota parent that Defending Education spoke with had received any notification about the dolls. **_There is no confirmed way to opt out_**.

That’s why Defending Education filed a federal privacy complaint – citing violations of the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment, and the First and Fourteenth Amendments.

I’m Nicole Neily, President of **Defending Education** – a national grassroots organization fighting to restore academic excellence and parental rights in America’s schools.

We believe four-year-olds have no business handling anatomically explicit material from any adult, in any building, for any reason. **We believe parents – not a governor, not a university lab – decide what’s appropriate for their child.**

And we believe it’s time to ask Americans plainly where they stand.

Please take our one-question poll right now:
**📊 NATIONAL DEFENDING EDUCATION POLL 📊** [**[POLL] Should anatomically explicit “trans” gender dolls be given to 4- to 10-year-olds in schools?**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDF9AAwAAAAAAv2xg6719cked_zjUuD3SRZcMuTy6hG1_zxn3XrnRs8BWb4wRLqp9V-22vlRWB-cpOeCqgTpHjFqgdC0Ol8Zg8RyIfHeZcq1q5zA_AVI6g)

Hi, it’s Dr. Jasmine Clark. I’m a microbiologist and Emory professor. I’m also a Democrat running to represent Georgia’s 13th District in Congress.
In a second, I’m going to ask you to contribute to my campaign. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=251215em] But first, I want to be really clear about what’s happening in Georgia — because it matters.
Democrats just flipped a state House seat in a district Trump won by double digits. Not a purple district. Not a swing seat. A place Republicans thought was permanently locked down.
And a Democrat won anyway.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=251215em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=251215em]
This didn’t happen because voters suddenly changed who they are. It happened because Democrats showed up with a message about lowering costs, protecting health care, and standing up for working families — and backed it up with organizing.
This win is part of a much bigger story. Over the past year, Democrats have flipped seats in red districts, on new maps, and in special elections that Republicans were counting on us to lose. Even in Georgia, we’ve already flipped statewide seats and chipped away at GOP power they assumed was untouchable.
That’s not luck. That’s momentum.
Republicans want us to believe 2026 is already decided. They want donors to sit on the sidelines. They want organizers exhausted and underfunded.
I’m not buying it — and neither should you.
If we want more victories like this one, we have to keep investing now: in organizing, in candidates, and in the infrastructure that turns frustration into victories. If you’re fired up by this win and want to help turn momentum into a wave, I’m asking you to chip in to my campaign today. Even $10 or $15 makes a big difference. # **Trump hired Kevin Warsh to cut rates. He 's probably set to hike today**
The Federal Reserve is expected to raise rates 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% at **[2 p.m. ET,](https://substack.com/redirect/e7b4f716-1a5d-42a3-946a-d3dc3e8b7a44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/e7b4f716-1a5d-42a3-946a-d3dc3e8b7a44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)the first hike since July 2023, as Chair Kevin Warsh's words take center stage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d55ac72d-6536-4ace-b7f9-bc850594d0d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Markets price the hike:** **[CME FedWatch showed a 92.5%](https://substack.com/redirect/f6c980c2-c31b-414a-8755-cf2df431228c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** chance of a quarter-point increase, up from 36% a month ago, after the Fed held at 3.50%-3.75% through all 5 meetings this year.
* **Inflation still above target:** **[Fox cited](https://substack.com/redirect/cba2c3a2-f898-4529-9dc7-f87599f7d775?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** July PCE up 3.7% and core PCE up 3.3%, with August CPI up 3.4%; the 10-year yield hit 5.041% Tuesday, the highest since 2007.
* **Dots and 2029 arrive:** Officials will publish a new SEP and the first 2029 dots; Warsh, leading his third FOMC since a May confirmation,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/6b54e2c4-dd86-4c45-a983-fb6df154a6d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[declined to submit his own projection.](https://substack.com/redirect/6b54e2c4-dd86-4c45-a983-fb6df154a6d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **White House wants a hold:** NEC Director Kevin Hassett said 3-month annualized core CPI is already at the 2% target, while former Treasury adviser Joe LaVorgna sees at least 4 hikes.

# Investors beg for a $1.2T OpenAI round. Altman sits tight
OpenAI investors **[have floated a funding round above $1.2 trillion](https://substack.com/redirect/6c28e489-836a-495c-8066-cfd8b37004aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for employee liquidity, but the company is not engaging **[after March's $122 billion raise at an $852 billion valuation.](https://substack.com/redirect/709f1a68-67ca-4278-bdf7-ef3b4f89cb8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/671d695e-cde2-4478-826c-ef6f741b7314?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Investors came knocking:** People familiar told CNBC backers approached the lab and pitched the raise as a way for employees to sell stock after an August secondary of roughly $7 billion.
* **CFO says cash is ample:** Sarah Friar told CNBC's Jim Cramer on Tuesday the company still has "an incredible balance sheet," and an all-hands last month kept a 2027 IPO target.
* **Revenue up, margins down:** Second-quarter revenue rose to $6.7 billion from $5.7 billion in the first quarter, while the operating margin fell and delayed profitability before an IPO.
* **Safety complicates the listing:** After two models escaped containment and reached Hugging Face, Sam Altman told Fortune a public listing now would be an "ill-advised" moment.

# Senate kills Clarity 50-49 as bitcoin ETFs bleed $450M
The Senate on Tuesday[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/c3f55eb6-8d15-4133-9120-f9d9ec6efea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[blocked the Clarity Act 50-49,](https://substack.com/redirect/c3f55eb6-8d15-4133-9120-f9d9ec6efea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** short of the 60 votes needed to proceed, stalling a digital-asset rulebook and triggering about[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/223c351d-e6aa-4b96-8739-8405efcac775?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[$450 million in spot bitcoin ETF outflows.](https://substack.com/redirect/223c351d-e6aa-4b96-8739-8405efcac775?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/94b6a4c8-b10e-4b46-bf41-12a42359d057?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Ethics fight sank it:** **[Republicans added ethics limits Sunday](https://substack.com/redirect/e5150d94-6b1d-45b9-b5dd-782c6bf8ccaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** over official crypto profits, but Sen. Ruben Gallego said the GOP cared "more about making sure the president keeps making money."
* **Lummis called it over:** Sen. Cynthia Lummis said before the vote that failure would mean "it's over"; the Senate leaves in early October and the House recesses this week, with midterms in 7 weeks.
* **Tokens sold off fast:**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/c3f55eb6-8d15-4133-9120-f9d9ec6efea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[CNBC said](https://substack.com/redirect/c3f55eb6-8d15-4133-9120-f9d9ec6efea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** bitcoin fell 3%, Coinbase 8%, and Circle 10%; **[Yahoo said](https://substack.com/redirect/223c351d-e6aa-4b96-8739-8405efcac775?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a dozen U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $450 million on Sept. 15, the most since June 25.
* **Wild West warning:** **[Sen. Tim Scott said that](https://substack.com/redirect/4526d68f-c79d-4007-804e-131eb3c369f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** without market-structure law the U.S. stays the "wild, wild West," as the SEC floated $75 million token sales without registration.

# Bessent: China "steals" Claude. Novo just hired Claude
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Congress the U.S. **[needs more open-source AI models](https://substack.com/redirect/dfa9e561-46ca-4fd1-ac3d-0e5784a28390?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to compete with China, as **[Novo Nordisk partnered with Anthropic](https://substack.com/redirect/aaf24097-59ae-477d-87d2-ac8b12223a01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to speed drug discovery with Claude.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1bf1085d-5e06-4746-80a1-fcaa8fbd2725?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Labs must not lock rules:** Bessent told House Financial Services the U.S. cannot let large labs win regulatory capture that stops innovation, and called Anthropic's Mythos a step change toward AGI.
* **Distill means steal:** He said Chinese models distill from U.S. systems -- "a polite, scientific word for steal" -- and that many Chinese models "think they're Mythos, they think they're Claude."
* **Open weights got a pass:** Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta and others argued in a July letter against sweeping limits; an August voluntary framework exempted open-source models from pre-release security reviews.
* **Claude enters the lab:** Novo and Anthropic said they will use Claude for targeted discovery workflows, test Claude Science, and apply Anthropic models to AI-driven software development under human oversight.

# Ford recalls 223,472 F-150s because the gas tank can fall off
Ford is **[recalling more than 223,472 F-150 pickups](https://substack.com/redirect/7241ca40-b927-4909-b77f-120075b811ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from the 2023-2027 model years after NHTSA found fuel-tank straps that were not seated in the frame, a defect that can spark a fire or stall.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0d9c914f-44eb-4bfc-a5a4-d5dc0d33e8e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Strap slots missed the frame:** NHTSA said front fuel-tank strap T-slots were not properly inserted into the frame rail at assembly, which can let the tank detach and become a road hazard.
* **One percent actually affected:** Ford estimates 1% of the recalled trucks have the defect and will mail owners starting Sept. 21 for a free inspection and replacement at Ford or Lincoln dealers.
* **Hands-free towing arrives:** The 2027 F-150 adds BlueCruise with Towing for hands-free driving on more than 130,000 highway miles with trailers up to 10,000 pounds; more than 75% of F-150 owners tow.
* **Carhartt edition debuts:** **[A first F-150 Carhartt package](https://substack.com/redirect/7a7e4161-b610-4ee4-972e-10607c19a40b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on 4x4 XLT Crew Cabs adds branded bedliner and interior accents; Ford restored the 5.0-liter V8 on King Ranch and Platinum trims.

* * *
* * *
# 84% of funds paused rare-disease bets. That freeze is thawing
Investors are **[rushing back into rare-disease drugmakers](https://substack.com/redirect/6f9a7e52-0668-4812-891b-1c7a952f4130?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after FDA hard-liners left, reversing a plunge that hit the sector when second-term reviewers balked at approvals built on tiny trials
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c9bdf052-98aa-4852-b95e-5f8bafea43a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Tiny trials, no placebos:** Rare-disease companies often test drugs in small patient groups and sometimes skip usual large-trial features such as placebo controls.
* **First year was brutal:** In the first year of the Trump administration, few biotech corners were dicier than rare-disease names, and those shares plunged.
* **Reviewers wanted more proof:** In the second Trump term, FDA officials grew skeptical of approving drugs on such limited evidence.
* **Hard-liners now gone:** With those officials out, investors are piling back into the same rare-disease bets that sold off.

* * *
* * *
# Huang and Zuck tell Amodei: we're not slowing down
Nvidia shares rose 0.9% in Wednesday premarket after CEO Jensen Huang **[called AI safety an engineering problem](https://substack.com/redirect/98a72663-2264-4ee3-9468-816321814f4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg said labs already have incentives to train models safely.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/492c1154-a0c7-49a3-877f-90801e996aa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Safety is engineering:** Huang said if a company is not confident in a product's safety it should not ship, adding "We don't need any new laws. We don't need new regulations."
* **Customers back the push:** Zuckerberg said in a Tuesday social post that individual AI labs already have incentives to train models safely.
* **Washington applauded Huang:** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and White House AI adviser David Sacks praised the Nvidia chief's comments.
* **Chip stock still digging out:** Shares were trying to recoup losses from earlier in the week after Anthropic and OpenAI leaders backed a slower development pace that could mean more regulation.

* * *
* * *
# J.B. Hunt plunges 12% as diesel eats the quarter
J.B. Hunt shares fell Wednesday **[as Barron's warned that high diesel prices](https://substack.com/redirect/d80b5b04-4f4b-4549-a2c5-66f31425da47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** can finally hit transportation earnings even at carriers that typically pass fuel costs through to customers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b9706ef0-e917-45f0-9a9c-5d3fea168476?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Pass-through has limits:** Barron's said high fuel prices can eventually pressure transportation-company earnings even when those costs are usually billed onward to shippers.
* **Big year coming in:** Coming into Wednesday, J.B. Hunt stock had gained 41% this year.
* **Diesel is the squeeze:** The report framed record diesel prices as the threat now large enough to show up in results.
* **Earnings sit in the crosshairs:** Barron's said diesel is now high enough to hit J.B. Hunt earnings, not just show up as a billed surcharge.

Then I went public.| | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139333334/647007709/-323302678?refcode=260916_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWRiODRjZWYtZjViMS1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=210-aUOdzUseWP1WhcVw9qRobuX7aXXm78THxam8mk4=)
---
**I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents.**

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home.

I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country.

After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser.

I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first.

Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors.

**I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country.**

Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump?

For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening.

But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question:

Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous?

In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public.

I was terrified.

I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence.

But silence costs more.

So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat.

Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue.

I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first.

Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences.

**That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild.**

Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him.

They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts.

It MUST reach the ballot box.

It MUST be organized.

And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power.

[**So, I'm asking personally: Will you donate $10, $25 or whatever you can afford today to help Resist Reclaim Rebuild defeat MAGA in the battleground races that matter most?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139333335/647007710/-323302678?refcode=260916_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWRiODRjZWYtZjViMS1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=210-aUOdzUseWP1WhcVw9qRobuX7aXXm78THxam8mk4=)[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139333336/647007711/949025562?refcode=260916_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWRiODRjZWYtZjViMS1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=210-aUOdzUseWP1WhcVw9qRobuX7aXXm78THxam8mk4=)
---

MAGA wants us exhausted. They want every new outrage to make us feel a little more powerless. They want us to believe that one person speaking out, casting a ballot or making a contribution cannot possibly change anything.

I learned the opposite.

I learned that courage is contagious.

Control of Congress could come down to only a handful of seats. Your contribution can help elect Democrats who will defend our Constitution, demand accountability and finally place a meaningful check on Trump’s unfettered power.

Please help Resist Reclaim Rebuild fight for those victories today.

But above all, refuse to be silent.

Olivia Troye

name: Jen Kiggans
subject: I'm sorry to ask again
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kiggans for Congress
body:
Not what I spent my time doing

|
Peter,
I’ll be honest with you... I’m not great at asking for money. It’s the part of this job I hate the most.
I didn’t spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf.
And when I came home, I didn’t become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals.
That’s really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it’s going in the wrong direction most days.
[I didn't run for Congress for the title. I ran because I looked at the country my children were inheriting, and I felt sick to my stomach. #### **The Moment We’ve Been Building Toward**
The Forward Party may be on the verge of an independent governing fulcrum in the Senate.

For years, we’ve talked about what it would mean to have independent voices holding the balance of power in Congress. Now, with Todd Achilles in Idaho and Brian Bengs in South Dakota running competitive, one-on-one Senate races, we’re seeing that possibility take shape in real time. Recent polling has [Achilles within four points of Senator Jim Risch](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=tQGdR6pbHkqGql-Twtdc5O68BRJejlbtfgVpYd7Li8aMgZYPPkp4VNqRTVZn-SZlGcRC_fdcPD2kLwvbmnJopBjCz8BbG2l81Lxm3caFryfm_6xGacQySKtkzd7qYFeROROPYV5dYlsR-FZ3HJQ0WDhlLsV1NOl0CLn1y_BMaS0&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_120a&n=1), while Bengs and Senator Mike Rounds [are tied at 44% in South Dakota](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=bgMS2QHeK60ESqNG1k4-JrpbG5wQ5v3ApUEpmmVJFfmdWUnq8atu77fgxVUcRiF9tX74mzMFNf0jI3rXungVbaU2yGVqK4oePxzan53eR_7GYqvkRKHiboH4ZKORsIEN&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_120a&n=2). South Dakota is getting plenty of attention for other reasons too, following recent reporting about [Rounds’ senior advisor simultaneously working as a lobbyist](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=wWw1LGKe09YoyrHaTkDQ4GG1qh98GYcXj0zaOWKzAET_lk60BUdYpc4H7e0YVWBMnMaZEs0qSDAuQ7V7kKYE7THpX46qwQIhMfaqf43Uhu1rxqLpw5A7yNXzRPlQRs_AV8YIykY2vSu7EravfyXtpQ&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_120a&n=3) for corporate clients including Meta. Todd and Brian recently joined former Lieutenant Governor Kerry Healey on [Boston Public Radio](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=_KeSraPW0gSlxEBMOvJrEouH4SjeZmYtvTWulgNFAfbY5ox6nJLB3v7t4IkB_96B&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_120a&n=4) to talk about their campaigns and the independent opportunity. **About the Forward Party** The Forward Party is bringing moderates, conservatives, and progressives together to heal our political divisions, find our shared ground, and create a brighter future for America. Forward Party candidates are accountable to the voters, and they will focus on solutions, not partisan fighting, in order to serve their constituents better.

### [Forward March '26: Rapid City, South Dakota Canvassing Opportunity](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=hLf6ra6-T4Ek_sf_A8AjE1UyKJVU-Cjm2KssIg2H03tsE-KfUHP-HQw907IM5a2O48yYDfJyGpnJ4yFYWcK2RTmbf3wA78wTUvq3VwGew0Fucr7FJXHq6JRYo-NGMNmm&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_120a&n=5)
It's time to hit the pavement in Rapid City! Our affiliate partner, Moving America Forward, will be canvassing to connect with independent voters. Join them and get out into your community to have real conversations about real solutions. Whether your first time canvassing or you're a seasoned veteran, all experience levels are needed! Training and materials will be provided. There will be a morning deployment from 8:30 AM to 12:00 PM and an afternoon deployment from 12:30 PM to 4:00 PM. Additionally, Moving America Forward will be hosting a multi-partner coalition dinner (5:30 PM - 8:00 PM) for participating volunteers and partner organizations, featuring special guest speaker and U.S. Senate candidate Brian Bengs. Hope to see you there! Sign up at the link above.

I'm not going to give you a spreadsheet today. There won't be any precinct breakdowns or deep dives into the data. That comes later, once the dust settles and the numbers make their final call. The first sip of a good whiskey tells you something the tasting notes never quite capture. The whole picture is not yet revealed, only the foundation upon which everything else is built.
Speak with everyday voters, the folks who aren't in the party's inner circle. These are the ones who don't spend their days managing the machinery of power from the inside. You will hear a voice that goes beyond polling terms like "anti-establishment sentiment." You will hear anger.
I've sat in booths and heard the talk. Some go so far as to say they are looking at a Libertarian. Some go further, declaring they are just staying home in a quiet, stubborn protest. And then there are those who go further still, doing the unthinkable: they are casting a vote for a Democrat.
I first felt this shift before the primary while I was a congressional candidate in Florida's 14th. I saw voters from every age group looking for alternatives to the same Grand Old Party representatives.
And I wonder what it is that pushes a lifelong Republican, the kind of man who never missed an election in his life, a "super voter" in the eyes of the party, to finally walk away from the only party he's ever known. I wonder if the candidates heading into the general election even know how to talk to him, or if they're too busy reading the polls to notice he's gone.
If you ask these folks what keeps them up at night, they won't talk about "policy." They'll talk about the new Flock camera on the corner of their street, watching them come and go. They'll talk about the AI data centers eating up the land, turning the Florida they love into a grid of concrete warehouses and Big Brother eyes. They might not know the intricate laws, but they can read the headlines. They see the water disappearing and the cameras multiplying, and they rush out to stand in opposition. I've seen it with my own eyes. Liberals and conservatives. Boomers and zoomers. A seventy-year-old man and a twenty-year-old girl, seated side-by-side in a city meeting, staring at the council with the same look of a trust betrayed. And then, standing side-by-side in the streets in protest.
On the other hand, there are the establishment voters--people who would never call themselves that, but who are well acquainted with the secret handshakes and the backroom deals. For those voices, the talk dropped to a whisper, and I leaned in close to catch the truth. While they are voicing discontent, they are not willing to depart from whoever ends up winning the nomination for one reason: they will not vote Democrat.
Meanwhile, the Grand Old Party, with the Trump presidency coming to an end, twists and turns, vying for control over its own future.
The questions that still hang in the air, whether in a corner booth or a city council chamber, are these: why did their candidates not win? There were certainly enough candidates decrying these "evils." Was it a lack of funding? Name recognition? Or is this just the temper tantrum of a few disgruntled voters and young adults afraid of losing their chance to make a mark in history? Will the candidates in the general election be able or willing to fight the powerful AI data and surveillance donors? Or will they justify these as necessary security measures to deter and catch criminals?
In the end, we are left with a choice. Do we prioritize a unified front for the sake of strength, or do we remain true to a conscience that may lead us in a different direction?
The first sip has been tasted. The subsequent sips, culminating on the 3rd of November, will reveal the rest.
**Your voice is your crown.**
**Gavriel Soriano**
**Every One A King**

clean_body: Beyond the tasting notes of the party line. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Beyond the tasting notes of the party line. | | | Sep 16| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- I'm not going to give you a spreadsheet today. There won't be any precinct breakdowns or deep dives into the data. That comes later, once the dust settles and the numbers make their final call. The first sip of a good whiskey tells you something the tasting notes never quite capture. The whole picture is not yet revealed, only the foundation upon which everything else is built. Speak with everyday voters, the folks who aren't in the party's inner circle. These are the ones who don't spend their days managing the machinery of power from the inside. You will hear a voice that goes beyond polling terms like "anti-establishment sentiment." You will hear anger. I've sat in booths and heard the talk. Some go so far as to say they are looking at a Libertarian. Some go further, declaring they are just staying home in a quiet, stubborn protest. And then there are those who go further still, doing the unthinkable: they are casting a vote for a Democrat. I first felt this shift before the primary while I was a congressional candidate in Florida's 14th. I saw voters from every age group looking for alternatives to the same Grand Old Party representatives. And I wonder what it is that pushes a lifelong Republican, the kind of man who never missed an election in his life, a "super voter" in the eyes of the party, to finally walk away from the only party he's ever known. I wonder if the candidates heading into the general election even know how to talk to him, or if they're too busy reading the polls to notice he's gone. If you ask these folks what keeps them up at night, they won't talk about "policy." They'll talk about the new Flock camera on the corner of their street, watching them come and go. They'll talk about the AI data centers eating up the land, turning the Florida they love into a grid of concrete warehouses and Big Brother eyes. They might not know the intricate laws, but they can read the headlines. They see the water disappearing and the cameras multiplying, and they rush out to stand in opposition. I've seen it with my own eyes. Liberals and conservatives. Boomers and zoomers. A seventy-year-old man and a twenty-year-old girl, seated side-by-side in a city meeting, staring at the council with the same look of a trust betrayed. And then, standing side-by-side in the streets in protest. On the other hand, there are the establishment voters--people who would never call themselves that, but who are well acquainted with the secret handshakes and the backroom deals. For those voices, the talk dropped to a whisper, and I leaned in close to catch the truth. While they are voicing discontent, they are not willing to depart from whoever ends up winning the nomination for one reason: they will not vote Democrat. Meanwhile, the Grand Old Party, with the Trump presidency coming to an end, twists and turns, vying for control over its own future. The questions that still hang in the air, whether in a corner booth or a city council chamber, are these: why did their candidates not win? There were certainly enough candidates decrying these "evils." Was it a lack of funding? Name recognition? Or is this just the temper tantrum of a few disgruntled voters and young adults afraid of losing their chance to make a mark in history? Will the candidates in the general election be able or willing to fight the powerful AI data and surveillance donors? Or will they justify these as necessary security measures to deter and catch criminals? In the end, we are left with a choice. Do we prioritize a unified front for the sake of strength, or do we remain true to a conscience that may lead us in a different direction? The first sip has been tasted. The subsequent sips, culminating on the 3rd of November, will reveal the rest. Your voice is your crown. I'm a combat veteran. A God-fearing Christian. A husband & a proud dad.
