There is perhaps no clearer admission of institutional failure than paying students simply to show up. Yet that is precisely what the Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has begun doing on an industrial scale. High school students can now earn $100 per week in Visa gift cards for perfect attendance, while middle schoolers collect $50 weekly for the same feat (age discrimination class action lawsuit, anyone?).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eb169eec-2d28-4f9b-95fa-3e5283e5e8c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The district is expanding this program after a pilot run in early 2026 during which roughly 12,800 high schoolers--nearly 84% of the enrollment--received at least one payment. Chronic absenteeism among high school students did drop, from 64% to 54%, but when a school system must resort to cash incentives for basic attendance, the crisis runs far deeper than empty seats.
Detroit's academic results tell the story behind the absenteeism. For years, DPSCD has ranked among the lowest-performing urban districts in the nation. While district officials recently pointed to growth gains outpacing state averages in some grades, proficiency rates remain catastrophically low. Students aren't skipping class because they lack $100 gift cards; they are disengaged from a system that has consistently failed to teach them. When families see schools producing abysmal outcomes regardless of attendance, the incentive to send a child every morning evaporates. The district's response--paying for presence rather than improving proficiency--treats a symptom while the disease of educational failure festers.
Compounding the academic rot is a pension crisis that has financially hollowed out the system. DPSCD alone was carrying an estimated $1.2 billion in unfunded pension liabilities as of 2014, and the statewide Michigan Public School Employees' Retirement System faces tens of billions in shortfalls. Pension debt payments consumed roughly 27% of Detroit's per-pupil foundation grant, diverting funds away from classrooms and toward obligations created by decades of poor fiscal management. A system that spends its money on past promises cannot adequately invest in present instructional quality. Teachers face a system that is simultaneously broke and broken; students sit in classrooms starved of resources because the books are already balanced against retiree checks.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cd16717c-9a86-441c-bc8a-d77e5b799bab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The collapse of morale within Detroit Public Schools is fueled by a glaring financial hypocrisy: while the district's top superintendent commands one of the highest administrative salaries in the state, veteran teachers--who are the actual frontline educators--remain near the bottom of Michigan's pay scale despite recent modest raises that barely keep pace with inflation. This pay hierarchy signals to teachers that the system values bureaucratic leadership over classroom instruction, breeding resentment and accelerating turnover among exhausted staff who already face impossible conditions. Those conditions are made worse by a climate of violence and disorder that has plagued Detroit campuses for years, with assaults, weapons incidents, and general lawlessness pushing many students and teachers toward the exits. When educators are underpaid relative to administrators and simultaneously fearing for their physical safety, the classroom ceases to be a place of learning and becomes a war zone nobody wants to enter--making the district's cash-for-attendance scheme look less like innovation and more like hush money for a system that has already failed the people inside it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/02d12c73-ca51-477c-a458-7bdb138d8ce4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The attendance bribery, then, is not a creative solution but a desperate one. The It was just last year that the Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) investigated a fraud and theft scheme tied to its "Perfect Attendance Pays" program.
It suggests a district that has lost the ability to compel attendance through competence. When a public institution has to pay its customers to use its services, it ceases to be an institution of learning and becomes a transactional operation. The gift cards may fill seats on paper, but they cannot replace the credibility Detroit Public Schools have forfeited through years of failing scores and crushing pension debts. A student paid to sit in a classroom is still owed an education--and Detroit has not yet shown it can deliver one.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: President Trump just stepped off the stage
body:
He told a lot of lies – about me, my record and the grassroots movement we’re building.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1371&source=&t=1&akid=3614%2E124072%2EuVvYpP) | | | |
---
Peter,
President Trump just stepped off the stage in North Carolina after flying down for a rally in support of my GOP opponent, Michael Whatley.
He told that crowd a lot of lies – about me, my record and the grassroots movement we’re building and, maybe most offensively, about North Carolina being “one of the worst states” in the nation. Finally, he begged voters to pretend he was on the ballot in a last-ditch effort to turn out the vote against me.
**I know I’m getting tired of this, and I’m sure you are too, but we can’t let up now.**
Thanks to grassroots supporters like you, we’ve had the resources to fight back against the false attacks I’ve had to face thus far in the race. For that, I’m so grateful – **but we’re still falling behind on the $100,000 rapid-response goal my team set this morning. We’re tracking donations coming in from this email at this link:** [**_https:/ /secure.actblue.com/donate/cooperemail_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1371&amount=5&t=8&akid=3614%2E124072%2EuVvYpP)

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139335341/647014525/2110272206?amount=25&refcode=260916em_rb_pc&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNDJkNTIzZi1mYmIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=yU08znSyg5zQOh9MStXUZIgyUD2dns9l9u3DYjcPIno=)
---
Let me tell you why I’m suing:

**The Trump administration rolled out a new rule that gives immigration officers practically unlimited discretion to deny someone a green card because they or their family members used — _at any time, for any reason_ — a public benefit program like food assistance or Medicaid.**

_The cruelty of this administration knows no bounds._

This policy is clearly designed to force immigrant families to forego healthcare and food assistance out of fear that using those public benefits could jeopardize their immigration status.

_Not only is this policy cruel, but it’s illegal, too._

So on behalf of the millions of immigrants who call California home, we’re taking the Trump administration to court and we will fight tooth and nail to overturn this illegal rule.

---
[_**This is the work your support makes possible, and it gets more important with each passing day, so I have to ask: will you step up and contribute any amount right now to power this movement for justice for all?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139335342/647014526/2110272206?amount=25&refcode=260916em_rb_pc&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNDJkNTIzZi1mYmIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=yU08znSyg5zQOh9MStXUZIgyUD2dns9l9u3DYjcPIno=)

---
[ CONTRIBUTE NOW ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139335343/647014527/2110272206?amount=25&refcode=260916em_rb_pc&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNDJkNTIzZi1mYmIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=yU08znSyg5zQOh9MStXUZIgyUD2dns9l9u3DYjcPIno=)
---
When you tell families that getting help with groceries, healthcare, or rent can be used against them in an immigration decision, people will stop getting the help they need.

We know, because we’ve seen this before: during the first Trump administration, 1 in 4 low-income immigrant adults in California stayed away from public programs because they feared what using them could mean for their immigration status — and it wasn’t just people seeking lawful residency. _Among those who stayed away, nearly half were already U.S. citizens or green card holders._ That’s what the fear and confusion this administration is purposely sowing does — it drives people away from the help they’re legally entitled to.

**The sad reality is that this rule is just the latest move in Trump’s endless, inhumane, and often unlawful anti-immigrant campaign — but it is a rule and a campaign we will continue to fight, with the law on our side.**

More to come. Thank you for being here.

—Rob

Tonight I'll be on stage at the **League of Women Voters candidate forum for Wisconsin's 6th District** , and I'd like you to be part of it. **The details:**
Wednesday, September 16, 7:00 PM
Ripon City Hall, Council Chambers
100 Jackson St., Ripon
Free and open to the public **Can't make it to Ripon?**
Watch it live on the Ripon YouTube channel: [https://youtube.com/@riponchannel](https://thurowforcongress.nationbuilder.com/r?u=KhXGFq3MNw96I5AcmJxbExlj-06onfu8BvQAuJ8tqv5lQsBAmnO80Z8qx-i-f-8c&e=059d48e40c70f813f03bf4261f6eb4fa&utm_source=thurowforcongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=lwv_riponforum&n=2).
Spectrum users can find it on Ripon channel 986. The League runs these straight down the middle. Audience members write the questions, and every candidate answers the same ones. **It is your chance to size us up side by side and decide for yourself** who is actually going to show up for this district. I will be there, because showing up is the job. Come see it in person, or tune in, and bring your questions. See you tonight, Mike P.S. **_Forward this to a neighbor in the district who is still deciding. The best way to reach people is one to one._**
---
* * *
---
**Want to help us win this?** This campaign runs on people, not corporate PAC money. If you can give a few hours, we need volunteers to knock doors, make calls, and talk to neighbors, [sign up here](https://thurowforcongress.nationbuilder.com/volunteer?e=059d48e40c70f813f03bf4261f6eb4fa&utm_source=thurowforcongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=lwv_riponforum&n=3 "Volunteer link"). And if you are able to chip in, every dollar goes straight into reaching voters, the doors we knock and the calls we make, because an independent has no party machine behind us. [Donate here](https://thurowforcongress.nationbuilder.com/r?u=LAw6Hqp82is5wS3lRmYKfNtaA3VE-DPqqvUuA_if5wI2IG25mhKj2DaByNxv0KHl&e=059d48e40c70f813f03bf4261f6eb4fa&utm_source=thurowforcongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=lwv_riponforum&n=4 "Donate").

| | | **Oregon pioneered vote-by-mail 25 years ago. This year alone, President Donald Trump has tried to dismantle it three separate times. Three times, he's lost.****As Oregon's Secretary of State, here's what I know:****this isn't over.**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139335896/647016171/-569431239?refcode=260916-over&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4YzQxN2JiMC1mY2IxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lc0FJFbzmL9qOCxrrNwRVSpbDJmUxmFfgK7kcPqjqoY=)
---
**Trump's own Attorney General admitted it out loud — after losing at the Supreme Court, his words were,****_"We're not going to stop the work that we're doing."_****That means we can’t stop the work we have been doing either.** Every Oregonian needs to know their ballot is safe and their vote will count — no matter how many more times this administration tries to sow doubt. That takes resources to communicate directly with voters and cut through the noise. **[That's why I'm asking you to chip in to my campaign today to help fund this work.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139335897/647016172/-569431239?refcode=260916-over&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4YzQxN2JiMC1mY2IxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lc0FJFbzmL9qOCxrrNwRVSpbDJmUxmFfgK7kcPqjqoY=)**

body:
No family should go through what ours did | | | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139336217/647016933/2141984067?sourceid=1151587&utm_campaign=27emage-0903aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MTI0MmE1My1mZGIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0xS_SlJJ9oYP-5jQ0ZCxnAZ0XrmQEX869YMrbhdNWpA=&emci=a0e7bc81-44b1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=81242a53-fdb1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237) | | [DONATE](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139336218/647016934/2141984067?sourceid=1151587&utm_campaign=27emage-0903aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MTI0MmE1My1mZGIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0xS_SlJJ9oYP-5jQ0ZCxnAZ0XrmQEX869YMrbhdNWpA=&emci=a0e7bc81-44b1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=81242a53-fdb1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237)

| _As a Center for Reproductive Rights supporter, we're honored to share this critical case update about our work directly from one of our plaintiffs. Thank you for being involved in this fight._ Dear Peter,

When we found out about our baby's fatal diagnosis, it was the worst day of my life.

[Little did I know that, due to the laws in my home state of Oklahoma, that awful day would turn into having to flee the state to access care while experiencing this tragic loss.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139336219/647016935/1134457483?sourceid=1151587&utm_campaign=27emage-0903aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MTI0MmE1My1mZGIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0xS_SlJJ9oYP-5jQ0ZCxnAZ0XrmQEX869YMrbhdNWpA=&emci=a0e7bc81-44b1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=81242a53-fdb1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237)

After years of struggling with infertility, I had finally become pregnant with our second child. But at my 19-week scan, we received devastating news.

My baby's brain and skull were not developing. It was a fatal diagnosis.

[I had two options. I could leave the state to get medical care. Or I could stay in Oklahoma, carry to term, and watch my baby die an agonizing death.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139336220/647016936/1134457483?sourceid=1151587&utm_campaign=27emage-0903aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MTI0MmE1My1mZGIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0xS_SlJJ9oYP-5jQ0ZCxnAZ0XrmQEX869YMrbhdNWpA=&emci=a0e7bc81-44b1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=81242a53-fdb1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237)

For my family and me, the choice was clear. I needed an abortion.

The doctors knew the care I needed, but the state of Oklahoma disagreed. My husband and I had to travel 600+ miles to New Mexico so I could receive basic health care.

All I remember is feeling numb, hiding out on the uncomfortable hotel bed. My husband was right there, supporting me every step of the way. But I was so far from home and felt so alone, like I was on an island.

[No one should have to go through what my family went through. That's why, today, I'm suing the state of Oklahoma with the help of the Center for Reproductive Rights. ](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139336221/647016937/1134457483?sourceid=1151587&utm_campaign=27emage-0903aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MTI0MmE1My1mZGIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0xS_SlJJ9oYP-5jQ0ZCxnAZ0XrmQEX869YMrbhdNWpA=&emci=a0e7bc81-44b1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=81242a53-fdb1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237)

This case is about expanding access to critical care that so many people desperately need. It's about making sure that when another family receives news like mine did, they can receive care from their own doctor in their own communities, instead of being forced to pack a bag and leave the people they love behind.

Even in the midst of tragedy, I experienced moments of kindness. I remember the UPS driver who hand-delivered my baby's ashes, telling me: "I couldn't just leave this on your doorstep."

[I think about that kindness a lot. I wish my own state had given me the same basic decency.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139336222/647016938/1134457483?sourceid=1151587&utm_campaign=27emage-0903aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MTI0MmE1My1mZGIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0xS_SlJJ9oYP-5jQ0ZCxnAZ0XrmQEX869YMrbhdNWpA=&emci=a0e7bc81-44b1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=81242a53-fdb1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237)

I was born and raised in Oklahoma, and I've built my life here. I don't want to leave. I want this state to be better — for my girls and for every family who comes after us. And I’m willing to fight for it.

In gratitude,

Magon Hoffman | [Donate Now](https://click.everyaction.com/k/139336223/647016939/1134457483?sourceid=1151587&utm_campaign=27emage-0903aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=oklahoma&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MTI0MmE1My1mZGIxLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0xS_SlJJ9oYP-5jQ0ZCxnAZ0XrmQEX869YMrbhdNWpA=&emci=a0e7bc81-44b1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=81242a53-fdb1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=954237)

Rogers is a corporate shill who dodges debates and would be nothing more than an errand boy for Trump. We’re fighting to get money out of politics, put more money in your pocket, and pass Medicare for All. Peter, we can't do any of that without your support. Grassroots donations power our campaign, and they're the only way we'll beat a $70 million opposition this November. Last month, I took the debate stage against Doris Matsui -- and one moment has stuck with me ever since.

I looked Doris Matsui in the eye and asked her about the money her campaign takes from ICE contractors -- companies that profit from detaining and deporting our neighbors.

Her response?

_"I don't even know what companies you're talking about right now."_

Read that again. A member of Congress who has represented this region for 21 years told a room full of voters she doesn't know who is funding her own campaign.

At best, it's a stunning lack of accountability. At worst, it isn't true. I'll let you decide which is more troubling.

Doris Matsui voted, again and again, for spending packages that funneled billions to ICE. That's her record. And when you take money from the contractors who cash in on that system, you don't get to plead ignorance about it — not when families in our community are living in fear of a knock at the door.

I said something on that stage I believe with everything I have: it's really important to know who actually funds your campaign.

**I know exactly who funds mine. It's you.**

It's working families across CA-07 chipping in what they can. I have never taken a dime from corporate PACs, and I never will — because I answer to this community, and no one else.

Friend — you may have seen this disappointing bit of pop culture news.
**But this story is about way more than rappers, concerts, and stadiums.**
For the last three years, the political, business, and media establishment has worked to silence and punish anyone who speaks out against Israel’s genocide and occupation, and for the freedom and dignity of Palestinians.
We saw it when the 2024 campus protests were violently dismantled, and nonviolent protesters were either kicked out of school or, in some cases, charged with crimes.
We saw it when Trump used DHS and ICE to round up legal residents who have spoken out against Israel’s genocide and put them in illegal indefinite detention.
We saw it when countless actors, musicians, writers, journalists, activists, and more were blacklisted — and many regular people fired from their jobs — for telling the truth and speaking their conscience.
And we saw it when 38 states passed bills or executive orders designed to discourage or penalize boycotts of Israel and its occupation.
**The establishment in the US has decided to crack down on free speech, First Amendment be damned.**
And the reason why is clear: The more people speak out, the more people shine a light on what is happening in Gaza, the West Bank, and Lebanon, the more people learn the truth about the atrocities committed. The establishment has decided it’s better to crack down than to admit that Israel has gone too far, and that it’s time to rethink the US’s relationship.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: The GOP’s strategy is working
body:
Peter, I need you today.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1518&source=&t=1&akid=3589%2E124072%2Ew9avDT) | | | |

Peter, President Trump has set his sights on defeating me in North Carolina, and he’s not backing down.
Just last week, President Trump’s super PAC started flooding this race with millions of dollars, bringing total Republican ad spending to more than $100 million. Their war chest is being used to spread lies about me on the airwaves and prop up my MAGA opponent, Michael Whatley.
**The GOP’s attacks have been relentless, and their strategy is working:** A recent poll shows that our narrow lead has been _cut in half_ with just weeks to go until the election.
**However, President Trump isn’t stopping there. He’s coming to North Carolina TODAY for a massive rally with Whatley – and his visit will give a green light to MAGA megadonors across the country to pour millions more into this race to help the GOP keep this seat and the Senate in their hands.**
The only way I can fight back is with your immediate grassroots support. If we don’t have the resources to stay competitive with the GOP at this very moment, we will continue to lose ground – in the race that experts say could decide Senate control.
[**_Please, Peter, I need you. Will you make a well-timed donation of $5 or any amount right now to help me flip North Carolina and retake the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1518&amount=5&t=8&akid=3589%2E124072%2Ew9avDT)

name: Shelly Arnoldi
subject: Campaign Update: Yard Signs are here & Forum Video is Coming Soon
body:
A quick note of gratitude — and a simple way to help spread the word
| | | | |
---

---
|

---
| |
---
| Dear Fairfax County Friends and Neighbors,
I am asking you to help me stay in this fight! Virginia's 8th District is treated like a locked office. Parents, veterans, federal workers, and small-business owners still live here. They still pay the bills. Their voices still belong on that ballot.
I am a Navy veteran, an engineer, and a Fairfax mom. I did not come out of a party machine. I came out of school closures, mandates, wasted tax dollars, and a government that stopped answering to the people it serves. I am running so this district is not written off before anyone knocks on a door.Donations keep this campaign on the ground: reaching voters, printing materials, getting to forums, and making sure CD-8 hears something other than the usual script.
I will not send our money overseas to fund foreign wars. I will not treat abortion as health care. I will not let schools shut parents out. I will fight for term limits, honest elections, and a government that lives within its means.If you can give $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can spare, or even just put up a sign! do it now. The seat is expensive. The voices in this district are worth it.Stand with me so CD-8 is heard.

I am running this campaign as a true grassroots effort, without paying for traditional campaign services, so any help you can provide means a great deal. Whether that means displaying a sign, volunteering, sharing information with friends and neighbors, or helping spread the word online, every bit of support helps us reach more voters across Congressional District 8. Thank you again for your encouragement and support.
I am grateful to have so many people standing with me in this next phase of the campaign.
With gratitude,
Shelly Arnoldi Libertarian | Virginia's 8th Congressional District shellyarnoldi4va.org 202-285-7474

I won’t sugarcoat it, Peter.

We’re less than 50 days out from the midterms. This is it. This is the
final stretch, and we can’t afford to stumble for even a second if we’re
going to win in November.

From here on out, we’re laser focused on flipping critical seats from red
to blue and electing leaders with real integrity who will put a check on
Trump’s anti-democracy agenda.

I’ve spent the last few months on the road with our candidates — at
community events, fundraisers, and on the doors. I can tell you firsthand:
they have what it takes. Seriously, these are districts we can really
flip. Real, flippable seats in states where just one more fearless leader
could send the GOP supermajority spinning.

That is the power of our work and this grassroots team. But these races
are going to be decided by the resources we can put behind each of our
candidates. How long they can keep their ads on the air, how many more
doors they can knock, and how strong their digital programs are. That’s
why I really need your support right now.

If you’ve been waiting for a good moment to chip in, this is the time. And

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Greg Abbott is facing the most challenging election of his career
body:
Read what I have to say about the New York Times publishing a story on our campaign.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
The _New York Times_ just published a major story on our campaign for Texas Governor, highlighting that we can win this November.
**We’re closer to beating Greg Abbott than _anyone_ thought possible.** The _New York Times_ knows it, national outlets are reporting on it, and political analysts across the country are confirming the undeniable shift happening right here in Texas. But turning this into a victory will require us to show up in full force over these next 7 weeks.
**[Will you chip in $5 right now so we can hit the ground running across Texas during these critical final 48 days?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260916_2_nyt.R6otjL&refcode=em20260916-2136&amount=5&t=1&akid=2136%2E299639%2Ewlw1UJ)**
[****](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260916_2_nyt.R6otjL&refcode=em20260916-2136&amount=5&t=2&akid=2136%2E299639%2Ewlw1UJ)
When I first looked at this election, the conventional wisdom was that _no one_ could beat Greg Abbott, and no other Democrat was stepping up to run.
**But I looked at what was happening in our state and decided I needed to try. I had to fight for Texas.** And now, together, we’re going to prove everyone wrong this fall, and we’re going to beat Greg Abbott.
But right now he’s outspent us more than 10-to-1 – and he’s spending so much because he knows he’s at risk of losing. He knows that his 12 years as governor of Texas are up, so he’s using everything at his disposal to disempower our movement with culture war ads and attacks on social media.
_I can’t stress this enough_ — **we don’t need to match his millions, Peter.** We just need enough resources to reach voters on the ground and through ads to make sure that my message isn’t drowned out by Abbott’s lies.
**[Peter, will you please make a donation of $5 today to keep our momentum going, reach every voter in Texas, and win this race in the 7 weeks we have left.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260916_2_nyt.R6otjL&refcode=em20260916-2136&amount=5&t=3&akid=2136%2E299639%2Ewlw1UJ)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260916_2_nyt.R6otjL&amount=5&refcode=em20260916-2136&t=22&akid=2136%2E299639%2Ewlw1UJ)
Thank you,
Gina

name: Bradstock Campaign
subject: Join Alan’s Mon Valley Barnstorming Tour This Saturday
body:
| |
---
Dear Friend, This Saturday, September 19, Alan Bradstock is hitting the road for a full day of events across the Mon Valley -- and we want you to join us! From Belle Vernon to Monongahela to Alan's hometown of Donora, we'll be meeting voters, talking with neighbors, knocking doors, marching in a parade, and building the grassroots campaign we need to win in November. **Join us for one stop -- or spend the day barnstorming with Alan!**
### 10:00 AM -- Belle Vernon Rally

I was so proud to campaign alongside Elaine during my 2018 Senate re-election race, when she was running for Congress for the first time. That year, Virginia ushered in a massive blue wave and helped flip the House, thanks in large part to Elaine’s great victory flipping Virginia’s 2nd Congressional District blue. I was even prouder to have Elaine as a partner in the Virginia congressional delegation, where she accomplished so much — from cutting prescription drug costs and lowering ACA premiums to helping get the largest expansion of veterans benefits in our lifetimes across the finish line. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. _They're right_ -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, **Lincoln Media Foundation** was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. _That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation._ They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the _first place._ I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and **[every dollar you give to LMF goes directly toward keeping reporters like me in the field](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=0a0fdde9f4ea4b59bc46c2f8d76128e5&_e=KF3bqGiXAL9HZCmHunDoUG5sbCT4iwhtw62NF8r6LnFtw0kg86M7rl9A-fw3L7udVfgu8Q_LlzcIvUq42_QrKmPexGmFgmNXdkafTH7Y1sJiguJx807bMHhFWU81UHE1UfADrSqPODwMEnIlWNzcF5wqFPzdeUsXUWRx5RdRw9B5HDLAMYh0g5rwGPGhRe7NV1dPGx_lzmR2OAI_VD01-dqR2jqODT6R8aI4zF46guASonovQvXrQIw0rwMiY_P0n0GROM2SSH_aEv1EzsnivOuI1p-FYcbA2OBWPgCgqfdLo5QYcpdffJFEA_b8Gnt9B1ivrAPyBZZcMRo3stBp_I7zVizG7GAaLyytokE2h9r0yVQBwrwDYwdvdydo0oB5LxctpYwqtur0iTP0xvGEAd_nHdAaaOkfL1gD0_2DulHWweRyaYSx8rIoP4RSMZMzbRuzPyTk3yygmjDTY6eoQOCtDZcNDa0cgWIoEBc7W6htle_rkvaXoAfyqllvWd06BVwG1uuomQHdcPd7Fi0MK2GslgLvAWTy6CssW6mLDGbakYX_Gz2p6BvVSCPa0MIXJ0IbXhXjLeyLt8IDZqx_iQwCxjhGs14pvJs-Uz-PkU1saXtGIMk5096Qz3abCvnUWoXoM44EzWMebYah2UGtCKZD3IFnzeliK9qZYRYdcBahsKt1GtM4BFbqjUy_O1cSP2OZ4dX_dDUAycm5vEABIdA_94K8R2Y7DFwezMubj8aZUpGBt9tdhYgdnG11HYDY)** - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them.

clean_body: The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Friend, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Friend: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Friend. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Just three days after a statue honoring the late Charlie Kirk was unveiled at Turning Point USA's headquarters in Phoenix, it was defaced. On the morning of Sunday, September 13, the 8-foot bronze statue was spray painted red, mocking Kirk's assassination. Offenders also targeted his eyes, 'Freedom' shirt, and MAGA hat with huge splotches of horrific red paint. They also targeted a sign at the base of the statue, which read "Jesus defeated death so you can live." They scratched out "Jesus" and replaced it with "Satan."

Defacing the statue of Charlie Kirk isn't merely an act of graffiti. It's part of a long, evil pattern of violence. The left didn't mourn the death of Kirk, they celebrated it. They condoned it.

In August, HHS released a **[report](https://substack.com/redirect/87a1b9a2-9857-420d-99e3-933cf35ca1c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** confirming what everyone already knew: There is a link between radical ideologies, like transgenderism, and left-wing violence. The report stated that those who engaged with gender ideology had "positively associated with justification of political violence across six targets: killing Charlie Kirk, killing Donald Trump, killing Brian Thompson, arson of ICE buildings, damaging wealthy people's property, and violence against police."
Polling has shown that a rising number of Americans who identify as left-wing will justify political violence. A **[Network Contagion Region Institute Poll](https://substack.com/redirect/4c64204b-5ec4-468b-adf4-b8146bb18774?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** found that 55% of left-of-center respondents believed it was at least "somewhat justified" to murder President Trump. About 15% of those left-of-center respondents also claimed that murdering President Trump was "completely justified." Those on the left-of-center also had a greater likelihood of justifying the vandalization of a Tesla dealership, using BlueSky, and feeling powerless.
The NCRI poll also found that many on the left supported Luigi Mangione, the alleged assassin of Brian Thompson. Mangione has earned substantial support from radicals online, being praised as a vigilante hero. Under the guise of memes and "jokes," militant assassination culture has become a real threat.

The past decade has been brimming with violence masquerading as protest. From BLM riots to the tearing down of American statues, the severity of the attacks have only increased. The grotesque 'assassination culture' hasn't been warded off, but has become a form of social currency, especially online. The vandalization of Kirk's statue is proof that, even a year after his murder, radical leftists still find joy in that tragedy.
Turning Point isn't backing down, though. The organization says it has surveillance systems which will help authorities capture those suspected of defacing the Kirk statue. TPUSA's CEO Erika Kirk addressed the attack, saying "Charlie once said we should be building two statues for every statue that they tear down."
She continued, "They thought a bullet would silence my husband's voice but it only made it louder. They think spray paint can obscure his legacy, but it will only spread it further. Every attempt to tear down what Charlie built makes us root deeper and work even harder."

Daniel Tatlow-Devally, Leandra Rollo, Vi Kovarbasic, Crow Tricks, and Zo Hailu, known as the "Ulm 5," are shown behind bulletproof glass at their trial in Stuttgart, Germany for allegedly vandalizing an Elbit Systems factory in the German city of Ulm. Photo by Hebh Jamal for Drop Site News.
STUTTGART, Germany--Nearly fifty years after the infamous Red Army Faction trials, Germany's maximum-security Stammheim Prison is once again the setting of a high-profile case that calls into question the conduct of the German state. This time, however, the defendants are five international pro-Palestinian activists charged with vandalizing a factory in the German city of Ulm owned by Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems.
On September 8, 2025, the five Berlin-based activists, now known as the Ulm 5, broke into Elbit's facility and carried out acts of vandalism that they recorded using body cameras and posted online. They destroyed equipment and spray painted "free Palestine" and "baby killers" on the walls. In their videos, the activists--citizens of Britain, Ireland, Spain, and Germany--[say](https://substack.com/redirect/faddcad8-0265-428f-854d-37460df3b801?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) they carried out their direct action "to dismantle the tools used to commit genocide in Gaza" and to call attention to Germany's complicity with it.
No one was injured in the action, which allegedly caused €1.04 million in damages, and the protesters remained at the scene to be arrested. Even so, German prosecutors have clearly decided to treat the Ulm 5 with unusual severity, charging them with membership in a criminal organization, Palestine Action Germany, in addition to trespassing and criminal damage. An additional charge concerns the use of "symbols of an unconstitutional or terrorist organisation"--referring to Hamas--based on the defendants' use of slogans including "From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free."
The courtroom itself has been staged for maximum drama, as if the proceedings concerned dangerous criminals rather than nonviolent protesters. The five defendants sit behind a double layer of bulletproof glass that separates them from both their legal team and the public gallery.
Members of the public and press sit behind another layer of bulletproof glass and must pass through an intense security process that includes an invasive pat down behind closed doors. Only accredited journalists may bring writing utensils into the court room, since pens and pencils could be used as "slash and stab weapons," according to the judge and prosecutor. Heavily armed security personnel stand watch.
Lynn Boylan, an Irish member of the European Parliament who chairs that body's Delegation for Relations with Palestine, described the security theater surrounding the case as a "show trial."
"I initially thought the parents of the Ulm 5 were simply exaggerating because they're not used to the German court system, but what I experienced on this parliamentary trip really shocked me," Boylan told Drop Site. "We were not allowed to bring in a pen and paper and take our own notes," Boylan said, adding that she had to ask permission to take a handkerchief into the courtroom.
"My colleagues visited the Irish citizen, Daniel Tatlow-Devally, in prison and they were concerned with the mind games that the prison staff were playing with Daniel," Boylan said. "Daniel is incarcerated for 23 hours a day in what is essentially solitary confinement and that can have a serious impact on a person's mental health. It is completely unnecessary. Daniel and the four others--they're not violent criminals, and yet they're being treated as if they are the worst of the worst offenders in a prison system. They should be out on bail."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a3ec232d-1adc-4563-a1f1-53a78d93ef70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Activists rally in Stuttgart, Germany before the start of the trial against five pro-Palestine activists, known as the Ulm 5, accused of vandalizing an Elbit Systems factory in Ulm, Germany. Photo by Julian Rettig/picture alliance via Getty Images.
## Precriminalization
The logistics of the case seem calculated to impose hardship on the activists, four of whom are not German citizens. Tatlow-Devally and the other four defendants--Zo Hailu and Crow Tricks from Britain, Spain's Leandra Valenzuela, and Vi Kovarbasic, from Germany--are being held in five different prisons and are not allowed to communicate with one another. They receive a single hour of visitation per month that is heavily monitored and accompanied by translators and prison guards. Families and loved ones are not allowed to talk about the case during their visits.
The trial was initially scheduled to take place over 16 hearings spanning approximately three and a half months. In mid-May, however, shortly after proceedings began, the presiding judge, Katherin Lauchstadt, unilaterally added an additional 28 hearing dates extending into January 2027.
Lauchstadt rejected a Drop Site request to interview the five defendants in prison, arguing that doing so would help spread information between the defendants and would therefore interfere with the trial.
On April 27, the first day of the trial, the five defendants entered in handcuffs and were seated separately from their lawyers behind the bulletproof barrier. The arrangement immediately triggered a confrontation. The 11-member defense team refused to take their seats, demanding that their clients be brought forward so they could communicate with them directly and confidentially.
A chaotic standoff between the court and the defense ensued as the lawyers repeatedly attempted to challenge the seating arrangement and raise procedural motions, while the judge refused to give them the floor, and eventually turned off their microphones. The legal team all left the courtroom at that point in protest, prompting a two hour recess.
Attorney Nina Oner, who represents Zo Hailu, described to Drop Site News how the courtroom itself contributed to the breakdown in proceedings. Unlike in a conventional courtroom where lawyers can address the judge directly, the Stammheim facility requires lawyers to press a button to request permission to speak, after which the court must activate their microphones. On the first day, she said, the court refused to activate the defense microphones at all, preventing the lawyers from formally submitting even a single motion.
"The intention is to build the image of five extremely dangerous individuals that are not allowed to speak to their lawyers freely, even in the breaks," Oner told Drop Site.
Among the motions the defense sought to file was a motion for recusal, asking the court to remove itself from the case over concerns of bias. Oner stressed that such a motion must be submitted at the appropriate stage of proceedings or the defense can lose its right to raise it later.
"We have never experienced any such a thing that the court won't even let us file our motions," Oner said. With the indictment about to be read, Oner said the defense was left with what it saw as its only remaining option: collectively leaving the courtroom. "Our only chance to stop the indictment from being read and us losing our rights," she said, "was to collectively leave the courtroom as the trial cannot continue without us."
The progress of the trial has been slow. Procedural motions are routinely presented only for the judge to reject nearly every single one with very little or no legal justification, according to the Ulm 5's lawyers. Consistent breaks disrupt the flow of evidence, although sometimes these breaks are called by the legal team due to their inability to speak with their clients and understand their wants while court is in session.
In contrast to some of the Palestine Action cases in the UK, the Ulm 5 have not been charged with terrorism under Section 129a of the German criminal code. Oner said the effort to censor and monitor communication between the defendants and the defense that could apply to terror cases should not apply here.
"We don't have a Section 129a case, and yet these are the measures that the court is pushing through the court house that are even extreme when it is a 129a case," she said.
For comparison, in a Section 129a terrorism trial that's happening at the same time, the defendants--members of the extremist Reichsburger movement accused of attempting to overthrow the German government, who allegedly shot German police officers--are allowed to sit with their defense team, and some have even been released from pre-trial detention.
"This definitely sets a new kind of precedent," Sophia Hoffinger, a monitor project officer at the European Legal Support Center told DropSite. "There are very few comparable prolonged forms of pretrial detention in Section 129 cases."
Hoffinger said that similar charges have been made against members of the climate justice group, Last Generation, for belonging to a criminal organization. Yet "none of the members have been forced under the same conditions as the Ulm 5 defendants," she added. "There's no pretrial detention [in that case] and none of the refusal to allow defendants to consult with their lawyers privately."
Germany's federal domestic intelligence agency has not only [described](https://substack.com/redirect/a78b6ec5-4dd9-4635-bce5-c8f993d5bb9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Ulm 5 as extremists, even before they have been convicted, but also [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/eebdb214-c23b-4085-a3bc-e6e6f571d445?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the legal aid organization 3ezwa of being involved in "prisoner assistance extremism" solely because it has provided support for the trial. Hoffinger described this as a form of "precriminalization."
"Just because a support structure expresses political support for five people who have not been convicted of anything yet and who are still on trial shows the extent of this precriminalization," Hoffinger said. "This is a wider trend that Germany is imposing because of expressed support for Palestine. They have politicized this case by even using their own intelligence agencies to interfere and accelerate the accusations against the defendants because of their economic interests in delegitimizing the Ulm 5," she added.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/da86fe20-dd91-46da-b6ed-cd73fac1fa15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A drone is on display at the Elbit Systems Deutschland booth during the International Aerospace Exhibition at the Berlin ExpoCenter Airport, on June 11, 2026. Photo by Sebastian Christoph Gollnow/picture alliance via Getty Images.
## Elbit and Israel's Genocide
As Israel's largest private arms manufacturer, Elbit Systems has become a frequent [target](https://substack.com/redirect/02bda344-ff35-4da7-900a-8fd8a893b184?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of direct actions and the BDS movement internationally. The company produces a wide range of military equipment--including artillery shells, tank rounds, surveillance equipment, drones, and parts for F-35 jets--many of which have been deployed during the genocide in Gaza.
In Germany, Elbit's subsidiary produces highly specialised components for laser targeting and communications systems.
Political economist Shir Hever, an expert on the Israeli arms industry, said Elbit's factory in Ulm develops laser sensors used for gathering digital information and terrain mapping as well as [software defined radios](https://substack.com/redirect/1f739ed6-94e3-4c38-b25a-d4342d794837?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that serve as the primary communication platform for the Israeli military.
"This is where Germany plays a very important role in the supply chain, as the same radios and sensors manufactured and developed in Ulm" are used in Gaza, Hever said.
Elbit Systems Germany did not respond to a request for comment.
Under the German legal system, the public prosecutor is legally required to investigate both incriminating and potentially exonerating evidence. That has not happened in this case, and the defense argues the prosecution failed to adequately examine evidence that could potentially justify or contextualise the five defendants' actions during the alleged break in. This includes investigating Elbit's complicity in Israel's war crimes in Gaza.
Instead, the prosecutor, Ronny Stengel, alleges the action was motivated by antisemitism, an aggravating factor in Germany. Since the five sprayed "Baby Killers" on the walls of Elbit facility, the prosecution alleges, they contributed to the antisemitic trope of blood libel, since Elbit is a "Jewish-owned company."
On June 19, the seventh trial date, the legal team introduced the Dutch newspaper Der Volksrant's award-winning investigation, "[What the Wounds Are Telling Us,](https://substack.com/redirect/16b0bb5b-13d0-42ee-8ac1-1be513f55a9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" by Maud Effting and Willem Feenstra, detailing evidence that Israeli forces had deliberately targeted the heads and chests of Palestinian children in Gaza. This was done provide context for understanding the motivations of the defendants and how their conduct should be legally evaluated. Instead of allowing the defense to read out the article in English, however, the judge insisted that it be translated verbally into German, creating a dramatic moment during the proceedings as the translators became visibly emotional, choking up as the material was read aloud in court.
The defense's argument ultimately depends on a question: What was the five activists' direct action intended to stop? They argue that Elbit plays a direct role in Israel's genocide in Gaza and that the defendants' vandalism was thus justified.
According to Ihsan Adel, chairperson of Law for Palestine and an attorney working on a case filed before the International Court of Justice (ICJ) by Nicaragua, "Germany has a legal obligation to prevent and punish genocide."
"Proceedings in the Nicaragua case against Germany before the ICJ, together with information available in the public record, indicate that Germany has not taken the measures required under international law to prevent genocide in Gaza," Adel said.
According to a new [report](https://substack.com/redirect/2d868129-943b-41ea-a8df-3a2f12c3521a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) published by Forensis Berlin, Germany approved approximately €1.41 billion in licenses to export military equipment to Israel between October 2023 and June 2026, including €800 million in the first six months of 2026 alone.
The report documents that in 2023 and 2024, Germany ranked first and second respectively among the EU states that reported arms exports to Israel.
Matthias Goldmann, a professor of international law at EBS University, told Drop Site the defendants must meet five conditions for their action to be considered legitimate civil disobedience. The first would be a fundamental interest of the community, such as upholding and respecting international law. The second is that the action was undertaken without regard for their own self-interest, financial, or political gain. The third condition is non-violence, and Goldmann said that "violence begins when people are harmed," and that vandalizing the Elbit Systems factory does not meet the threshold of a violent act. The fourth condition is that the action must attempt to impact or influence political discourse and correct the course of politics.
"We can disagree about what legitimate resistance is, as one man's freedom fighter is another man's terrorist. So to get around that there are criteria," Goldmann said.
The final criterion, Goldmann said, was that the Ulm 5 meet have demonstrated a willingness to accept their punishment, because they waited on site for the authorities to arrest them.
"Constitutional or international law alone is never self-sufficient; a legal order is subject to different criteria than just the state's constitution, so I believe the Ulm 5 does meet the criteria of civil disobedience," Goldmann said.

Crow Tricks' sibling Tessi Tricks told Drop Site how jarring it was for the families to see the defendants treated like dangerous criminals. "The five activists just don't look threatening at all. So it's like this quite confusing experience because you feel like they're getting treated like they could set off a bomb or they could do something really awful, and it's like they're literally just standing there trying to have access to their lawyers, trying to be able to defend themselves. They're being treated way disproportionately to what they've done," Tessi said.

The window is frosted glass and can't be opened, and outside is a concrete yard with no greenery of any kind."
During visits, she said, her son was kept in a glass room and she was unable to hug her child for the five months she visited them. It was only after she involved Richard Boyd Barrett, a member of Ireland's lower house of parliament, that a meeting was arranged with the German ambassador. They had their first touch from a loved one in five months. Daniel had no social contact, no physical contact, and combined that with almost no intellectual contact since they were refused the right to have books sent to them. It's torture if you think about it," Mimi said.

"Each time Crow moves they get very stressed because they don't know who they're going to share a cell with. Last year was quite difficult for Crow when they were threatened by a cellmate. They complained to guards who responded by saying, 'it's not our issue unless we see blood on the ground,'" Tricks said.

Boylan, the Irish member of the European Parliament, said that Germany's violent treatment of the Ulm 5 is part of a wider pattern of violence against Palestinian solidarity.
"I think anybody looking at what Israel is doing to the Palestinian people, you know, cannot deny what they see with their own eyes. So I think that that's part of it that [Germany] have taken this very very heavy-handed approach against all Palestine solidarity," she said. "They want to send a message to the wider public that you know if you do what the Ulm 5 did, there's going to be very heavy consequences."

Photo by Hebh Jamal for Drop Site News. STUTTGART, Germany--Nearly fifty years after the infamous Red Army Faction trials, Germany's maximum-security Stammheim Prison is once again the setting of a high-profile case that calls into question the conduct of the German state. This time, however, the defendants are five international pro-Palestinian activists charged with vandalizing a factory in the German city of Ulm owned by Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems. On September 8, 2025, the five Berlin-based activists, now known as the Ulm 5, broke into Elbit's facility and carried out acts of vandalism that they recorded using body cameras and posted online. They destroyed equipment and spray painted "free Palestine" and "baby killers" on the walls. In their videos, the activists--citizens of Britain, Ireland, Spain, and Germany-- they carried out their direct action "to dismantle the tools used to commit genocide in Gaza" and to call attention to Germany's complicity with it. No one was injured in the action, which allegedly caused €1.04 million in damages, and the protesters remained at the scene to be arrested. Even so, German prosecutors have clearly decided to treat the Ulm 5 with unusual severity, charging them with membership in a criminal organization, Palestine Action Germany, in addition to trespassing and criminal damage. An additional charge concerns the use of "symbols of an unconstitutional or terrorist organisation"--referring to Hamas--based on the defendants' use of slogans including "From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free." The courtroom itself has been staged for maximum drama, as if the proceedings concerned dangerous criminals rather than nonviolent protesters. The five defendants sit behind a double layer of bulletproof glass that separates them from both their legal team and the public gallery. Members of the public and press sit behind another layer of bulletproof glass and must pass through an intense security process that includes an invasive pat down behind closed doors. Only accredited journalists may bring writing utensils into the court room, since pens and pencils could be used as "slash and stab weapons," according to the judge and prosecutor. Heavily armed security personnel stand watch. Lynn Boylan, an Irish member of the European Parliament who chairs that body's Delegation for Relations with Palestine, described the security theater surrounding the case as a "show trial." "I initially thought the parents of the Ulm 5 were simply exaggerating because they're not used to the German court system, but what I experienced on this parliamentary trip really shocked me," Boylan told Drop Site. "We were not allowed to bring in a pen and paper and take our own notes," Boylan said, adding that she had to ask permission to take a handkerchief into the courtroom. "My colleagues visited the Irish citizen, Daniel Tatlow-Devally, in prison and they were concerned with the mind games that the prison staff were playing with Daniel," Boylan said. "Daniel is incarcerated for 23 hours a day in what is essentially solitary confinement and that can have a serious impact on a person's mental health. It is completely unnecessary. Daniel and the four others--they're not violent criminals, and yet they're being treated as if they are the worst of the worst offenders in a prison system. They should be out on bail." | | ---|---|--- Activists rally in Stuttgart, Germany before the start of the trial against five pro-Palestine activists, known as the Ulm 5, accused of vandalizing an Elbit Systems factory in Ulm, Germany. Photo by Julian Rettig/picture alliance via Getty Images. Precriminalization The logistics of the case seem calculated to impose hardship on the activists, four of whom are not German citizens. Tatlow-Devally and the other four defendants--Zo Hailu and Crow Tricks from Britain, Spain's Leandra Valenzuela, and Vi Kovarbasic, from Germany--are being held in five different prisons and are not allowed to communicate with one another. They receive a single hour of visitation per month that is heavily monitored and accompanied by translators and prison guards. Families and loved ones are not allowed to talk about the case during their visits. The trial was initially scheduled to take place over 16 hearings spanning approximately three and a half months. In mid-May, however, shortly after proceedings began, the presiding judge, Katherin Lauchstadt, unilaterally added an additional 28 hearing dates extending into January 2027. Lauchstadt rejected a Drop Site request to interview the five defendants in prison, arguing that doing so would help spread information between the defendants and would therefore interfere with the trial. On April 27, the first day of the trial, the five defendants entered in handcuffs and were seated separately from their lawyers behind the bulletproof barrier. The arrangement immediately triggered a confrontation. The 11-member defense team refused to take their seats, demanding that their clients be brought forward so they could communicate with them directly and confidentially. A chaotic standoff between the court and the defense ensued as the lawyers repeatedly attempted to challenge the seating arrangement and raise procedural motions, while the judge refused to give them the floor, and eventually turned off their microphones. The legal team all left the courtroom at that point in protest, prompting a two hour recess. Attorney Nina Oner, who represents Zo Hailu, described to Drop Site News how the courtroom itself contributed to the breakdown in proceedings. Unlike in a conventional courtroom where lawyers can address the judge directly, the Stammheim facility requires lawyers to press a button to request permission to speak, after which the court must activate their microphones. On the first day, she said, the court refused to activate the defense microphones at all, preventing the lawyers from formally submitting even a single motion. "The intention is to build the image of five extremely dangerous individuals that are not allowed to speak to their lawyers freely, even in the breaks," Oner told Drop Site. Among the motions the defense sought to file was a motion for recusal, asking the court to remove itself from the case over concerns of bias. Oner stressed that such a motion must be submitted at the appropriate stage of proceedings or the defense can lose its right to raise it later. "We have never experienced any such a thing that the court won't even let us file our motions," Oner said. With the indictment about to be read, Oner said the defense was left with what it saw as its only remaining option: collectively leaving the courtroom. "Our only chance to stop the indictment from being read and us losing our rights," she said, "was to collectively leave the courtroom as the trial cannot continue without us." The progress of the trial has been slow. Procedural motions are routinely presented only for the judge to reject nearly every single one with very little or no legal justification, according to the Ulm 5's lawyers. Consistent breaks disrupt the flow of evidence, although sometimes these breaks are called by the legal team due to their inability to speak with their clients and understand their wants while court is in session. In contrast to some of the Palestine Action cases in the UK, the Ulm 5 have not been charged with terrorism under Section 129a of the German criminal code. Oner said the effort to censor and monitor communication between the defendants and the defense that could apply to terror cases should not apply here. "We don't have a Section 129a case, and yet these are the measures that the court is pushing through the court house that are even extreme when it is a 129a case," she said. For comparison, in a Section 129a terrorism trial that's happening at the same time, the defendants--members of the extremist Reichsburger movement accused of attempting to overthrow the German government, who allegedly shot German police officers--are allowed to sit with their defense team, and some have even been released from pre-trial detention. "This definitely sets a new kind of precedent," Sophia Hoffinger, a monitor project officer at the European Legal Support Center told DropSite. "There are very few comparable prolonged forms of pretrial detention in Section 129 cases." Hoffinger said that similar charges have been made against members of the climate justice group, Last Generation, for belonging to a criminal organization. Yet "none of the members have been forced under the same conditions as the Ulm 5 defendants," she added. "There's no pretrial detention [in that case] and none of the refusal to allow defendants to consult with their lawyers privately." Germany's federal domestic intelligence agency has not only the Ulm 5 as extremists, even before they have been convicted, but also the legal aid organization 3ezwa of being involved in "prisoner assistance extremism" solely because it has provided support for the trial. Hoffinger described this as a form of "precriminalization." "Just because a support structure expresses political support for five people who have not been convicted of anything yet and who are still on trial shows the extent of this precriminalization," Hoffinger said. "This is a wider trend that Germany is imposing because of expressed support for Palestine. They have politicized this case by even using their own intelligence agencies to interfere and accelerate the accusations against the defendants because of their economic interests in delegitimizing the Ulm 5," she added. | | ---|---|--- A drone is on display at the Elbit Systems Deutschland booth during the International Aerospace Exhibition at the Berlin ExpoCenter Airport, on June 11, 2026. Photo by Sebastian Christoph Gollnow/picture alliance via Getty Images. Elbit and Israel's Genocide As Israel's largest private arms manufacturer, Elbit Systems has become a frequent of direct actions and the BDS movement internationally. The company produces a wide range of military equipment--including artillery shells, tank rounds, surveillance equipment, drones, and parts for F-35 jets--many of which have been deployed during the genocide in Gaza. In Germany, Elbit's subsidiary produces highly specialised components for laser targeting and communications systems. Political economist Shir Hever, an expert on the Israeli arms industry, said Elbit's factory in Ulm develops laser sensors used for gathering digital information and terrain mapping as well as that serve as the primary communication platform for the Israeli military. "This is where Germany plays a very important role in the supply chain, as the same radios and sensors manufactured and developed in Ulm" are used in Gaza, Hever said. Elbit Systems Germany did not respond to a request for comment. Under the German legal system, the public prosecutor is legally required to investigate both incriminating and potentially exonerating evidence. That has not happened in this case, and the defense argues the prosecution failed to adequately examine evidence that could potentially justify or contextualise the five defendants' actions during the alleged break in. This includes investigating Elbit's complicity in Israel's war crimes in Gaza. Instead, the prosecutor, Ronny Stengel, alleges the action was motivated by antisemitism, an aggravating factor in Germany. Since the five sprayed "Baby Killers" on the walls of Elbit facility, the prosecution alleges, they contributed to the antisemitic trope of blood libel, since Elbit is a "Jewish-owned company." On June 19, the seventh trial date, the legal team introduced the Dutch newspaper Der Volksrant's award-winning investigation, "" by Maud Effting and Willem Feenstra, detailing evidence that Israeli forces had deliberately targeted the heads and chests of Palestinian children in Gaza. This was done provide context for understanding the motivations of the defendants and how their conduct should be legally evaluated. Instead of allowing the defense to read out the article in English, however, the judge insisted that it be translated verbally into German, creating a dramatic moment during the proceedings as the translators became visibly emotional, choking up as the material was read aloud in court. The defense's argument ultimately depends on a question: What was the five activists' direct action intended to stop? They argue that Elbit plays a direct role in Israel's genocide in Gaza and that the defendants' vandalism was thus justified. According to Ihsan Adel, chairperson of Law for Palestine and an attorney working on a case filed before the International Court of Justice (ICJ) by Nicaragua, "Germany has a legal obligation to prevent and punish genocide." "Proceedings in the Nicaragua case against Germany before the ICJ, together with information available in the public record, indicate that Germany has not taken the measures required under international law to prevent genocide in Gaza," Adel said. According to a new published by Forensis Berlin, Germany approved approximately €1.41 billion in licenses to export military equipment to Israel between October 2023 and June 2026, including €800 million in the first six months of 2026 alone. The report documents that in 2023 and 2024, Germany ranked first and second respectively among the EU states that reported arms exports to Israel. Matthias Goldmann, a professor of international law at EBS University, told Drop Site the defendants must meet five conditions for their action to be considered legitimate civil disobedience. The first would be a fundamental interest of the community, such as upholding and respecting international law. The second is that the action was undertaken without regard for their own self-interest, financial, or political gain. The third condition is non-violence, and Goldmann said that "violence begins when people are harmed," and that vandalizing the Elbit Systems factory does not meet the threshold of a violent act. The fourth condition is that the action must attempt to impact or influence political discourse and correct the course of politics. "We can disagree about what legitimate resistance is, as one man's freedom fighter is another man's terrorist. So to get around that there are criteria," Goldmann said. You are receiving this email because at some point, you signed up for updates from me when I was running for Congress. Well, I didn’t make it past the primary, but I DID start a [Substack](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.jTd4CJP2oHMhBHdrjS9uuoqcULmuM8MzW6kC57n8D_Z2TnMJ7SaLXquHDdPbUHtLNhgVQkepnaLuUT83gNzgPC0YLFxNsj7C-MnX0KEnQbV3aqqNiDg-T9dXuBm1Voxp4Vctu1nyjoV4hg5EOcbhoCU-yyGadsoJ0Cv49k8thw38VeQo9yc9eUINcr2yR8urtPZk8Wuzb55bJ6lIppMyU4JWJefMgPf4Fb9xwMf1-CvLIj1TIEotZGHu8QS-YVcQ/4u3/PjTYp7UuRTuOmxnGdunlkQ/h2/h001.2SPGJjdNtTgwgVFSMJatWke1WfmCUvwLG29Rn1wkTX0), and moving forward, I'll be emailing you from there. The idea behind this newsletter is to talk about what we can still do, both the politics and the policies, to turn this country around so it works for everyone and not just a handful of people at the top. **TL;DR:** Since the primary, the question I get most is “what’s next?” The short version: we started **SF Solidarity PAC** to point our people-powered voter contact machine at other progressive races, we launched a [**new democratic club in San Francisco**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.A3cd-kVlFz1CzUMSYeTvVWDHKp0Z9ZKKY0G-0BCDBgMw6yx9tCnreXbSIjyL8K8gir5RWQciTLDCjbkwH-S-LhtFicBMTvgXQMP3jmM7pEvDvHKSB4Ih6_xJca1GMnSW-L9nT1SvOf4l0sUivhLN30ghkYYTISVQmzr1dCYUG2nEpocl8Pt3uEfTwTvc_x2iCRc3r4FXZJl2Ja473dQhkSu_zrMQbVYYPusecz-GXfAGabKM5Om1oB35dX21WJDxd9oq-FQxt2JFnZ3Ie4hRNLmnjQKXBvB7HlOQ98jGLMtx0_cDxDEt2bIW41V-mcmMtMvlgAfYMhc0FkC513d-iDNjggEclNfCATc4q17moLA/4u3/PjTYp7UuRTuOmxnGdunlkQ/h3/h001.dfgMmmwdV5-LTNugd8IwnKR-HP7FEagfpKy8gLAVFk0) organized around policy instead of neighborhood or identity, and I’m going back to [**New Consensus**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.nTQp_FEIcSHl649vCJCicna86wdqoaaqU1KfavwLn5nsQQmEcwZCZA6UJ0piFQagXzv9CuQuu7tiAYQWPwesmWjnbeVa9ipqWXsvK7KW5N4jxLJz-GfVyi-VGJPT4xV1M2F6KVBbgAeYYdqmlyriR7tiP2-U7AaoRDKvsAZ0g_HUThFpnjEp1AtMO0Ocf-7zK-ncQDXBBvjlR6drFAsxj5aIpf2WmkhXH6qgLhjRiRovAgC1kRUj_mpgS8x2gIyY/4u3/PjTYp7UuRTuOmxnGdunlkQ/h4/h001.ZL8eWfHd2VLjlgl1a7SmUaWwzPbEo0ybXLGW9JTaZHc), the think tank I co-founded in 2017, to work on the big economic ideas that the 2028 presidential primary is going to be fought over. This newsletter is where I’ll write about that work. Details on all of it below. Since my unsuccessful run for Congress, the number one question I’ve gotten is: what will you do next? Well, after not sending any updates to you all in about three months, I figured it’s high time to answer that. On June 2, I was of course disappointed by the results, but I don’t regret running. I am incredibly proud of the campaign we ran and especially of the people who volunteered and worked on the campaign. Most of the people who showed up to our canvasses, town halls, and rallies were completely new to politics. We mobilized a whole new electorate in San Francisco, and together, we created an incredibly impressive voter contact program. Part of that was the hard work everyone put in, but a lot of it was the culture of that team. This was honestly the best group of people I’ve ever worked with. Throughout the campaign, I said constantly that it wouldn’t be enough to just elect me to Congress. If we want to pass Medicare-for-all, tax the rich, end corruption in our politics, and wrench control of our government away from the corporations and back into the hands of people, it will take a movement of elected officials working together on the inside, backed by a movement of people supporting them on the outside. That kind of inside-outside organizing has been at the center of every big moment of change in our history, from the New Deal to the civil rights movement. That’s why, at our biggest rally of the campaign, we didn’t just promote our own race. We brought Darializa Avila Chevalier, Melat Kiros, and Angela Gonzales-Torres out here to show the strength of this movement and support their campaigns too: So even though I won’t be part of that movement on the inside, I can still be part of it on the outside. Here’s what that’s looked like so far.
## SF Solidarity PAC
On June 3, the day after the primary, we got to work helping progressives get elected across the country. We started SF Solidarity PAC to point our people-powered voter contact machine at other races. Here in San Francisco, we’ve been knocking doors and making calls for Connie Chan. I ran against Connie in the primary and we have our disagreements, but it was clear to me that in Congress she’ll work with other progressives on the issues I care most about. She takes no corporate money and has been an active fighter against corporate influence in San Francisco. She supports wealth taxes on the ultra-rich. And I’m glad to see she’s come out for an arms embargo on Israel to stop U.S. support of the genocide in Gaza. All told, so far we’ve talked to nearly 40,000 San Franciscans after making about 650,000 phone calls and knocking on about 12,000 doors for her, and we’re continuing to do that work through November. Beyond San Francisco, we’ve been phonebanking for races across the country — sometimes winning, sometimes losing, but doing everything we can. We just wrapped up the last primary of the cycle in Massachusetts, and here’s the final results of what we were able to accomplish: I ran this cycle because I felt we had a huge opportunity to elect a new group of progressives. The moment today reminds me of 2018. Back then, people were furious at the Democratic Party for losing to Trump and were looking for new leaders with a different vision. That moment of change is what allowed us to elect The Squad and push big new ideas like the Green New Deal, which ended up shaping a lot of the Democratic agenda under Biden. But the appetite for change today dwarfs anything I’ve ever seen, and I thought we had a shot at electing a much larger class of fighters willing to work together for a country that works for everyone, not just the wealthy few. That instinct has largely proven right. In 2018 we elected four amazing progressive leaders; this cycle, we’re already well past that. To everyone who worked and volunteered to help get these leaders elected: THANK YOU. You’ve already made a huge difference, and I believe 2026 is going to be remembered as the beginning of huge change in this country.
## A new democratic club in San Francisco
In July, we held a thank-you party for our volunteers and announced a new democratic club in San Francisco. About 200 people showed up. Democratic clubs in San Francisco have real power in shaping the party here. Most clubs in the city are organized around identity or neighborhood (nothing wrong with that, of course!), but we felt the city needed one organized around actual policy. And if the volunteers and staff from our campaign mostly joined, we’d have one of the largest and most powerful clubs in the city. The club is still new. We’ve just elected officers and are meeting now to hammer out the basics: bylaws, values, and endorsements for this cycle. If you live in the Bay Area and want to be part of it, join our Discord server here: | [Join the Discord](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.yjJN_MEbNx94PLaWzZ6hWzLgpY_TbOtf0RP-CQ0QV9QJ2a1l6vsq6evF_KZRrC6i-ctdQHifGrWHz6Gk6W-SXDFzF39Z2T0ZD_rhLmiL6uzOjmmJay4Xeyw0AfB7N0KPX2CiXbkml-PIX3jLM66XcPE8nr9usuh0T5Vm0kc9HP0q1UuuHhg9kuZBFA-AAW8vi4MQ5ALcEcJ7cI-_QT4F4wfpcVNkh1xtaKyMVZcu0hxEg7tPVN267q6QQJ0_syWa/4u3/PjTYp7UuRTuOmxnGdunlkQ/h5/h001.NmUNdsKCxi-WJrko_KuDwSgjNUuHiZ93gunFSAhyJys)
