## Why I’m going back to policy, and the 2028 moment
Looking ahead, I believe the opportunity is huge. A new class of progressive, anti-establishment fighters is headed to Congress, and the truly exciting part — having talked to many of them — is that they want to actually _do_ work together, not just be individual congresspeople. I’m feeling plenty of FOMO not being in there organizing with them, but I plan to support them from the outside and help them lead the fights.
At the same time, the Democratic presidential primary is going to kick off right after November, and it’s going to be a fight over ideas and vision unlike any we’ve seen. After 2016, a lot of Democrats treated Trump as an aberration and assumed there was a “normal” we could go back to. That was much of the case for Joe Biden — the safe, back-to-normal candidate. But Trump winning a second time, and then dismantling so much of our federal government, norms, and institutions, has shown people there is no normal anymore. We have to build something new.
Presidential primaries are the moment when the entire direction of the party can change. That was the whole strategy behind the Green New Deal in 2019. We never intended to “pass” it. The Green New Deal was a resolution outlining _how_ to build a clean economy that would create millions of high-wage jobs. The goal was to force everyone running for president in 2020 to respond with their own ambitious plans and to mainstream ideas like industrial policy. And because of how primaries work, that’s exactly what happened. Every candidate needed to distinguish themselves and push new ideas, and even Joe Biden responded with Build Back Better — a moderate plan that was still bigger than anything a Democratic president had proposed before.
So in 2028, at a moment when everyone is demanding a new vision, the opportunity to pitch big, bold ideas is enormous. That’s why I’m going to focus the bulk of my time on policy and vision at New Consensus.
---
## New Consensus
New Consensus is a think tank I co-founded in 2017. At the time, I was working to recruit candidates to run as Justice Democrats on an agenda that combined the Bernie 2016 platform with a vision for economic development and growth. When we looked around DC for think tanks working on the ideas we were pushing — industrial policy, using the state to build the economy we need — there weren’t any. So we started one.
At New Consensus, we believe there’s a tried-and-true playbook for getting economies unstuck and creating shared prosperity. We last used it in the New Deal and the World War II mobilization to build our industrial economy. And around the world, pretty much every modern developed nation today, from Asia to Europe, has used it as well. And right now, we have an incredible opportunity to put that playbook to work by tackling the massive challenges of today like climate change and AI.
A lot of the early development of the Green New Deal came out of New Consensus, and we’ve been working on a number of projects since, which I’ll cover in future posts. The biggest is the [**Mission for America**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMY23WlHQTrV_FskTHwUteJwz0yLQf7YMu33UgAInjZ_08KqNw6Emhh5Al091qjOqSpFueV4ZpuuL3LGLkdubQY8uE9jwvjhwdf3iSGb4rBqqcQLjY-JVndE8xKWhpO42MBsyQjaVsWIzRW-0KXRli-bRSNqOSiNH3kVrDz-Ie6ayG3beJxn6xnqslR6tJeaEvhgxZlHI03TUBXU7ftIzzU7-XlWc2GH5j0OYnNQevT1ZiGkt893Eb8-simnnTHIyTQ/4u3/PjTYp7UuRTuOmxnGdunlkQ/h6/h001.Jg4McphEL3N8tNWnmKbhYPS2vhQHmwaSAdFTe5GcDRM) — a comprehensive, detailed plan for how exactly we mobilize our economy to build clean alternatives in every sector and create the industries of the future where, frankly, China is kicking our ass.
We also have a [wealth tax plan](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMY23WlHQTrV_FskTHwUteJzSiDWCPp-T3sSZNH0rQfEJ4rmR6MwBnw5MBrfQJaKv3nECQtxmtCA_wgfkBC7m7uHu7A0piV2ksd377sUP1YkfFJu7S4o5Beir8XfU-vnFpNI-HDhObHXzhxaGVraUS_PJ35pBmcdznFuB_VXRLAKlf78si-7tTLcihnfEZGgSJTmZD9J7qnXN-fg-NUcWFAQa0pcX6kTz2DbAS4zNGo_cgYnnSl2Q_rFaanrcIIJmZwzIpSdXcPB7fA1G2CcJDCc/4u3/PjTYp7UuRTuOmxnGdunlkQ/h7/h001.U2TIYNSiHj-BCLk5foA-xm2aqtzrdPUjzlBLIfkRvl8), a [CrashLab](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.EtNV8HBC60Tl7UuGmXS3sVNIvKwZ-uwkCXG2N0uP3-HoKvx6UJs8EatAdW2odjGoPZJN0zlg7rVCfug3soOx62SJf9RH8lucVm48e80EaHbVL05VBTprt06G_xihi75qm1W9ouCTG1IkPeDLVcznrgZ3Wit-SHcuup85L3I1hBZHY4jNvC0qwAPmlU8kxRiuNWOpPvkS9IEBRGXH8dOCq2tJiPQcmAKIgVwyS5ky4_bycTA8905mPPLrtZn7iN75/4u3/PjTYp7UuRTuOmxnGdunlkQ/h8/h001.n7jBEJx3OmDhufW1ue0AoTRCMxyOl-6Jk7GzFfIqh4Y), which monitors how close our economy is to a crash, and we’re working on plans for healthcare, what to do if the AI bubble pops, and a Project 2029 outlining what a Democratic president with a Democratic Congress could do — even without getting rid of the filibuster.
I got into politics because I believe our economy is really stuck, and we need to fundamentally change our politics to change our economy. I’ve always approached this work policy-first. So it’s very exciting to me to be able to go back to dedicating most of my time to the policy. Of course, I’m going to also continue doing everything I can to make sure that policy actually goes somewhere. That means engaging with members of Congress — especially the new group of progressives who are going to be willing to take risks — and continuing to spread these ideas in the media and social media.
So, to that end, I’m going to use this Substack to talk about that work. But I’d also love to hear from you all about what you’d like to read about. So reply to this email to let me know if there’s anything you’d like for me to cover.
Thanks for sticking with me. More soon.

name: Carleigh Beriont
subject: What now?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Carleigh Beriont for Congress
body:
A huge thank you for everyone who stepped up.
A huge thank you for everyone who stepped up.

| |
---
| | Dear David, First, allow me to apologize for not reaching out sooner. Since the election last Tuesday, life has returned somewhat to normal in our house. The kids and Eric have started their school years, we did the laundry that had been piling up for several weeks, and the garden we left untended the last few months got some serious weeding. We also packed up boxes of campaign buttons and stickers and drove around the district taking down signs and storing them away for an unknown future. Meanwhile, we are all hurtling towards an extraordinarily consequential election here in New Hampshire and around the country, and there is important work to be done! As you know, we came up short last week in our campaign to represent New Hampshireʼs First Congressional District in Washington, D.C. I want to congratulate Stefany Shaheen on winning the Democratic nomination. As I told her at the Democratic Unity Breakfast on the day after the primary, she has my full support in her bid to represent us in Washington as our next Congresswoman. Over the next seven weeks, I will do everything in my power to help us win our US House and Senate races, our Governor’s race, our Executive Council seats, and a majority in our State House and Senate. **I want thank the 1200+ absolutely incredible volunteers who knocked over 11,000 doors, made 10,000 phone calls, waved signs, and wrote 35,000 postcards to friends and neighbors.** We built a grassroots movement that brought so many different people together and gave us all a sense of hope, possibility, and power. This is crucial at a time when our politics too often feels depressing, dysfunctional, and disempowering. Our knowledge that we can listen, organize, and build power so that we can bring about the changes we need here in New Hampshire and in the United States will keep us motivated and focused in the months and years ahead. To the New Hampshire Young Democrats, the New Hampshire Youth Movement, Southern New Hampshire Indivisible, Peace Action, the Progressive Democrats of America, the UAW and GEU UNH UAW, Firefighters, SEA/SEIU and the hundreds of local and state elected leaders and candidates, activists, students, teachers, parents, grandparents, and organizers who stepped up to support our movement: thank you. You are and will continue to be the heart and soul of the Democratic Party this country deserves. I ran for Congress because I believed that more of the same won’t fix this. And, we must fix healthcare, immigration, campaign finance, housing, and public education and never fail to recognize that there is so much that we can agree on here in NH, whether you are a Republican, a Democrat, or an Independent voter. It was a privilege and a joy to spend fifteen months in your living rooms, backyards, union halls, small businesses, libraries, and coffee shops asking what you wish Washington understood better about our lives and talking about the things that keep us all up at night and what we can do about it. After driving over 29,600 miles around our spectacular district, it is clear to me that the biggest divide right now is not between Democrats and Republicans, and it’s not between progressives and moderates: it’s between regular people trying to live our lives and a political and economic system that treats us like we don’t matter. **We do matter.** This campaign is proof that we can compete. Despite spending less than $600,000, we won 18,000 votes and 23% of the electorate. We planted the seeds for a political movement that we can and will continue to nurture _(more on that soon!)_. As I wrote in the more than 3,600 thank you notes I sent out over the course of this campaign. Here’s to building a better world together. Yours in solidarity, forever. Carleigh

pages of heavily redacted Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
records through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit revealing
that Thomas Matthew Crooks, the gunman who attempted to assassinate
then-presidential candidate Donald Trump at a July 2024 campaign rally
in Butler, Pennsylvania, purchased “a chest rig and ceramic
plates,” exhibited increasingly unusual behavior, including talking
to himself, pacing at night, staying awake for extended periods and
exhibiting impulsivity issues.

I needed to reach out with an urgent update:
**President Trump is coming to North Carolina tonight to hold a massive MAGA rally alongside my GOP opponent, Michael Whatley** - and we have less than a few hours to prepare for all the attacks about to be hurled our way.
**[Will you rush a contribution right now toward my $100,000 rapid-response goal to ensure we can fight back as soon as President Trump takes the stage? Meeting this goal by tonight 's deadline is the only way we'll have the resources to fight back against whatever comes next.](https://substack.com/redirect/3e32aff6-5510-4a4c-ba3b-704f7240f1a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

The president and the GOP know that if we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will lose out on our shot to take back the Senate majority.
That's why they're pulling out all the stops to defeat our people-powered movement: holding rallies, spreading lies and misinformation about me and investing millions of dollars to crush our momentum. With President Trump having just poured $5 million from his own campaign war chest into this race, the GOP is now investing more than $100 million so far to defeat me.
**Tonight 's Trump visit will give the green light to MAGA megadonors across the country to flood North Carolina with even more dark money - all because Senate control is at stake in this race.**
There's no way I can fight back - let alone flip this seat blue - without the support of people like you. This is an all-hands-on-deck moment, so I'm personally asking:

Roy Cooper

The press release recaps Himes grilling Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent at the September 15th House Financial Services Committee hearing and repeating the line for the record:
> **" I can think of no administration in the last 50 years that is quite as communist as the Trump administration."**
Himes did not mutter it in a hallway. He said this to the Treasury secretary, then published it under his own name. The target was Trump: tariffs, government equity stakes in private firms, bond-market operations, even the President's talk of $5,000 for voters. In Himes's telling, that package is communism.
This economic activity and investment is not. The reply belongs in the same public record. Readers can find Goldstein's running commentary, including the campaign press releases and the longer record on Himes, at [The Goldstein Substack](https://substack.com/redirect/7ad694ea-6e98-4cdc-b16a-3275eb26d858?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The word Himes chose is not a throwaway. He is a resident expert on the subject of Communism. He did not learn it from a textbook. He learned it in Nicaragua, among the Sandinistas he chose to study and plainly admired the Communist regime that rules Nicaragua.
**He Loved the Field Laboratory**
As a Harvard undergraduate, Himes wrote his senior thesis on **" The Sandinista Defense Committees and the Transformation of Political Culture in Nicaragua."** In the summer of 1987 he spent two months in Nicaragua living among the committees and interviewing Sandinista organizers. _**That was not a required survey course. It was a chosen apprenticeship in how a Marxist-Leninist movement remakes a country.**_
I wrote about that thesis two years ago, in February 2024, because Himes's own words--not mine--show how closely he studied the machinery of revolutionary political culture. That essay is here: [How Himes Wanted To Transform A Country Into A Marxist Leninist Autocratic State -- In His Own Words, Not Mine](https://substack.com/redirect/495fbbe3-d95b-4a23-8c35-8e59e274437b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Himes quoted Lenin on an elite party as "**the agent of transformation.** " He quoted Castro that "**revolution and education are the same thing**." He described the Sandinista program as calling for "**the complete overhaul of Nicaraguan socio-economic and political structure.** " He treated neighborhood defense committees as the instrument for changing what people believed, not merely what the state owned. That is the work of someone who found the communism model compelling.
I said so two years ago because Himes' paper does not read like a cold brief. It reads like a student who went looking for a revolution and liked what he found. A thesis is not a membership card. It is also not a shrug. _**Himes picked the Sandinistas. He lived with their organizers. He wrote them up as a case study in how to transform political culture. That is expertise. It is also affinity and qualifies him as a subject matter expert on communism.**_
If anyone sitting on Financial Services should know that "communist" is not a synonym for "tariff," "equity stake," or "Treasury buyback," it is the congressman who made himself a student of Sandinista power. He knows the difference between a customs duty and a vanguard party. He used the heavier word anyway.
**The Charge Does Not Fit the Tool**
Tariffs are not a communist invention. They are among the oldest economic tools of the United States government.
The Congressional Research Service reports that tariffs and other customs charges were the largest source of federal revenue in the 18th and 19th centuries and generated the bulk of federal revenue until the Civil War. Alexander Hamilton's system under President Washington relied on customs duties, along with excise taxes, to finance the new government and service the debt.
It would go too far to say tariffs were the federal government's only revenue source. Excise taxes existed too. The larger point is unmistakable: America relied heavily on tariffs long before it relied on a permanent federal income tax.
The first temporary federal income tax arrived in the Civil War. The Sixteenth Amendment was not ratified until 1913. Washington's America had tariffs. It did not have the modern federal income-tax system.
**Why Tariffs are Needed Today? - Domestic Production and National Security**
The Trump administration has said, in its February 2026 tariff policy, that import duties are meant to "incentivize the return of domestic production." Later actions on steel, aluminum, copper, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, drones and polysilicon have been tied to manufacturing, supply-chain security and strategic industries.
Those policies can be good, bad, too costly, or poorly designed. The U.S. International Trade Commission found that the first Trump administration's Section 232 steel tariffs cut affected imports by about 24 percent and raised domestic steel production about 1.9 percent; aluminum imports fell about 31 percent while domestic production rose about 3.6 percent. The same report found higher prices, costs borne largely by importers, and reduced output among some downstream manufacturers.
_That is an argument about industrial policy. It is not an argument about communism. Himes is free to say the costs outweigh the benefits. He is not entitled to collapse that disagreement into a word he studied in Nicaragua._
**If Equity Stakes Are Communism, Start With Goldman Sachs**
Himes spent 12 years at Goldman Sachs and became a vice president there. His campaign biography confirms it.
On October 28, 2008, the United States Treasury purchased $10 billion in Goldman Sachs preferred stock and received a warrant for more than 12 million shares of Goldman common stock. That is in Goldman's own SEC filing. Himes did not arrange the deal. It happened before he entered Congress.
_**If government ownership of a slice of a private firm is "communist," then the crisis-era rescue of Himes's former employer belongs in the same conversation. The more honest description is that American administrations of both parties have intervened in markets in emergencies. An equity stake does not turn the United States into Nicaragua any more than a tariff does.**_
**Precision Is the Point**
Himes is a resident expert on communism long before the new school of democrat socialists that he has cozied up to. Himes wrote about Leninist vanguard parties, Cuban educational doctrine, and Sandinista committees built to remake a people from the block up. That is why the hearing line was not tough. It was cheap. A man who loved the communism field laboratory (while many from Nicaragua escaped to America) should not cheapen the word when the subject is steel duties and bond buybacks.
You can debate the tariffs, the buybacks and whether industrial policy is worth the price. Those are the questions that the Financial Services Committee exists to examine.
**Do not call two centuries of American customs policy that helped shape the nation and fund a nation prior to a federal tax system "communist" when you once sat in Nicaragua studying the real apparatus, wrote it up with sympathy, and then asked voters to treat you as a serious man on finance and intelligence.**
Himes raised the accusation from his committee seat. His own thesis gives the public a better dictionary than the one he used on Tuesday.
If Himes is so opposed to Communism why did he vote against the bill condemning socialism and the Democrat Socialists of America, a political movement that wants to destroy our system of government and have the state take over the means of production. That is communism. His rhetoric falsely accuses the Trump Administration of Communism and his vote in Congress confirms his support of Communism.
Himes is the true Communist and he will support the DSA if they take control of the US Congress.
**The best way to fight Communism in Connecticut is not to re-elect Himes.**

Diesel hit $6.05 per gallon yesterday -- the highest price ever recorded in U.S. history. All-time records fell in 28 states simultaneously. California's average is $7.98, and five stations are displaying $9.999 because their price boards physically cannot show a higher number. Americans are spending $700 million more per day on fuel than a year ago.
Right on schedule, the argument started. One side blames Trump and the war with Iran. The other says it has nothing to do with him. Both sides are missing the actual story -- and I think that's by design.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/636a45a7-1a07-4c50-a279-1ec0244bd0f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Orange County, CA 9/14/2026
**The Barrel Price Doesn 't Explain It**
The Iran war is real. The Strait of Hormuz is constrained. That's a factor. But stop there and you'll never understand why diesel is at $6 now, when crude oil isn't even close to it's all-time high.
Crude hit $100 per barrel this week. Sounds like a lot until you adjust for inflation. In 2008, crude hit $147 -- over $210 in today's dollars. In 1980, during the Iranian Revolution, it hit $36 -- over $160 today. Current crude is well below both peaks in real terms.
But diesel was never $6 during those crises. Not in 1980. Not in 2008. Not ever.
The barrel price doesn't explain $6 diesel. Something else does...

subject: I need to confess something
body:
Good ideas on their own don’t win elections
Hi, Peter, it’s Governor Josh Shapiro.
I’m reaching out because our fundraising has slowed down at the worst possible moment, and I’m hoping you can help us out.
**[If that’s all you need to hear, please use this link to rush $25 or whatever you can afford — split between our campaign and Wes Moore — before our critical End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline on September 30th:](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260916-2.NFURho&refcode=em-20260916-2&t=1&akid=1938%2E1086043%2E3Hn6wU)**
**[Rush a Donation](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260916-2.NFURho&amount=5&refcode=em-20260916-2&t=2&akid=1938%2E1086043%2E3Hn6wU)**
But I also need to confess something — and this isn’t something you’ll hear from many other elected officials.
**I don’t want you to chip in _just_ because of a fundraising deadline.**
I want you to chip in because you believe in the same things I do.
That freedom and opportunity should triumph over chaos and cruelty. That our government works best when it’s working for everyone — not the guy at the very top.
But I’m not naive. Good ideas on their own don’t win elections.

Josh Shapiro

| | Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya is a Palestinian pediatrician and longtime director of a Gaza hospital. Nearly two years ago, Israeli authorities detained him without formal charges or a trial. **Now, more than a year and a half later, he is still in Israeli custody without any formal charges or a trial. His lawyer says his physical condition is “near death.”** Dr. Abu Safiya has spent his career caring for children in Gaza. He was instrumental in keeping the hospital running through unimaginable conditions, including building a malnutrition unit that treated hundreds of children. **No physician should be punished for answering the call to care for people in crisis.** As a pulmonary and critical care physician, I know how quickly a person’s health can deteriorate when they are denied the medical care they need. _Dr. Abu Safiya needs medical care. He needs due process. Most urgently, he NEEDS to come home._ Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D., and I led a Congressional letter with 69 total members of Congress, calling for Secretary of State Marco Rubio to immediately secure Dr. Abu Safiya’s release. clean_body: | | | | | Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya is a Palestinian pediatrician and longtime director of a Gaza hospital. Nearly two years ago, Israeli authorities detained him without formal charges or a trial. Now, more than a year and a half later, he is still in Israeli custody without any formal charges or a trial. His lawyer says his physical condition is “near death.” Dr. Abu Safiya has spent his career caring for children in Gaza. He was instrumental in keeping the hospital running through unimaginable conditions, including building a malnutrition unit that treated hundreds of children. No physician should be punished for answering the call to care for people in crisis. As a pulmonary and critical care physician, I know how quickly a person’s health can deteriorate when they are denied the medical care they need. Dr. Abu Safiya needs medical care. He needs due process. Most urgently, he NEEDS to come home. Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D., and I led a Congressional letter with 69 total members of Congress, calling for Secretary of State Marco Rubio to immediately secure Dr. Abu Safiya’s release. | | | | | A physician should not have to die in custody before the world pays attention. We cannot wait. End the cruelty. We can stop this administration in its tracks and elect a Congress that works for working people.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41576%2E3422442%2EzkwTTK)
Peter,
Democrats have to flip _just three seats_ to take back the House this year, and it will be a group of fearless women leading the way.
That’s why I’m proud to support three outstanding candidates fighting to flip Republican-held districts that we need to win: **Lindsay James (IA-02)** , **Rebecca Cooke (WI-03)** , and **Marni von Wilpert (CA-48).**
**[Can you split a donation between their campaigns and Truth to Power to give them the resources needed to win?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260916_1_ak.JbJ4j3&refcode=em20260916-41576&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41576%2E3422442%2EzkwTTK)**

These three candidates are the type of champions we need more of in Congress:
**Lindsay James** is a chaplain and state legislator. She has been a strong advocate for everyday Iowans and has championed the idea that the government should serve the people, not the powerful. We can count on her to bring Congress together to find real solutions to our biggest problems.
**Rebecca Cooke** is a small business owner, nonprofit leader, and waitress running to beat MAGA extremist Derrick Van Orden. Raised on a dairy farm, she understands the challenges facing rural families, and how Congress needs to do more for working people.
**Marni von Wilpert** is a San Diego city councilmember with a proven record of delivering real results. She’s running in a newly winnable district created by Prop 50 in California to stop Trump’s chaos and corruption and put an end to ICE’s lawlessness.
Right-wing billionaires are spending big trying to defeat these candidates. But if enough grassroots supporters step up, we can stop MAGA extremists in their tracks and elect a Congress that works for working people.
**[I’m counting on you to help us take back the House, Peter. Rush $5 to Lindsay, Rebecca, Marni, and Truth to Power to send three women who will fight for us to Congress.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260916_1_ak.JbJ4j3&refcode=em20260916-41576&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=41576%2E3422442%2EzkwTTK)**

Thank you,
Katie Porter

Hey team, I know this isn't the kind of email I usually send, but before we head into the final stretch of this election, I wanted to take a moment to tell you why I'm still in this fight. [_**And when I'm done, I hope you'll chip in to help me win reelection this November and keep delivering results for Kansas' 3rd District.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139347233/647046950/-1547774912?refcode=email_091626_story&amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYmRkMTk3My0xM2IyLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1W-I1w21pDKjS_YuQ4LLfrlpeZcNYN18fUn1RGiguOA=) | | [Chip in →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139347234/647046951/-1547774912?refcode=email_091626_story&amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYmRkMTk3My0xM2IyLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1W-I1w21pDKjS_YuQ4LLfrlpeZcNYN18fUn1RGiguOA=)

Growing up, not many people would have looked at me and pictured a future Congresswoman.
My mom raised me on her own while spending 20 years serving our country in the Army. She taught me what hard work and responsibility look like — not by telling me, but by showing up and living it every single day.
I held on to those lessons when I worked multiple jobs to get myself through school. I held on to them through my work in economic and community development on Native American reservations. And I held on to them in 2018, when I launched a campaign to take on a four-term Republican incumbent in Congress.
Back then, plenty of people told me I couldn't win. In their eyes, an LGBTQ+ Native American woman and former MMA fighter didn't belong in Washington. **But I didn't listen to the naysayers then, and I'm not listening to them now.**
Because the naysayers haven't gone _anywhere_.
Over the past year, Republicans pushed to redraw Kansas' congressional map for one reason: To force me out of this seat. They came up short. Now, they're lining up behind yet another challenger, hoping to flip this must-win seat in November.
I ran for Congress because I believe our government should look more like the people it serves — working people, fighters, people with real-world experiences facing real-world struggles.
And over the past eight years, I've worked hand-in-hand with hardworking Kansans to deliver real results: Millions of dollars in infrastructure projects, thousands of clean-energy jobs, the most significant bipartisan gun safety law in a generation — and I’m committed to continuing that fight.
[_**But our work is far from finished — and with less than seven weeks left until Election Day, I need everyone on this grassroots team stepping up and pitching in. If there's one thing my mom taught me, it's that hard work is _good work_. That's why I'm still in this fight — and if you're ready to stand with me, please chip in any amount to help us hold KS-03 and take back the House →**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139347235/647046952/-1547774912?refcode=email_091626_story&amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYmRkMTk3My0xM2IyLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1W-I1w21pDKjS_YuQ4LLfrlpeZcNYN18fUn1RGiguOA=)

The Shipping Data Says the Chokepoint Is Nearly Closed. The Rhetoric Says a Deal Is Close.
Six down sessions in seven, a 2007-era yield high, and Hormuz traffic down to four ships a day — all before the Fed has even spoken.

| | What Moved
---|---
**Verified fact:** Tuesday marked the sixth decline in seven sessions across major U.S. indexes — the S&P; 500 down 0.45% to 7,585.73, the Dow down 0.63% to 52,093.11, the Nasdaq down 0.78% to 25,981.57 — as the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.006%, its highest since 2007, and Brent crude rose 2.14% to settle near $107.90, briefly spiking to $108 intraday before retreating on comments from President Trump that Iran wants a deal.
| | Rotation Signal 01 — The Physical Shipping Data Contradicts the Optimistic Headlines
---|---
**Verified fact:** Hormuz transit fell to just four commodity vessels Monday, down from ten the day before and a pre-war baseline north of 100 daily transits. War-risk insurance premiums have risen to 3–10% of hull value, meaning $3–10 million per single tanker crossing. Separately, the IRGC Navy claimed responsibility for disabling the Panama-flagged vessel El Gaia with mines — Tehran's first acknowledged strike on a named merchant hull since the conflict resumed. **Our interpretation:** whatever the diplomatic rhetoric, the physical chokepoint is functioning at a small single-digit fraction of pre-war capacity, and Iran has now directly claimed a strike on a merchant vessel rather than only being accused of one — a harder, more confirmable data point than any of this week's statements about progress toward a deal.
| | Rotation Signal 02 — A Second Escalation Landed Overnight, in a Different Location
---|---
**Verified fact:** Saudi Arabia said it intercepted a Houthi drone aimed at Mecca and called the attempt a “red line,” the first such attempt since a 2017 ballistic missile strike on the city. **Our interpretation:** this event sits geographically and militarily separate from the Hormuz and pipeline stories that have dominated recent editions, but it further reduces the odds of a near-term, cooperative Saudi posture toward any regional diplomatic framework — compounding, rather than replacing, the chokepoint risk already priced into energy markets.
| | Rotation Signal 03 — Six Down Sessions in Seven Is Itself the Signal
---|---
**Current classification: CONFIRMATION.** A single bad session can be noise; six declines in seven, alongside a 2007-era yield high and a still-rising oil price, is a market that has stopped treating this week's individual headlines as isolated and started pricing a sustained, compounding risk regime — energy, rates, and geopolitics reinforcing each other rather than offsetting.
| | What to Watch This Afternoon
---|---
Whether risk assets treat the Fed's 2:00 PM decision as the resolution of this week's uncertainty (a relief move regardless of hike or hold) or as one more data point in an already-deteriorating run will be visible within the first hour of trading after the announcement.

Speaker Mike Johnson just canceled House votes for tomorrow — sending us home a day early, after he had _already_ canceled two full weeks of votes in the second half of the month. If you’re doing the math, it means the House will be out of session for SEVEN weeks instead of working for the American people.

Why?

Because yesterday, a Republican Member of Congress filed articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth, and Mike Johnson is terrified to let us vote on them.

He knows, just like you and I do, that Hegseth is an absolute disaster, and it's not just what's spelled out in the articles of impeachment: \- Waging an illegal and reckless war with Iran
\- Putting civilians and service members at risk
\- Spending billions of dollars to be losing a war that we shouldn’t be in in the first place
\- Using our military to murder civilians in the Caribbean and the Eastern Pacific
\- Kidnapping a foreign leader
\- Proven to be reckless with classified operational details
\- Controlling the press and trying to hide the truth
\- Wasting taxpayer dollars on lobsters and steaks
\- Bringing his pastor (the one who wants to get rid of women’s right to vote) in to preach to service members at the Pentagon on the public’s dime The Speaker doesn’t want to give the House an opportunity to hold Hegseth accountable.

He’s a coward, and he shouldn’t be leading the House of Representatives.

So come November, we’re going to kick him out of power and take back a majority that will work to pursue real accountability for this administration’s failures and end this needless and illegal war in Iran.

If you’re with me, I’m asking for your support. _Republicans are winning on the advertising front, with _$263 million_ more in TV ads booked through the midterms, and they continue to hold a serious cash advantage over Democrats._

clean_body: Come ON.| | | | Speaker Mike Johnson just canceled House votes for tomorrow — sending us home a day early, after he had already canceled two full weeks of votes in the second half of the month. If you’re doing the math, it means the House will be out of session for SEVEN weeks instead of working for the American people. Why? Because yesterday, a Republican Member of Congress filed articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth, and Mike Johnson is terrified to let us vote on them. He knows, just like you and I do, that Hegseth is an absolute disaster, and it's not just what's spelled out in the articles of impeachment: \- Waging an illegal and reckless war with Iran \- Putting civilians and service members at risk \- Spending billions of dollars to be losing a war that we shouldn’t be in in the first place \- Using our military to murder civilians in the Caribbean and the Eastern Pacific \- Kidnapping a foreign leader \- Proven to be reckless with classified operational details \- Controlling the press and trying to hide the truth \- Wasting taxpayer dollars on lobsters and steaks \- Bringing his pastor (the one who wants to get rid of women’s right to vote) in to preach to service members at the Pentagon on the public’s dime The Speaker doesn’t want to give the House an opportunity to hold Hegseth accountable. He’s a coward, and he shouldn’t be leading the House of Representatives. So come November, we’re going to kick him out of power and take back a majority that will work to pursue real accountability for this administration’s failures and end this needless and illegal war in Iran. If you’re with me, I’m asking for your support. Republicans are winning on the advertising front, with $263 million more in TV ads booked through the midterms, and they continue to hold a serious cash advantage over Democrats. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. Team, While you were filling up your tank at record-high prices, Jay Feely was in Dallas. Not working for Arizona. Not fighting for relief. Partying with billionaire donors at the GOP's multi-million-dollar "Trump-a-Palooza" — celebrating the very agenda that's draining your wallet. Here's the damage Trump's reckless war with Iran has done to Arizona families: **→ $4.56** per gallon of gas **→ $5.99** per gallon of diesel **→ $477** more spent per family just to get the kids to school and get to work And where was Jay Feely? Schmoozing with the ultra-wealthy in Texas. Yet again, Republicans show their loyalty lies only with the highest bidder — never with working families. If Arizona voters can't trust Republicans not to bail on their own people, how can they trust them to govern on their behalf? This is who Republicans are. body:
I wanted you to hear it personally from me:
| Hi Friend, I wanted to reach out personally because a lot of conservatives are frustrated right now. Honestly, I don't blame them. Too many political groups treat grassroots supporters like ATMs. They send fake threats, pretend every message is from President Trump himself, and never even stop to say thank you.

That's not how we do things at the Republican Governors Association.

My name is Sophie, and I work with the RGA team helping support conservative Governors across the country. I just wanted to personally thank you for standing with the America First movement already. We truly appreciate it.

But I also need to be honest with you: Democrats are coming into 2026 organized, angry, and loaded with cash. They're targeting Governor races all across the country because they know Governors control election law, veto power, public safety policy, and the firewall against the Radical Left's agenda. If Democrats take these Governor mansions, they'll use them to block President Trump, protect sanctuary state policies, and push the same failed agenda we've seen destroy states like California and Illinois.

That's why support from grassroots conservatives matters so much right now. And unlike a lot of organizations, we're not going to threaten you or guilt you if you can't give today.

But if you are able to chip in a few dollars to help defend conservative Governors, it would genuinely mean a lot. But I also need to be honest with you: Democrats are coming into 2026 organized, angry, and loaded with cash. They're targeting Governor races all across the country because they know Governors control election law, veto power, public safety policy, and the firewall against the Radical Left's agenda. We have an opportunity to flip a seat here |
Peter,

This kind of opportunity doesn't come often. But for the first time in a long time, we have a real chance to flip a deep blue seat.

There are two main reasons why.

The first is because Radical Democrat incumbent Raul Ruiz is a long-time career politician who has voted consistently with his party's leadership and has opposed key efforts on taxes, spending restraint, and election-integrity measures like the SAVE Act.

**Ruiz has been doing this for years.**

The other reason is because of the Republican candidate, Joe Males.

Joe is not another career politician. He's a Marine veteran who enlisted at 18, served overseas, and was honorably discharged as a Sergeant. He's a small business owner who started out in an entry-level job and built his company from the ground up. He's a city council member who has focused on safer neighborhoods, infrastructure, and local business growth.

**Joe Males has been able to attract serious attention to this race and we are now closer than ever to flipping this seat.**

body:
Join us on Sunday, September 27th for a special Resistance Lab focused on immigration justice.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260916-6727-footer&t=1&akid=6727%2E420207%2E7P9365)
Peter, ICE’s cruelty has not stopped.
The raids and deportations haven’t slowed down. And the terror our communities are feeling hasn’t gone away.
This administration is weaponizing fear and division against immigrant communities to advance their authoritarian agenda, tear families apart, and silence anyone who dares to speak out against it.
**_We refuse to let that stand._ That’s why on [Sunday, September 27th at 11am PT / 2pm ET](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/53935?utm_source=em20260916-6727&t=2&akid=6727%2E420207%2E7P9365), we’re hosting our next Resistance Lab focusing entirely on immigration justice.**
[****](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/53935?utm_source=em20260916-6727&t=3&akid=6727%2E420207%2E7P9365)
**[RSVP](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/53935?utm_source=em20260916-6727&t=4&akid=6727%2E420207%2E7P9365)**
She’ll lead this training herself, alongside expert guest speakers, bringing decades of organizing experience and her work on the frontlines of this fight in Congress. Pramila was an immigrant rights organizer before she ever set foot in office, and as the top Democrat on the Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, she is a true expert on how you can create real change in our system.
Here’s what we’ll cover:
* The history of our immigration system and how this administration is weaponizing it to advance an authoritarian agenda
* Concrete actions you can take right now to protect immigrant communities and organize locally
* How to defend our democracy against this administration’s constant attacks and attempts to consolidate power

Over 30,000 people and counting from all 50 states have joined us for a Resistance Lab. Whether you’re a first timer or a seasoned member of this movement, this training is for you!
**[If you’re able, please join us on Sunday, September 27th at 11am PT / 2pm ET to train, organize, connect with your people, and continue building our movement together.](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/53935?utm_source=em20260916-6727&t=5&akid=6727%2E420207%2E7P9365)**
We hope to see you there!
— Team Jayapal

We’re in the home stretch of the election.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8960%2E582294%2E8Bq5Gt)
Hi, it’s Chris.
**_Can I get a few moments to reintroduce myself —[and explain why I’m asking for your $5 donation today?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260916_3.rEKl1_&refcode=em20260916-3&t=2&akid=8960%2E582294%2E8Bq5Gt)_**
Over 100 years ago, my great-grandfather came here from Greece and opened our family restaurant that became a beloved local spot. That’s where I learned how to work hard and show up for my community – lessons I carried with me into the State House, Congress, and now my run for Senate.
I’m running against John Sununu, the son of a political dynasty family with deep pockets. He said he’d like to “send me back to bussing tables,” as if that’s an insult.
John Sununu doesn’t know a thing about hard work.
I’m proud to be running this race the right way – no corporate PACs, just a grassroots team built by people like you, chipping in what they can, when they can.
But with just 48 days until the election, recent polls show Sununu is surging into the lead, **and this race has officially shifted to a Toss Up.**
I know what it takes to win in a swing state like New Hampshire – and we can’t flip the Senate if we don’t win this open seat.
**[That’s why I need you to stand with me today. Please chip in $5 to help my campaign win this seat and give Democrats a shot at taking back the Senate.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260916_3.rEKl1_&refcode=em20260916-3&t=3&akid=8960%2E582294%2E8Bq5Gt)**

**Ever since I was a student, I knew I wanted to fight for justice and make a difference.** I’m the daughter of two special education teachers. I was raised in a working class family that instilled in me the values of hard work, opportunity, and serving others.
_So I always knew I wanted to fight for justice and make a difference._
It’s why I started my career investigating threats to democracy and civil rights.
Then I served as a law clerk to a federal civil rights judge in Detroit, protecting and defending people’s civil rights and freedoms.
Then, as Dean of Wayne State University Law School, I worked to make sure all students could afford their education by freezing tuition and expanding scholarships.
It’s why, as Secretary of State, I’ve fought to make everyday life easier for all Michiganders, secure our elections, and expand voter access.
**But I know our work is far from finished. So now, I’m running for Governor to make sure Michigan is a place where everyone – from our kids to our seniors – can stay and thrive.**
But Michigan is one of the most competitive states in the country, and the latest polls show this race is going to be extremely close. Winning here won’t be easy... or cheap.
**I’m committed to building a campaign built by the people, for the people. While my Republican counterpart has already accepted $5 million from the DeVos family funneled into a shady super PAC, our campaign is building real momentum, and we can’t let it stall. [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mp-em-q326?refcode=em260916-1-av&refcode2=1121_3892029_L-9kad&akid=1121%2E3892029%2EL-9kad)

Peter -
My name is Mary Peltola, and I’m the pro-fish, pro-family, pro-freedom Democrat running for United States Senate in Alaska.
I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support in the last 8 weeks of our campaign.
But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this link to contribute today:
[**https://act.marypeltola.com/go/fish-family-freedom](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mp-em-q326?refcode=em260916-1-av&refcode2=1121_3892029_L-9kad&akid=1121%2E3892029%2EL-9kad)**
**[CONTRIBUTE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mp-em-q326?refcode=em260916-1-av&refcode2=1121_3892029_L-9kad&akid=1121%2E3892029%2EL-9kad)**
Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just _crushing_ Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying more than 25 bucks for a gallon of fuel in rural Alaska. _They don’t even believe us._
They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
**This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.**
So I am asking:
[**Please contribute to my campaign for the U.S. Senate today as we begin the general election. No donation is too small. They will all add up fast to give us the resources we need to WIN in November.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mp-em-q326?refcode=em260916-1-av&refcode2=1121_3892029_L-9kad&akid=1121%2E3892029%2EL-9kad)

name: Roy Cooper
subject: We knew this was coming
body:
Folks aren’t paying attention. But Trump is.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1517&source=&t=1&akid=3575%2E124072%2EVquq0z) | | | |
---
Peter, we knew this was coming – even so, **it's not good.**
JD Vance has visited North Carolina to rally the GOP base and spread lies about me. MAGA loyalist Stephen Miller has gone on Fox News to rant and rave about me. President Trump’s DHS Secretary, Markwayne Mullin, has perpetuated lies against me on Newsmax, and the president himself has personally attacked me on social media in front of his millions of followers.
Now, Trump is upping the ante because this race in North Carolina could decide Senate control: MAGA Inc.’s super PAC is pouring millions into the effort to defeat me, bringing total Republican spending in this race to over $100 million (and counting).
**Peter, those attacks are working: A new poll shows our already narrow polling lead _cut in half._**
We warned folks that this was going to be a close race. In North Carolina, winning a U.S. Senate race by a "landslide" means winning, at best, 51% of the vote. That’s how competitive our state is, no matter what the pundits or the latest ratings say.
Unfortunately, many people seem to have turned their attention elsewhere, and as a result, we’re losing critical ground with just weeks to go until the election.
**I know we can get back on track, but not if we get complacent. Not without grassroots support from folks like you – right here, right now.[_That’s why I’m urgently asking, Peter: Will you chip in $5 or any amount to my campaign to help me respond to Trump and the GOP, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1517&amount=5&t=8&akid=3575%2E124072%2EVquq0z)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1517&amount=5&t=9&akid=3575%2E124072%2EVquq0z)

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

The Democrats are desperate to gain control of the Senate. They are pouring millions into the Treasure State to install a Democrat who will vote in lockstep with Chuck Schumer, Adam Schiff, and Elizabeth Warren. They believe their road to majority control runs straight through Montana. I know loyal Republicans like you have been asked to provide support many times already this year, but time is running out and our Party does not have anywhere else to turn. Our resources are already spread thin. There are 35 U.S. Senate races with 22 seats up for election held by Republicans and just 13 are held by Democrats. I’m passionate about helping elect Kurt Alme because I’ve seen his record of service and leadership for the people of Montana. And I know he’ll be at the forefront of efforts to help enact President Trump’s America First agenda. Fellow Patriot, there are no "moderate" Democrats in the U.S. Senate. The radical Left dictates their agenda - tax increases, job-killing regulation, government expansion, woke mandates, and restrictions on our Constitutional rights and freedoms. I am proud to stand with Kurt, a proud conservative leader who is running to return power to the people – and ensure that the liberal Washington, D.C., establishment is held in check. But to win this race, We need to elect Kurt Alme and keep our Republican Senate Majority so we can continue to enact real, lasting conservative reforms to grow our economy, improve our security, and protect our Constitutional freedoms. # **LA homeless-funding fraud crackdown reveals millions of tax dollars stolen, several arrested**
Federal authorities charged Michael Young, founder of nonprofit Home At Last, with **[misappropriating millions](https://substack.com/redirect/41e20ea7-2f69-4b60-a24f-040052ecc15e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from over $118 million in public homelessness funds -- including spending on a Tahiti vacation, a vintage car restoration, and a high-end Inglewood nightclub -- as part of a broader fraud sweep.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a020824-b5d9-440e-abd8-f19a1c33b56a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Michael Young, Lakiya Malone, and Donye Mitchell, 55 (DOJ)
* **Lakiya Malone, an employee of Special Service for Groups, was arrested** on charges she accepted over $180,000 in bribes to fabricate homeless client files, including fake participants, in exchange for priority housing referrals from another nonprofit's director, who has agreed to plead guilty.
* **A third defendant, Donye Mitchell, remains at large** after allegedly using over $1.2 million in grant money obtained through false claims for personal expenses. Officials warned more arrests could follow as they urge reporting of similar fraud.

# **El-Sayed had a big problem with breast cancer research and funding, past essay exposes**
A 2012 essay from Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed **[criticized what he called the"breast cancer lobby"](https://substack.com/redirect/c1715707-1f2a-4098-988b-73fa4f7e70a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for driving disproportionate federal research funding, arguing the disease's high visibility created an inaccurate sense of "imminent danger" while diverting resources from other diseases with less "social power."

name: OnePA Team
subject: Thank the postal workers who stood up
body:
When working people organize, powerful people cannot simply make the rules for everyone else. | |
---
Peter, **The Supreme Court just blocked Donald Trump’s attempt to restrict mail ballots for the midterms. That is a win for our communities, and it belongs to organized people.** Postal workers, their union, and everyday voters refused to let the administration turn the Postal Service into a tool for keeping eligible people from voting. **The American Postal Workers Union (APWU) -- as well as the National Association of Letter Carriers, the National Rural Letter Carriers Association, and the National Postal Mail Handlers Union -- has been standing in the way of this attack from the beginning****.** The Trump-backed USPS rule would have let the Postal Service refuse to deliver ballots unless states handed over voter lists and followed a new federal scheme. APWU called that rule unprincipled, unworkable, and unlawful. **Postal workers warned it would create chaos around election mail and abandon the public service they carry out every day.** That power matters far beyond one workplace. Strong unions give working people a voice. They build leaders in our communities. They create organized power that can stand in the way when politicians try to take rights away from the rest of us. That is exactly what postal workers did here. Their sacred role is delivering our ballots. **Vote by mail is secure and reliable. Nearly a third of voters use it. You can request a mail-in ballot, fill it out at home, and return it by mail, drop box, or in Pennsylvania to your county board of elections. Request it early. Return it early. Track it. Your ballot will be sent to you and received through the mail.** [**Sign on to thank Postal Workers for standing up to the administration and the USPS Board of Governors.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3-vIyBGl6yNLHygdycyp5sAuo8Boy1XzEXznv_UM5p59eAwtsYpVhkxp0v5SJzcRLEv2CTyLex-71umkUxV2gxJpQdjFI1PogYt24oZAs_aOuqsKk9SVjtE9-T-5LWgCpJCOj3LEJ3GLLuWjhjY6v4D50MRNVzcVqrUv60MJvb2isqEw2SPBE2chmyRCeYgDr8nOdfamONiNU2nT7CYx5o3JEkBTOA7RaEdByj1Rm6toG7GCFmdzOKjQjg-Htk0HC3hXMD9StD3y2s3B9zsUTcYqkX5HpfQZEh0WVcV_RHfoH2ug43NeazTDANfTvOkq8BnEMYyyX0A_JPJiB-pZ8Bo/4u3/LsXOr_tOQkim3DRLuDXFgQ/h0/h001.w1G6eZrDuVJAzNRsqQ8aqPxTK1IDhzWmTsMPaJDC1c0) | | [SIGN ON](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3-vIyBGl6yNLHygdycyp5sAuo8Boy1XzEXznv_UM5p59eAwtsYpVhkxp0v5SJzcRLEv2CTyLex-71umkUxV2gxJDk6b9I_e6rxkbH4pqA4zwZuhSG2ttKE9yajQo70REX27c0QxckOZ2_S4tIkQDG15qsi-9Lcet-olqbXL2eEpJJkbmugyuCfv2WrJ7tu3DRIPnJCwJB5FLFn6crFQ0c87xRjdjruB8sSFtyVxERZLZRnB8oW1l4bpWzsrZHFEIDv_NcJiTqn-imgD79UQO8NDePdGqqIIWAQ9_NjUTi6e5OVpAokThcSkXxTGXxAG1ZO93sNIdo64E5V0dlnzODBr/4u3/LsXOr_tOQkim3DRLuDXFgQ/h1/h001.-PYP74-LinKrQPhSrce8n_pKCZ2gWzkMfEXEK0xZ9dw)
---
**A court order protects vote by mail for this election. But the rule is still on the books. Postmaster General David Steiner wanted the Postal Service ready to move if the courts gave him an opening****.** The USPS Board of Governors should rescind this rule while the country is watching.
Two worrying nominees are awaiting Senate confirmation to that Board. Another is awaiting committee markup. Confirming them would hand more control of the Postal Service to the same political project that tried to choke off mail ballots. Keeping them off the Board is part of getting this rule scrapped and delivering ballots to voters.
When working people are organized, when Black communities can build political power, and when unions are strong enough to stand together, politicians and wealthy interests cannot simply push us aside. That is why people who want unchecked power work so hard to weaken unions, silence voters, and divide our communities.
**Generations of workers have shown us another way. We organize. We stand together. We build enough collective power to defend what previous generations won and push our communities forward.**
[**Thank the postal workers who stood up for our ballots. We must keep this rule off the books so vote by mail stays in the people’s hands.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3-vIyBGl6yNLHygdycyp5sAuo8Boy1XzEXznv_UM5p59eAwtsYpVhkxp0v5SJzcRLEv2CTyLex-71umkUxV2gxJjOXGVETORqlAzSiAMkNyvuEbO2oBED4Hb6D629A3QZ9ECQ9Az92vsbwMU_EOUOYL0J_oLlWvay0EQYjpFuUYupoH6HKmarxQLbauo7WdRJlssmIj9ijJMgamMoi20BQYYhM24VU4S--yFEjz7oqLMyiFcSmKqnTYQIryVq6tRjE4-_aMDVo6eD1W9nmmDHS-zbO1Qf5ISR8_Ykhcqp3Bi7rUJZBpttcZtw8ryyhm4eIcZ0Zf8apxIdEWvx2MU4vA/4u3/LsXOr_tOQkim3DRLuDXFgQ/h2/h001.n2Yv0xpI7v3WuPm9LEFJep8oT53ZW24dz3FgwNeJD3w)

From skyrocketing costs to declining fish stocks, Alaskans are losing the ability to feed our families. I’ve seen it firsthand, and I hear about it from communities across the state.

We’re tired of politicians in DC beholden to corporate factory trawlers and multi-national farmed salmon companies. Alaska deserves a senator who cares more about fish stocks than their own stock portfolio. That’s why I’m running for Senate to take on the corruption that’s hurting all of us – but I can only win with your support.

name: Gina Hinojosa
body:
This is the moment we’ve been working toward, Texas.
Look at this:
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260916_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.jKzvy4&refcode=em20260916-1713&amount=5&t=1&akid=1713%2E2118727%2EVnFINI)
In June, we were down 6 points. In August, down 1. Last week, a brand-new Univision poll showed this race TIED. 47-47.
_This is the moment we’ve been working toward._ It's the first poll of this campaign to show us dead even with Greg Abbott. But it's not the first to show us within striking distance. Seven other polls in the last month have had this race statistically tied. **Four of those had us within a single point.**
That's not a fluke. It's not simply a good week. It's a clear trend that’s been moving in one direction. **[Make a donation to my campaign to help us take the lead and take back Texas.](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260916_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.jKzvy4&refcode=em20260916-1713&amount=5&t=2&akid=1713%2E2118727%2EVnFINI)**
Here's what’s changed since the June poll showing us down 6: Texans are getting to know me. Every time voters learn more about who I am and what I’m fighting for, our numbers go up. And every time they take another look at the man who's run this state for twelve years, Abbott's poll numbers go down. His approval is underwater. His favorability is underwater.
I don’t need to tell you why. You’re living it. Rising grocery bills, rising premiums, rising property taxes. Data centers flooding our state. And a governor who’s spent over a decade protecting the people at the top instead of the Texans footing the bill.
**All the wind is at our backs. Ours is the campaign with all of the momentum. But we don’t have the resources to match it — not yet, not without your help.**
**[DONATE ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260916_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.jKzvy4&refcode=em20260916-1713&amount=5&t=3&akid=1713%2E2118727%2EVnFINI)**
We are TIED with Greg Abbott, but he has nearly $70 million in the bank. He is going to spend every dollar of it to make sure Texans who are ready for change don't show up in November. A tie is not a lead. We have to go and take it for ourselves.
**[Can you donate $5 right now to my campaign to help us break this tie and finally defeat Greg Abbott in November?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260916_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.jKzvy4&refcode=em20260916-1713&amount=5&t=4&akid=1713%2E2118727%2EVnFINI)**
It’s because of your support that we’ve erased Greg Abbott’s lead. This is a tied race: 47-47. We can finally win back Texas and make it work for regular Texans, but we need your support again today. Let’s make it happen.
Gina

Peter - I'm going to be straight with you, because that's the only way I know how to do this.

_We just won._ Two elections in two weeks: the special primary, then the runoff.

Grueling doesn't begin to cover it. Every dollar this campaign had went into turning out voters, running ads, and getting our message into every corner of this state.

**And it worked.**

But here's the part nobody tells you on election night: winning a runoff doesn't put a single dollar back in our account. Right now, after everything we just spent, our campaign finances are running on fumes.

**Annie Andrews has $4.1 million.**

She's raised nearly $11 million since she got into this race, from liberal donors across the country. She's had months to build that war chest while we were fighting a two-round primary just to get our name on the November ballot.

Countless conservatives in SC put their trust in me, and I promise to carry forward the conservative agenda for the next six years in the United States Senate. After asking me to run, President Trump stood on stage with me and told you why he trusts me, too. I don't intend to let a bigger bank account decide whether I get to keep that promise.

clean_body: | Peter - I'm going to be straight with you, because that's the only way I know how to do this. We just won. Two elections in two weeks: the special primary, then the runoff. Grueling doesn't begin to cover it. Every dollar this campaign had went into turning out voters, running ads, and getting our message into every corner of this state. And it worked. But here's the part nobody tells you on election night: winning a runoff doesn't put a single dollar back in our account. Right now, after everything we just spent, our campaign finances are running on fumes. Annie Andrews has $4.1 million. She's raised nearly $11 million since she got into this race, from liberal donors across the country. She's had months to build that war chest while we were fighting a two-round primary just to get our name on the November ballot. Countless conservatives in SC put their trust in me, and I promise to carry forward the conservative agenda for the next six years in the United States Senate. After asking me to run, President Trump stood on stage with me and told you why he trusts me, too. I don't intend to let a bigger bank account decide whether I get to keep that promise. The general election is November 3. That sounds far off. It isn't. It's less than 70 days away. Every week between now and then, Annie Andrews's campaign will be on television, in your mailbox, and on your phone - funded by liberal donors who wanted to defeat Lindsey and now, defeat me. We have to be able to answer that, and right now, we can't. My opponent has a $4 million head start. To catch up and rebuild, I need not only patriots who were with us over the last six weeks, but folks who are stepping up for the first time. Don't let the most radical candidate South Carolina Democrats have nominated buy this seat. Thank you for standing with me, Darline Graham United States Senator P.S. Peter,Josh Shapiro’s Department of Health has quietly submitted over 500 pages of proposed regulations that would give his administration sweeping new powers over your home, your medical records, and your children:🚨 Warrantless entry into private homes📄 Access to confidential medical records without consent👧 Private interviews with your child at school — without notifying you — and school staff prohibited from interfering😷 Statewide school mask mandates🗃️ A mandatory vaccine databaseAll of it controlled by one office that reports directly to the Governor. Pennsylvanians voted to limit exactly this kind of power in 2021 when they amended the constitution after COVID. Shapiro is trying to do an end-run around that amendment through regulation — bypassing the legislature entirely.**Why? Because he’s building a résumé for 2028.** This isn’t about public health. It’s about showing national Democratic primary voters that Josh Shapiro is willing to use government authority aggressively. You are not a prop for his presidential campaign. Your rights are not a stepping stone to the White House.**The public comment period closes September 21. Here’s how to make your voice heard:**

I'm utterly flabbergasted by this Mitch McConnell thing. And maybe I shouldn't be at this point. Maybe I should just become a cold, ruthless bastard who can't be surprised by anything anymore. But I'm not there yet. And somehow, what happened today made this whole thing even more absurd.
* * *
**Today 's rant is sponsored by Ground News.**
I've been paying more attention to how differently the same story gets covered depending on where you read it--especially lately, when everything feels optimized for speed and outrage instead of context.
Take this one--_over a 1,000 outlets_ have reported on Donald Trump's pledge at the recent GOP Midterm Convention, to send every American adult $5,000 if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in the November midterm elections.
**Mother Jones** who is owned by an independent, non-profit media organization (The Center for Investigative Reporting), _refers to Donald Trump as "your deadbeat president",_ _citing his latest pledge has drawn wide criticism from his own supporters and right leaning media conglomerates and spokespeople._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5bd089f4-1ee7-4361-a02f-65b0ab6b4368?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**World News Daily (WND)** whose ownership is not stated, reports _the President doubled down on plans for a $5,000 dividend to every adult American, providing in-depth quotes from Donald Trump._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5bd089f4-1ee7-4361-a02f-65b0ab6b4368?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Same story--completely different narratives.

That's why I use Ground News. It pulls together 50,000+ sources so you can compare coverage side by side, see political bias, who owns the sources you're reading, how reliable they are and understand how framing changes the story.

See how the left and right cover the same story, what each side emphasizes or leaves out, and discover overlooked stories in the Blindspot Feed, which surfaces coverage disproportionately reported by either side.

* * *
On Monday, they dragged this poor husk of a man out for a dog and pony show. They brought in more Capitol Police than you can imagine, all to conceal his actual condition from the public. They wheeled out a man we hadn't seen in three months, a man who wasn't in particularly good shape even before this weird cardiac event, and who certainly wasn't physically or mentally up for the job. And they had him speak to reporters for about two minutes.
But first, they told those reporters they couldn't record video or audio. No footage. No sound. Nothing that would let us hear his voice or see how frail he really is.
And the media complied. That's wild to me. And frankly, insulting to his constituents.
What right do Mitch McConnell's staffers have to keep the public in the dark for months and then expect a blatantly censored appearance to end every legitimate question about his ability to do the job? What right do they have to decide that the people of Kentucky don't get to know the condition of the man who is supposed to be representing them?
He disappeared again yesterday, missing several voters -- and then this afternoon, McConnell reappeared. And somehow that made this story even crazier by voting to advance the Farm Bill (finally!) after multiple people had to help him cast his vote.
These people work for us. Their salaries are paid with _our_ tax dollars. Asking whether our elected officials are actually capable of doing the work we pay them to do is not some outrageous invasion of privacy. It is the bare minimum of democratic accountability.
And I'm sorry, but I have some questions.
Because this isn't some meaningless ceremonial vote. This is the Farm Bill. This is the legislation that helps determine what happens to the food system you rely on every single day. It affects whether farmers can protect themselves when crops fail or markets collapse, how families access food assistance, how farmland is conserved, and how billions of taxpayer dollars flow through rural America.
It affects whether a farmer can keep planting next year. Whether food makes it from a field in Iowa to the grocery store where you buy dinner. Whether families can put food on the table. These are real people, real livelihoods and real public money.
And Congress generally rewrites this thing once every five years.
The bill McConnell helped advance is more than 900 pages.
Nine. Hundred. Pages.
Maybe -- just maybe -- that deserves more than somebody showing up after three months away and casting the deciding vote without the public having any meaningful idea how carefully he studied what the hell he was voting on.
* * *
_**I 've started paying more attention to how the same story can feel completely different depending on who's reporting it. Ground News makes that easy to see by showing coverage from across the political spectrum and pointing out what certain outlets leave out.**_
_**My team and I use it because it helps cut through the noise.**_
**[See every side of every story with Ground News->](https://substack.com/redirect/735e88f4-c649-42b5-a11a-5ff8ff88504a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
_Try it today!_
[ Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/735e88f4-c649-42b5-a11a-5ff8ff88504a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
And that's why the victory lap we're seeing now from Republican operatives and people in the media pisses me off so much. They are spiking the football -- saying: look how stupid these Democratic content creators look... they thought Mitch McConnell was dead.
Let me be very clear about something: The only reason I thought Mitch McConnell might be dead is because they wouldn't put him on camera and show him to us. You don't get to hide a sitting senator for three months, ban cameras when you finally trot him out, and then mock the people who asked where he was.
And you definitely don't get to act like today's vote settles the matter.
To me, today's vote makes the questions more consequential. His vote mattered. Without that twelfth Republican vote, this legislation hadn't moved. Today they had it. Today it moved.
I don't like talking about any of this. I'd much rather be talking about the important issues of the day. But I can't, because Congress won't do anything about the important issues of the day. And Congress won't do anything because we have people like Mitch McConnell in power who can't physically or mentally do the job, surrounded by a whole apparatus of people willing to cover for a gerontocracy that is incapable of delivering on anything that matters to the American people. But the more I think about it, the more I realize _this_ _is_ one of the important issues of the day. Because this isn't really about Mitch McConnell anymore. It's about what we allow power to become in this country. It's about politicians clinging to power to the detriment of people's livelihoods and the wellbeing of our country.
They can't rein in an out-of-control fascist president. They can't end this ridiculous, illegal war in Iran. They can't fix our broken economy. They can't regulate AI, or deal with the data centers and Flock cameras that are driving Americans crazy every single day. They are not capable of dealing with any of it. And it's because of exactly this.
So to the pundits online who were so happy to lecture people like me: screw that.
Mitch McConnell did show up again today, this time to cast the vote his Republican peers proclaimed they needed to move the farm bill forward. It's bullshit. But that doesn't erase any of my questions about what the hell is actually going on here.
If I'm being honest with you, what we've seen of him this week deeply concerns me. And that's if you can even say what we have seen this week was Mitch McConnell. I don't think it really was. It was whatever's left of him. He is not capable of doing this job. It's incredibly sad. It's elder abuse.
And this keeps happening in America. We have so many members of Congress who have clung to power for far too long and done nothing to create the conditions for the next generation of American politicians to step up, not just into ordinary seats, but into leadership. I am tired of this entire class of people acting like we're being annoying for asking basic questions about what the hell is going on in this country and why it keeps happening.
It is not okay for a sitting member of Congress, whether it's Mitch McConnell or Tom Kean or any of the others, and that includes plenty of Democrats, to disappear for months with no update on their health. None.
Why hasn't the Senate removed Mitch McConnell? Why haven't they moved the farm bill forward without him? Why haven't they stripped him of his committee assignments? That's what would happen in a functioning government. And a functioning media would spend a hell of a lot more time on this story instead of moving on the moment they got played by a bullshit dog and pony show.
I remain bewildered. And I'll be honest about why I keep talking about McConnell. Yes, it gets clicks. It does. But that's not why I keep coming back to it. I keep talking about it because this story is a window into everything that is broken about American politics right now. It is maddening that we're expected to just tolerate this kind of crap.
And that's before we even get to the fact that the current president of the United States is very clearly in substantial physical and cognitive decline. He doesn't know where he is half the time. He is not up for the job. And he's being taken advantage of by some of the least qualified people you have ever seen on this planet.
We are in bad shape in America. And until we break up these concentrated power structures that are manipulating the American people and destroying our economy, and relentlessly, ruthlessly demand real transparency and accountability from the people who wield them, we are never going to take this country back. We are never going to get to a place where we have a government that worthy of the people it represents.
Because Mitch McConnell showed up today.
He cast the vote his party demanded of him was needed.
A piece of legislation advanced.
And somehow, after three months of gaslighting, we're supposed to believe that 'showing up' is the same thing as delivering for the American people.
It's not.
It's the bare minimum. The American people deserve representatives who can actually do the work -- and a government honest enough to tell us when they can't. We deserve a hell of a lot better than this.
With urgency,
--Mike
